title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
source: Nature Materials
abstract: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-atom catalysts (SACs), in which isolated atoms lack extended coordination and are prone to oxidative instability. Here we design atomically dispersed Ru-O-Cr motifs that enable oxidation damping during acidic oxygen evolution. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows attenuated Ru oxidation synchronized with anticorrelated and partially reversible Cr redox evolution, consistent with proximity-dependent redox coupling. This buffered redox response is accompanied by bounded and partially reversible changes in the local metal-oxygen coordination environment. These coupled dynamics support proximity-coupled Ru-O-Cr redox units, enabling a 55.7-fold increased resistance against oxidation-induced Ru dissolution compared with conventional SACs. In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, catalysts incorporating proximal Ru-O-Cr configurations exhibit degradation rates that are 6.8-fold and 14.4-fold lower than those of Ru SACs and commercial RuO2, respectively, at 1 A cm-2. These results suggest proximal oxidation damping as a potential design principle for stabilizing atomically precise electrocatalysts.

abstract: Seasonal breeders often depend on predictable resource pulses, yet climate change may alter reliability without shifting average timing. Focusing on average timing alone could mean that climate impacts on species are overlooked. The authors show that, for a tropical seabird model species, winter–spring phytoplankton blooms kept a stable mean timing but became more variable between years. Breeding synchrony weakened and reproductive success declined and became less consistent over the same two decades.

title: A bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an aromatic cyclopentadienide ring
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, yet they are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of pentabenzocorannulenide (PBC-), a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide (Cp-) ring. The five-membered Cp- ring is generated quantitatively by aromatization-driven nucleophilic dealkylation (C-C bond cleavage) of a pentabenzocorannulene derivative. Through single crystal X-ray diffraction and quantum chemical analyses, we reveal the unique structural features and physicochemical properties of PBC-, demonstrating uncommon bonding pattern and electronic characteristics distinct from corannulene, fullerenes, end caps of carbon nanotubes and other geodesic polyarenes. PBC- has an exceptionally strong conjugate acid, undergoes reversible covalent functionalization and engages in η5-type metal complexation. Incorporating the iconic Cp- ring into a fully conjugated sp2 carbon network opens avenues for exploring non-conventional π systems. A synthetic nanocarbon incorporating a five-membered cyclopentadienide ring is depicted against the backdrop of a positively curved carbon network. The inset displays a vial of the nanocarbon dissolved in dichloromethane.

title: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core
source: Nature
abstract: Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

title: Two-dimensional material membranes with precisely tunable interlayer spacing from nanometre to submillimetre
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Precise and reversible control over ion channel size in membrane materials is crucial for realizing optimized device performance, but conventional approaches to channel regulation suffer from limited tunability, reversibility and precision. Here we report a deprotonation-ion coordination strategy for the precise, reversible modulation of interlayer spacing over five orders of magnitude in layered material membranes. The interlayer expansion is driven by electrostatic repulsion due to the deprotonation of intercalated cellulose nanofibers and is reversibly tunable via charge compensation through cation coordination. As a result, we achieve an unprecedented degree of structural tunability: porosity from 0% to 78%, interlayer spacing from 1.39 to 152,000 nm and membrane thickness from 43 to 5,400 μm. Our strategy enables on-demand performance customization with the same membrane platform. For example, a slight interlayer expansion (to 1.48 nm) boosts zinc-ion capacitance by 67% relative to non-expanded membranes; a 21,583-fold expansion (to ~30 μm) raises osmotic energy conversion power by 63%, and a 100,719-fold expansion (to ~140 μm) unlocks exceptional pressure sensing. These results establish a generalizable paradigm for nanometric microstructure engineering of various van der Waals materials.

title: Controlling the flow of information in optical metrology
source: Nature Materials
abstract:
Abstract
                  Optical metrology has surpassed the Abbe–Rayleigh limit by leveraging nonlinear phenomena and statistical accumulation, and has recently unlocked subatomic precision using artificial intelligence estimators trained on measurand variations. Here we argue that further gains can be achieved by optimizing the flow of Fisher information carrying metrological content. We show that Fisher information flow need not follow the optical energy flow and that it exhibits resonance, diffraction and interference, singular points, and vorticity. It can exhibit a Talbot-like effect in which Fisher information density patterns repeat periodically with propagation distance, and it can be focused beyond the diffraction limit, mirroring the effect of optical superoscillation. Material composition, resonances, geometry and environment determine where information is generated, how it propagates, and how it can be enhanced and directed to improve precision. This perspective recasts metrology as information flow engineering, for applications ranging from atomic-scale diagnostics and smart manufacturing to remote sensing, radar and LiDAR.

title: Inorganic Ionic Polymerization toward Fracture-Resistant, Self-healable Functional Hydrogels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fracture-resistant, self-healable functional hydrogels hold promise for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and intelligent devices. However, integrating these properties within a single structure remains challenging. Persistent load-bearing constraints hinder molecular rearrangement for repair, whereas excessive network dynamics can disrupt functional organization. Here, we uncover a reciprocal assembly mechanism based on bidirectional regulation between inorganic ionic oligomers and polymer chains. The acrylic acid/poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) environment suppresses calcium carbonate oligomer (CCO) aggregation, while CCO organizes PAA chains into birefringent acicular domains through multisite coordination and cooperative hydrogen bonding. These domains provide persistent load-bearing constraints and exchangeable interactions, enabling a fracture energy of 38.3 kJ m–2 and 87% tensile-strength recovery after 6 h of ambient healing. The same assembled network further exhibits 4.5% AM1.5G solar-weighted absorptivity and strong mid-infrared emission, remaining 5.1 °C cooler than neat PAA under simulated sunlight while retaining its cooling response for 21 days. This work establishes inorganic ionic oligomers as active reciprocal regulators of polymer organization, coupling dynamic network reconstruction with mechanical reinforcement and functional stability.

title: Chromophore Orientation as a Design Strategy for Self-Assembled Monolayers in p-i-n Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Self-assembled monolayers of the carbazole-based phosphonic acids recently became a popular choice for hole-selective layers in p-i-n perovskite solar cells. However, the role of molecular geometry in controlling interfacial coverage and device performance remains poorly understood. In this work, we have investigated anchor-to-chromophore connectivity as a molecular design parameter by synthesizing four carbazole phosphonic acid derivatives with T-shape and Rod-shape structures. The molecular pairs were designed to keep similar energetic properties while varying the spatial orientation of the chromophore relative to the phosphonic acid anchoring group. Optical spectroscopy and photoemission yield measurements confirm that the energy levels are governed primarily by the substitution position on the carbazole core, rather than by molecular orientation. In contrast, electrochemical impedance and cyclic voltammetry measurements reveal pronounced differences in charge-transfer blocking ability, indicating improved ITO surface coverage for Rod-shape molecules. When implemented in p-i-n perovskite solar cells, Rod-shape interlayers provide a reproducible improvement in device performance, although in part hindered by less favorable wetting behavior. After mitigating film formation and top interface losses, devices with 3-Rod reached a power conversion efficiency of 25.04%. These results demonstrate the importance of chromophore orientation for designing densely packed, high-performance phosphonic acid materials for perovskite solar cells.

title: A Sandwich-Structured Dual-Mode Fabric with Temperature-Adaptive Spectral Tunability for All-Season Outdoor Personal Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Owing to global warming, sudden temperature fluctuations are occurring with greater frequency, which exacerbates risks to public health. Passive radiative cooling and solar heating technologies have unique advantages of requiring no energy input, rendering them highly suitable for thermal management textiles. The operation of the dual-mode fabric with cooling and heating functions primarily relies on the contrast between the solar reflectance on the cooling side and solar absorption on the heating side. However, the regulation of infrared emissivity in both modes tends to be ignored. Here, we report a dual-mode woven fabric based on a sandwich structure that features temperature-adaptive spectral tunability for all-season outdoor personal thermal management. The combination of a polydimethylsiloxane/nano-zinc oxide (PDMS/nano-ZnO) radiative cooling layer with a polydopamine (PDA) solar heating layer constituted the basis of the dual-mode switchable fabric. More importantly, the introduction of eicosane into the porous fibers realized the spectral tunability in response to ambient temperature. The solar reflectance in the cooling mode showed an increase of nearly 6% at high temperature (>40 °C), while the infrared emissivity in the heating mode was reduced by 13.4% at low temperature (<10 °C). In addition, the introduction of eicosane also endowed the fabric with considerable latent heat to further improve thermal management performance. Its temperature range of response corresponds closely to the human thermal comfort zone. Under solar intensity (Isolar) of ∼500 W/m2, the resulting fabric achieved a temperature increase of ∼7.1 °C compared with bare skin in the heating mode and maintained the average temperature of the covered skin close to that of bare skin in the cooling mode. Thanks to the woven structure, the fabric exhibited desirable mechanical strength, waterproofness, washability, breathability, and moisture permeability. This dual-mode woven fabric was expected to provide further insight into developing responsive dual-mode personal thermal management textiles.

title: Particle Size Engineering of Injectable Poly( l -lactic Acid) Microspheres Modulates Material−Tissue Interactions and Extracellular Matrix Remodeling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Injectable poly(l-lactic acid) (PLLA) microspheres have been widely explored as regenerative biomaterials due to their favorable biocompatibility and ability to support extracellular matrix (ECM) formation. However, how microsphere size, as a fundamental structural parameter, influences degradation behavior, material−tissue interactions, and subsequent tissue remodeling remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed size-controlled PLLA microsphere systems, including single-sized and multiscale formulations, with polycaprolactone (PCL) microspheres as material controls, to investigate particle size-dependent biological responses. Microsphere size influenced degradation characteristics and was associated with distinct cellular and tissue responses. In vitro studies demonstrated that extracts from 50 μm PLLA microspheres induced stronger fibroblast ECM-related responses among single-sized formulations, accompanied by enhanced expression of LTBP1, COL1A1, COL3A1, and collagen-associated proteins. In vivo, multiscale PLLA microspheres exhibited distinct macrophage response profiles and were associated with more pronounced long-term collagen organization and ECM remodeling. Transcriptomic analysis identified gene-expression patterns associated with extracellular matrix organization, immune regulation, and tissue remodeling. Collectively, these findings identify microsphere size as an important biomaterial design parameter for tuning degradation behavior, host−material interactions, and ECM remodeling, providing a particle size engineering strategy for the development of injectable regenerative biomaterials.

title: Hierarchically Structured All-Polymer Composites for Enhanced High-Temperature Energy Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer dielectrics are promising candidates for high-temperature capacitive energy storage owing to the intrinsic electrical insulation and processing advantages. However, conventional polymer dielectrics usually suffer from low energy density and efficiency at elevated temperatures due to the difficulty in simultaneously achieving a strong polarization response and a high breakdown strength. Here, we propose a trilayer coaxial nanofiber hierarchical architecture to improve high-temperature energy storage performance. By confining highly polar polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) to the middle layer and utilizing thermally stable polyetherimide (PEI) to form inner and outer insulating barriers, such hierarchical interface design enhances dielectric displacement while suppressing leakage conduction loss at high temperatures. Based on the optimized PVDF/PEI film, boron nitride (BN) nanowhiskers are incorporated into the PVDF layer to further improve voltage resistance and performance stability under elevated-temperature conditions. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of polarization response, charge blocking, and breakdown reliability, the 1 wt % BN-15% PVDF/PEI nanocomposite film delivers a high energy density of 10.52 J cm–3 with 96% discharge efficiency at 150 °C under a maximum applied electric field of 750 kV mm–1. This work establishes a scalable and low-cost design strategy for improving the high-temperature performance of polymer-based nanocomposite dielectrics through hierarchical structure engineering.

title: Metalized Carbon Nanotube Films with Boosted Atomic Oxygen Resistance as Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Cladding for Low-Earth-Orbit Space Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are essential for electronic devices and spacecraft operating in low Earth orbit. Developing materials that combine ultrahigh EMI shielding with mechanical robustness and resistance to extreme space environments remains a critical challenge. Herein, large-area acid-treated carbon nanotube film/aluminum (A-CNTF/Al) composite films are fabricated via acid modification of CNTF, followed by Al deposition as a reinforcing layer. The pristine CNTF shows an electrical conductivity of 4.2 × 104 S/m, which rises to 1.6 × 105 and 6.1 × 105 S/m after acid modification and Al metallization, respectively. The as-prepared A-CNT/Al composite film (14 μm) exhibits an average EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 66.2 dB, attaining a high absolute EMI shielding effectiveness (SSE/t) of up to 102,160.49 dB cm2 g–1 across 8.2–12.4 GHz, which ranks among the highest documented metrics for lightweight EMI shielding composite materials. Remarkably, the composite film maintains favorable EMI SE (70.9 dB) at 12.4–40 GHz after atomic oxygen irradiation with a fluence of 4 × 1020 atoms cm–2, verifying its great prospect for long-duration on-orbit service. These results demonstrate that acid-induced surface engineering combined with aluminum metallization significantly enhances the electrical and EMI shielding performance of CNTF, providing lightweight, durable, and highly efficient shielding materials for extreme space environments.

title: Design and Synthesis of Nonfused Medium-Wide-Bandgap Acceptors for High-Efficiency Organic Photovoltaic Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the continuous exploration of organic photovoltaic (OPV) applications, medium-wide bandgap (MWBG) OPV cells demonstrate substantial potential for emerging applications, particularly in indoor environments. However, most high-performance MWBG acceptors rely on costly fused conjugated backbones, limiting the industrialization of MWBG OPV cells. Here, we report a nonfused MWBG acceptor, TBT-59, designed from a thiophene–benzene–thiophene central unit with bulky 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl side chains to modulate its molecular conformation. Due to a simple synthetic route, TBT-59 displays a low material cost of 12.50$·g–1. When blended with PB2, TBT-59 exhibits higher electron mobility, more balanced charge transport, and lower voltage loss than TBT-65. Therefore, the TBT-59-based OPV cell achieves a power conversion efficiency of 13.9%, among the best for nonfused MWBG acceptors with absorption onsets below 800 nm. Under 2700 K light-emitting diode illumination at 1000 lux, the TBT-59-based cell reaches an efficiency of 24.1%. This work demonstrates a cost-effective design strategy for MWBG acceptors.

title: Electron-Rich Cobalt Single-Atom Sites via Axial GaN Coordination Boost CO2-to-CO Conversion through an Optimized *COOH Pathway
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise tuning of the electronic structure of single-atom metal sites at their atomic scale to surpass their intrinsic activity and selectivity limits remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we constructed a well-defined electron-rich single-atom Co site by loading cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) molecules with CoN4 centers onto the gallium nitride (GaN) substrate (CoPc@GaN). Characterization analysis reveals that the work function difference between the GaN substrate and CoPc induces an interfacial built-in electric field (BEF), which drives electron transfer from GaN to the CoN4 center, forming electron-rich Co active sites. This configuration effectively optimizes the adsorption/dsorption behavior of reaction intermediates (*COOH and *CO) during CO2RR. In the H-type cell, CoPc@GaN achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 97.9% at –0.9 V (vs RHE), while in a flow cell, the efficiency increases to 98.8% at –1.0 V (vs RHE). The electrocatalyst maintains >90% selectivity across a broad potential window of 1000 mV and demonstrates stable performance over 32 h. In situ attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the electron-rich Co active sites significantly reduce the energy barrier for *COOH formation and facilitate CO desorption, validating the feasibility of the strategy of modulating metal phthalocyanines through substrate engineering.

title: Staggered cryo-plasma FIB milling enables high-throughput cryo-ET
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryo-focused ion beam (cryo-FIB) milling combined with cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a crucial technique for studying macromolecules in their native environment. To mill thick samples, plasma ion sources are used. However, the practicality of high plasma currents, which offer the greatest potential for increasing throughput, and their possible damaging effects on the sample have not yet been investigated. Here, we systematically examine high-current xenon plasma-FIB (PFIB) milling and quantify the current-dependent damage in over 4700 tomograms by preparing a total lift-out volume of 9000 µm³. We find that currents of up to 2500 nA can be used in cryo-ET lamella preparations, enabling increased milling speeds and sample volumes that can be examined while maintaining sample integrity. We demonstrate this using a newly developed high-throughput staggered milling routine for waffle-like preparations, in which we achieve high-resolution reconstructions of yeast ribosomes, and for tissue serial lift-outs, enabling a complete experiment within 24 hours. Our results and approach provide a strong foundation for future in situ structural investigations of medically relevant protein complexes in organoids, tissues, or entire organisms.

title: Liquid Metal–Spent Coffee Ground Composites for Flexible UV-Responsive Electrochemical Sensors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable functional materials derived from biomass waste offer promising opportunities for flexible electronics and photoresponsive systems. Herein, we report liquid metal gallium–spent coffee grounds–ethyl cellulose (Ga–SCGs–EC) composite films fabricated through particle-size reduction of SCGs, sonication-assisted Ga dispersion, and solution casting with EC as a binder matrix. The incorporation of Ga droplets, with their self-limiting 2D Ga2O3 skins, strongly influenced the film microstructure, leading to increasingly fine and Ga-rich domains as the Ga:SCGs ratio increased from 1:1 to 4:1. Structural and thermal analyses showed that the Ga droplets were physically integrated within the SCGs–EC matrix and predominantly retained liquid-state characteristics. Mechanical testing showed that Ga addition improved tensile performance, with the 1:1 composition exhibiting the highest mechanical reinforcement. In contrast, the 4:1 film displayed the strongest photoresponsive behavior, showing reversible and wavelength-dependent current modulation, particularly under 385 nm UV illumination. This enhanced response was associated with improved Ga dispersion and light-induced interfacial charge modulation involving native Ga/Ga2O3 interfaces and oxygen deficiency in Ga2O3. These findings highlight Ga–SCGs–EC films as flexible, biomass-derived composites with photoresponsive properties that can be readily integrated as electrodes for UV detection.

title: Atomic Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

title: Self-Induced Spin Glass in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness surpassing fragile rare-earth SISGs. Magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) calculations suggest that the high coercivity mainly arises from extrinsic spin pinning associated with the nanograined microstructure, contributing to macroscopic anti-interference. Ultimately, the creation of the MnNCN SISG and the elucidation of its magnetic competition extend the SISG paradigm to transition-metal compounds, establishing HPHT synthesis as a targeted methodology for tailoring complex magnetism.

title: Tailoring Spin-Crossover Transitions in Fe(HB(tz)3)2 via Cocrystallization for Low-Temperature Barocaloric Cooling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spin-crossover (SCO) phase transitions can drive large barocaloric effects─thermal changes induced by applied hydrostatic pressure that enable heat to be moved against a temperature gradient. Although several SCO compounds have been reported to display promising barocaloric properties─including high pressure sensitivity, a large entropy change, and minimal transition hysteresis─it is challenging to control the transition temperature of a material without adversely impacting its phase-change behavior. This limitation restricts the scope of thermal applications relevant to a given SCO material. Here, we show how cocrystallization with solid coformers allows the SCO transition of Fe(HB(tz)3)2 (HB(tz)3– = hydrotris(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)borate) to be manipulated across a wide temperature range. In particular, we report a series of cocrystals with SCO transition temperatures spanning from 185 to 350 K and varying degrees of associated hysteresis and cooperativity. We further establish structure–property relationships between coformer identity and SCO transition behavior through a combination of structural characterization, magnetometry, vibrational spectroscopy, and calorimetry. Notably, two cocrystals feature sharp SCO transitions near 200 K that produce large and highly reversible barocaloric effects in a low-temperature regime that has been difficult to access for most classes of barocaloric materials. More broadly, these results provide new insights into cocrystallization as a generalizable synthetic strategy for systematically tuning the properties of SCO materials.

title: Stereochemical Identity of a Single Fluorosugar Enables Noninvasive Dual-Biomarker Fingerprinting of Cancer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Clinical molecular imaging of cancer largely relies on single biomarker-attributable readouts. Through an efficient trapping mechanism, 2-[18F]FDG robustly links PET readouts to the Warburg effect, illuminating only a single metabolic axis within the multichannel biochemical network of cancer. The versatile chemical space of synthetic fluorosugars, however, may offer an attractive framework for broadening the repertoire of metabolic markers accessible to noninvasive imaging. Here, we report Fluorine Metabolic Imaging (FMI), a molecular MRI strategy for simultaneous in vivo mapping of two metabolic biomarkers using a single probe. FMI exploits the altered biochemistry of 3-fluoro-3-deoxy-d-galactose (3FDGal), which undergoes orthogonal intracellular redox transformations mediated by ALDH1A1 and AKR1B1, each yielding a stably trapped fluorine-labeled metabolite with a characteristic 19F-NMR peak. Concurrently mapped by 19F-MRI, these two enzyme-attributable readouts enable noninvasive spatially resolved dual-biomarker visualization. We establish the trapping mechanism of 3FDGal and its enzymatic basis, demonstrating that 3FDGal-initiated fingerprints reflect dual-biomarker variations across different cancer cells. In vivo, FMI distinguishes tumors with contrasting metabolic phenotypes, herein demonstrated in human xenografts not detectable by the canonical 2-[18F]FDG-PET approach. Establishing this proof-of-concept platform for noninvasive multilayered tumor subtyping, FMI with fluorosugars extends metabolic imaging beyond the Warburg scheme into unexplored dimensions of cancer diagnostics.

title: Sequential Charge Transfer via Synergistic Au Species Boosts CO2 Photoreduction under Near-Infrared Irradiation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 reduction in the near-infrared (NIR) region suffers from low efficiency and poor selectivity, stemming from the energy mismatch between the low-energy nature of NIR photons and the high activation energy barrier of CO2 molecules. Moreover, it is challenging to achieve directed charge transfer, hindering the catalytic reaction kinetics. To overcome the bottleneck, we report a hybrid photocatalyst consisting of atomically dispersed Au single atoms (SAs) and Au nanoparticles (NPs) anchored on ultrathin CuCrP2S6 nanosheets (Aun/Au1–CCPS) for efficient NIR-driven CO2 photoreduction. Integrated crystal orbital Hamiltonian population (ICOHP) analysis reveals that orbital coupling among Au-5d, Cr-3d, and Cu-3d states in Aun/Au1–CCPS enhances the carbon affinity of Au species and facilitates CO2 activation by lowering the energy barrier for molecular orbital activation. Combined spectroscopic analyses and constrained density functional theory (CDFT-MIXED) calculations reveal that Au SAs regulate the electronic structure of CCPS and serve as electronic bridges connecting the CCPS substrate and neighboring Au NPs by strengthening interfacial electronic coupling. Additionally, an interfacial built-in electric field (BIEF) is induced, which significantly accelerates electron-transfer kinetics. Furthermore, adjacent Au SA sites cooperate with Au NPs to lower the formation energy barrier of the key *COOH intermediate, promoting CO evolution. As a consequence, the optimized Aun/Au1–CCPS catalyst exhibits exceptional CO generation activity of 96.08 μmol g–1 h–1 with nearly 100% selectivity, outperforming the majority of state-of-the-art catalysts in the NIR region. This study provides novel insights into the design of cooperative catalytic systems for high-efficiency photocatalytic CO2 conversion under NIR irradiation.

title: Click-Functionalizable Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). Compared to light in the visible and NIR-I regions, NIR-II light undergoes less absorption and scattering by biological tissues, enabling deeper tissue penetration and higher imaging resolution. Tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate (TTFtt)-bridged bimetallic diradicaloid complexes exhibit bright NIR-II emission with high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) relative to other NIR-II fluorophores. These complexes are also particularly modular, as the capping ligands on the metal centers can be substituted to impart desired properties. Here, azide-functionalized bis(imino)acenaphthene (BIAN) capping ligands are introduced to leverage and expand this modularity. BIAN-capped TTFtt complexes exhibit chemical and photophysical properties comparable to previously reported TTFtt complexes. BIAN backbones functionalized with an azide group further enable Huisgen cycloaddition “click” chemistry for the attachment of diverse functional moieties while preserving the intrinsic NIR-II photophysical properties of the TTFtt core. As one example, a sulfonate-clicked TTFtt complex (1-C3) displays enhanced solubility and increased photoluminescence (PL) intensity in aqueous solutions compared to other TTFtt complexes. Notably, 1-C3 also exhibits pH-dependent PL intensity, suggesting its potential utility as an NIR-II-emitting pH sensor. Furthermore, the enhanced water solubility of 1-C3 enabled us to obtain in vivo gastrointestinal imaging in murine models. Overall, these results demonstrate the dramatically expanded modularity of TTFtt complexes through the use of clickable-BIAN ligands.

title: Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging Reveals the Kinetic Origin of Wettability-Controlled Photocatalytic Selectivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial wettability strongly influences photocatalytic selectivity, but the kinetic origin of this effect remains unclear. Although adsorption differences and dominant reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathways are often invoked to explain wettability-dependent selectivity, neither fully reveals how interfacial reaction environments determine catalytic outcomes. Here, we use single-molecule fluorescence imaging to directly resolve individual photocatalytic events on reversibly tunable hydrophilic and hydrophobic TiO2 interfaces that preferentially generate •OH- and 1O2-associated reaction environments, respectively. The results show that substrate adsorption remains largely comparable across different wettability states, whereas interfacial conversion kinetics constitute the dominant origin of the observed selectivity and product-release dynamics further amplify this effect. Combined with DFT calculations, the single-molecule analysis reveals the kinetic origin of wettability-controlled photocatalytic selectivity by correlating ROS-associated interfacial environments with interfacial reaction kinetics. This work establishes a single-molecule kinetic analysis framework for interrogating how interfacial microenvironments govern heterogeneous photocatalytic selectivity, providing an approach for linking interfacial regulation to catalytic kinetics and macroscopic outcomes.

title: Buried Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected Electrocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Protective overlayers are widely used to stabilize metal catalysts under harsh electrochemical conditions. Unlike graphene coatings, oxide overlayers introduce a buried metal-oxide interface that fundamentally reshapes reaction pathways by separating proton delivery from product release. Although proton transport through oxides has been extensively investigated, the fate of reaction products at buried interfaces remains unresolved; for example, H2-molecule vs H-atom pathways remain under debate in oxide-protected hydrogen evolution. Here, we revisit this buried interface using a microelectrochemical cell with well-defined model structures. Systematic measurements across nine metal-oxide heterostructures, combined with density functional theory calculations, reveal that product transport is governed by two sequential kinetic barriers: hydrogen spillover across the metal-oxide junction and hydrogen permeation through the oxide lattice. These coupled barriers determine whether reaction products are released, accumulate at buried interfaces, or induce interfacial failure. This work not only identifies superior Pt-TiO2 and Pd-TiO2 but also clarifies which step is impeded in Au-TiO2, Pt-SiO2, Pt-HfO2, Pd-SiO2, Pd-HfO2, Au-SiO2, and Au-HfO2 heterostructures. Guided by these model studies, we implement a TiO2 protection strategy in a proton-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer with remarkable durability. These findings provide a framework for constructing a complete proton-to-product route for buried interfaces, potentially resolving long-standing ambiguities in oxide-protected electrocatalysis.

title: Multitime Scale Operando Kinetic Decoupling of Photogenerated Carriers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The energy-conversion efficiency of photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is governed by photogenerated charge-carrier kinetics that span several orders of magnitude, from subpicosecond generation in the semiconductor bulk to millisecond consumption at catalytic surfaces. This vast temporal disparity severs the causal link between ultrafast carrier events and steady-state photocurrents, leaving the mechanistic origins of efficiency losses speculative and fundamentally hindering the rational optimization of PEC devices. Here, we bridge this gap by integrating multitime scale operando spectroscopies, ranging from transient absorption to electrochemical measurements, on model β-Fe2O3 photoanodes. This approach enables deconvolution of the temporal evolution of photogenerated carriers into distinct signatures attributable to bulk diffusion, charge accumulation, and catalytic-intermediate formation, thereby decoupling and identifying the dynamic fingerprints of carriers within a champion β-Fe2O3 photoanode. These fingerprints establish a mechanistic framework that directly connects multitime scale carrier dynamics and kinetics to the design principles of high-performance photoelectrodes, transforming the understanding of and approach to engineering solar water splitting systems.

title: Small-Molecule Activation Reshapes the Catalytic Conformational Landscape during Ca2+ ATPase Turnover
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover is a central challenge in chemical biology because activation arises from redistribution of transient populations that are difficult to resolve during catalysis. By integrating time-resolved X-ray solution scattering, molecular dynamics simulations, and kinetic modeling, we determine how the small-molecule activator yakuchinone A modulates the catalytic cycle of the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA), a prototypical P-type ATPase. We show that the activator accelerates the catalytic cycle by reshaping the conformational landscape during turnover, with a disproportionate enhancement of late-cycle transitions. This kinetic modulation of the rate-limiting step increases the population of Ca2+-bound E2P states, while significantly reducing accumulation of Ca2+-free E2*Pi transient states associated with dephosphorylation. Ensemble-based structural models quantitatively reproduce the experimental scattering profiles and support redistribution of conformational populations during turnover. Together, these findings provide a time-resolved mechanistic picture of how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover through redistribution of conformational populations and selective acceleration of rate-limiting transitions.

title: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.

title: Sulfurization Breaking the Ferroelectric Polarization Bottleneck in PbTiO3
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Robust ferroelectricity is crucial for high-performance ferroelectric nonvolatile memories. PbTiO3 (PTO) is expected to show large polarization with a high Curie temperature (TC). However, the inherent leakage current of PTO limits its actual ferroelectricity. To address this limitation, we prepare PTO films via sulfurization using a cost-effective sol–gel method. The pristine PTO films show notable remnant polarization (Pr) of 61.6 μC/cm2 with well-saturated electric field–polarization loops that have not been achieved in either bulk or thin-film forms previously. Upon sulfurization, Pr increases to approximately 180% of its pristine value, rising from 61.6 to 111.7 μC/cm2 alongside a moderate coercive field of 697 kV/cm, rendering the films competitive among currently reported large polarization ferroelectrics (Pr > 100 μC/cm2). Additionally, an elevated TC of up to 526 °C was observed in sulfurized PTO films, compared with 505 °C for pristine PTO thin films. First-principles calculations reveal that the sulfur-associated enhancement of tetragonal distortion substantially reduces the short-range restoring interaction, thereby shifting the balance between short-range and long-range forces toward a stronger polar instability; phase-field simulations further reproduce the enhanced ferroelectric polarization. Our study demonstrates an effective sulfurization method for achieving large ferroelectricity, holding great potential for ferroelectric devices.

title: Spiroselenopyrans: Reversible Light- and Soft-Acid-Triggered Switching of Spirocyclic C–Se Bonds
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spiropyrans (SPs) are among the most exploited molecular scaffolds for photoswitching. Despite the potential of heavy chalcogen substitution at the spiro site to reshape bond characteristics and unlock distinct functionalities, SP analogs with chalcogens heavier than sulfur remain underexplored. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of spiroselenopyrans (SSPs), an emerging family of selenium-centered photoswitches, using steric hindrance engineering to suppress undesired benzoselenophene cyclization, a strategy that readily yields diversely substituted SSP derivatives. Compared with oxygen/sulfur-centered counterparts, the elongated, low-energy C–Se bond and narrowed HOMO–LUMO gap of SSPs enable efficient and accelerated photoisomerization to the trans-planar ring-opened selenomerocyanine (SMC). Notably, SSPs exhibit distinctive selectivity for soft acids, undergoing spontaneous ring-opening upon binding to Ag+ to form a cis-nonplanar Ag+-SMC complex while remaining inert toward hard protons. This work establishes SSPs as robust dual-responsive switches, broadens the chemical space of SP chemistry, and paves the way for advanced multistimuli-responsive molecular systems.

title: Bandedge-State-Limited Single-Photon Emission from Volumetric Quantum Design of 2D Colloidal Quantum Wells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Present-day solution-processable single-photon sources are dominated by three-dimensionally confined colloidal quantum emitters, yet their particle-to-particle variation in single-exciton properties limits reproducibility and scalability. Here, to avoid such heterogeneity, we demonstrate reliable room-temperature single-photon emission from atomically flat two-dimensional (2D) colloidal quantum wells (CQWs) with inherently uniform one-dimensional quantum confinement, despite their long-standing limitations of efficient multiexciton emission and pronounced exciton-surface susceptibility. We resolve these challenges through volumetric quantum design (VQD) of CQWs, yielding a highly localized, single bandedge state. This design laterally confines the bandedge excitonic domain within the exciton coherent area and vertically decouples it from surface states via a thick, strain-relieved quantum-barrier shell that preserves strong confinement, overcoming the daunting thickness-confinement trade-off in 2D CQWs. Statistical single-particle spectroscopy reveals that VQD-CQWs deliver near-blinking-free (on-time: >99.5%) and fluence-insensitive antibunching (g(2)(0): ∼0.041), protected by a bandedge-state-filling bottleneck, together with linear polarization of up to 73% under cavity-free conditions, originating from synergistic transition-dipole and electric-field anisotropies. These advances establish 2D CQWs as a viable, homogeneous and scalable platform for quantum technologies.

title: Liquid-Phase Deep Carbon Elongation from C1 to Crystalline Graphite
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wet-chemical synthesis of well extended sp2-carbon from simple carbon feedstocks under mild solution-phase conditions remains a longstanding challenge due to the stringent requirements of reversible C–C coupling and error-correcting aromatization. Here, we show that a Lewis-acid-assisted triflic acid medium, TfOH/Hg(OTf)2, promotes the direct conversion of chloromethane solvents into condensed hydrocarbon products and even into crystalline graphitic flakes in a one-pot solution synthesis. GC–MS, time-resolved MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy experiments reveal the spontaneous establishment of a dynamic hydrocarbon pool. Within this pool, short-chain hydrocarbon intermediates from early C–C coupling were observed and evolved into highly branched alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) ensembles prior to the precipitation of crystalline graphitic solids. Raman, transmission electron microscopy, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements confirm the graphitic crystallinity and linear Dirac band dispersion of the isolated flakes. This work demonstrates that the dual-acid system can drive continuous carbon–carbon coupling and consecutive C(sp3)-C(sp2) hybridization transitions, overcoming kinetic barriers that conventionally require pyrolytic temperatures.

title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neural activity and eye movements are well-established predictors of human memory performance. Successful memory formation is associated with reduced alpha/beta power and increased eye movements. However, their coupling and combined contribution to memory formation remain largely unknown. Across four experiments combining eye tracking with scalp or intracranial electroencephalography during free or constrained viewing, we identify the degree of visual exploration, rather than subsequent memory performance, as consistent modulator of posterior alpha/beta power. Going beyond correlations, manipulating eye movements dissociated alpha/beta power reductions from memory. Together with the finding that saccade parameters predicted alpha/beta dynamics, our results directly link posterior alpha/beta activity to the oculomotor system. Moreover, the accumulation of saccades over time accounted for reduced alpha/beta power, resembling the canonical post-stimulus alpha/beta pattern. Our work demonstrates that posterior alpha/beta activity strongly reflects eye movements, supporting alternative perspectives on alpha/beta subsequent memory effects and the general function of posterior alpha/beta activity.

title: Metal-oxo clusters stabilize electron-selective interfaces for efficient perovskite solar cells
source: Joule
abstract: Efficient perovskite photovoltaics require durable interfaces compatible with scalable manufacturing. Solution-processable metal-oxo clusters combine robust inorganic frameworks with tunable organic components to enhance charge extraction and suppress ion migration. Complementary clusters stabilize both interfaces of the electron-transport layer, enabling a certified efficiency of 26.7% and improved operational stability. This modular strategy links molecular interface engineering with scalable coating, offering a pathway toward efficient, durable perovskite solar technologies.

title: Solar-Matched Colloidal Quantum Dots/Metal–Organic Framework Hybrid Materials for Photo-Induced Charge Transfer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lead sulfide colloidal quantum dots (PbS CQDs) are promising third-generation photovoltaic materials, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are complementary materials that are used as multifunctional charge storage and redox platforms. Hybrid materials combining CQDs and MOFs are highly promising for applications utilizing solar-driven charge transfer, but their synthesis can be challenging due to the thermal instability of solar-matched infrared CQDs. Here, we demonstrate a room-temperature, "bottle-around-ship" synthesis of a nanocomposite that integrates near-infrared (NIR) absorbing PbS CQDs with an iron-based MOF, MIL-88B(Fe). We employ a syringe-pump-assisted addition of precursors to achieve controlled nucleation and crystallization of the MOF around the CQDs under ambient conditions. Structural characterization confirms the formation of crystalline composites composed of co-localized CQDs with the MOFs. Steady-state, time-resolved optical spectroscopy reveals photoluminescence quenching and shortening of the exciton lifetime in the composite compared to the CQDs alone. Transient absorption data suggest a photo-induced charge transfer from the PbS CQDs to the MIL-88B(Fe) framework on a picosecond timescale. This work establishes a room-temperature synthesis approach for integrating thermally sensitive solar-matched CQDs with functional MOFs and performs an initial spectroscopic study to evaluate the potential of these nanocomposites as advanced hybrid materials for photocatalysis and optoelectrochemical devices in the future.

title: The need for electrolyte innovation in next-generation batteries
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Over the past decade, battery electrolytes have evolved from a mere ion-conducting media into active regulators of the electrode reaction, interfacial chemistry and cycling stability. Innovations spanning advanced liquid, solid-state and emerging electrolyte systems are opening new pathways towards safer, higher-energy and application-specific batteries.

title: Thiophene-Ring Triggered Channel Curving Enables the Separation of Benzene and Cyclohexane via Sieving
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The separation of benzene and cyclohexane remains a formidable challenge in the petrochemical industry. Herein, we propose a strategy to synergistically modulate the geometric and electronic properties of MOF frameworks. A novel 2D layered MOF (SYUCT-112) was constructed using 1,3-bis((2-methylimidazol-1-yl)methyl)benzene (1,3-bmimb) as the primary ligand and 2,5-thiophenedicarboxylic acid (H2TDC) as the auxiliary ligand. Benefiting from the intrinsic curved configuration and electron-rich nature of H2TDC, the thiophene-ring triggers a structural transformation from a 3D interpenetrated framework to a 2D layered architecture via a structural corner effect. More importantly, well-defined curved pore channels of 5.2 Å are fabricated, enabling precise size-sieving separation of benzene and cyclohexane. Adsorption measurements show that SYUCT-112 possesses a high benzene uptake of 105.9 mg g–1 and delivers an adsorption selectivity factor of 27.78 toward benzene/cyclohexane, accompanied by excellent recyclability. Molecular simulations further confirm that the superior benzene selectivity stems from the size-sieving effect of the curved channels and abundant weak inter-molecular interactions, including S···π and C–H···S contacts. This work provides an instructive guideline for the rational design of porous materials toward targeted molecular sieving applications.

title: Polymer Brushes on Polymerized and Patterned Lipid Bilayers via UV-Initiated RAFT Polymerization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Patterned lipid membranes functionalized with polymer brushes offer a versatile platform for controlling cell–surface interactions and developing biomimetic cell-culture systems. Here, we report a UV-initiated reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerization strategy for synthesizing poly(di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (PDEGMA) and poly(oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (POEGMA) brushes on polymerized and micropatterned supported lipid bilayers. Atomic force microscopy revealed linear brush growth over time, with POEGMA exhibiting a higher growth rate than PDEGMA. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed the successful formation of polymer layers on the lipid membranes. Cell-adhesion experiments using NIH 3T3 fibroblasts demonstrated distinct effects of the two brush chemistries: PDEGMA-modified membranes did not significantly reduce cell attachment compared with tissue culture polystyrene, whereas POEGMA-modified membranes exhibited pronounced antifouling properties, significantly reducing cell attachment independently of brush thickness within the investigated range. To provide a route toward surfaces that combine antifouling properties with controlled cell adhesion, POEGMA brushes were extended with a poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) block. The successful formation of the block copolymer was confirmed by atomic force microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The resulting epoxide-functionalized brush architecture provides a basis for future post-polymerization modification with cell-adhesive ligands. This approach combines spatially patterned lipid membranes with chemically tunable polymer brushes, offering opportunities to engineer cell-interactive interfaces for biomimetic cell culture and studies of cell–surface interactions.

title: Molecular Engineering of Customizable Resin-Derived Hard Carbon Framework for Efficient Sodium Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Owing to their high carbon yield and molecular controllability, resins have emerged as promising precursors for hard carbon (HC) anodes in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, achieving synergistic optimization of carbon microcrystals and sub-nanopores during resin pyrolysis to enhance sodium storage capacity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a spatial-chemistry-directed crosslinking (SCDC) strategy, based on the Mannich reaction of selected target molecules (TMs) within a resin network, is proposed. Owing to the steric hindrance of gem-dimethyl groups and the carboxyl-group-mediated interactions, the formation of nanoscale closed pores was facilitated while the continuity of sp2-hybridized carbon microcrystals was ensured and a large interlayer spacing was maintained. Through this approach, an HC architecture with elongated pseudo-graphitic domains and abundant closed pores is constructed in a synergistic manner, affording excellent electronic and ionic transport kinetics. The engineered HC exhibits an enhanced reversible capacity of 427.5 mAh g–1 and an outstanding initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.18%, along with a high reversible initial capacity of 346.7 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and a capacity retention of up to 85.3% after 500 cycles. This study provides new insights into the microstructural design for high-capacity, high-rate sodium storage.

title: Intelligent hydrovoltaic actuation with proactive ion regulation during solar desalination

abstract: Solar desalination offers a sustainable approach to freshwater generation, yet it is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation at evaporation interfaces. While common salt-rejecting strategies can mitigate macroscopic fouling, they fail to achieve real-time monitoring and active management of salts at the metastable stage. Local ion enrichment and associated pre-crystallization processes will degrade efficiency through increased mass-transfer resistance and vaporization enthalpy. title: Van der Waals-modulated integration strategy unlocks scalable fabrication of high-density organic electronic and optoelectronic devices
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The advancement of organic electronics and optoelectronics fundamentally depends on the development of high-precision integration technologies. However, existing manufacturing approaches for organic semiconductors, particularly conventional photolithography and stencil lithography, are plagued by an intractable trade-off between integration density and device performance. Here we report a van der Waals (vdW)-modulated integration strategy that circumvents this long-standing bottleneck, enabling concurrent high-density and high-performance organic devices. By tailoring the surface chemistry of an ultrathin Parylene shadow mask, we precisely tune interfacial vdW interactions to orchestrate deterministic mask manipulation and high-fidelity patterning. Consequently, organic field-effect transistor (OFET) arrays achieve a device density of 2,500 transistors cm−2 with an average on-state current density of 1.20 μA μm−1, among the highest reported for integrated organic electronics. Furthermore, this strategy is extended to monolithic OFET-organic light-emitting diode (OLED) integration, yielding efficient light-emitting transistor arrays. This work establishes an integration route that preserves the organic semiconductor interface while avoiding direct photolithographic contact with the active layer, opening a route toward large-scale, multifunctional organic integrated systems.

title: Naphthalene-Fused Meta-Dual-Boron Compounds Enable an 80 nm Red Shift with Concurrently Narrowed Full Widths at Half Maximum
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multiple resonance emitters are highly sought after for their intrinsically narrowband emission, yet achieving long-wavelength emission without spectral broadening remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a naphthalene-fused rigid π-extension strategy based on the meta-positioned dual boron framework BBCz-DB by replacing its peripheral carbazole units with naphthalene fragments to develop the yellow MR emitter DB-CzNa. This molecular design leverages the dual aromaticity of naphthalene: while the global π-delocalization effectively narrows the energy gap, the preserved local aromaticity maintains a highly rigid molecular framework, which significantly suppresses excited-state vibronic coupling. This synergistic effect allows the MR emitters to achieve a pronounced emission red shift without sacrificing their narrow emission characteristics. Consequently, DB-CzNa achieves an 80 nm red shift relative to BBCz-DB, delivering yellow emission at 546 nm with an ultra-narrow full width at half maximum of 16 nm (0.07 eV) in toluene. A sensitized fluorescence organic light emitting diode device based on DB-CzNa affords a yellow electroluminescence at 556 nm with a full widths at half maximum of 24 nm and a maximum external quantum efficiency of 26.9%. This work demonstrates that judicious naphthalene fusion on meta-dual boron frameworks provides a powerful strategy to overcome the trade-off between spectral redshift and broadening.

title: Dual-Targeted Thalidomide Nanoliposomes Suppress Neutrophil-Driven Inflammation in Intestinal Behçet’s Disease
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Excessive neutrophil recruitment, vascular activation, and platelet-associated inflammatory interfaces are implicated in intestinal tissue injury in intestinal Behçet’s disease (intestinal BD), whereas conventional systemic therapies offer limited spatial control over drug exposure within active intestinal lesions. Here, we developed thalidomide-loaded nanoliposomes co-functionalized with a neutrophil elastase-binding peptide (NEBP) and a P-selectin-binding peptide (PSN), designated Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip, to engage complementary activated neutrophil-associated and P-selectin-associated inflammatory interfaces. Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 116.6 ± 5.7 nm, a thalidomide encapsulation efficiency of 91.43 ± 0.71%, and reduced initial burst release, while maintaining colloidal stability during storage and simulated gastrointestinal exposure. Surface ligand density was estimated from the feed composition. Ligand-dependent interactions were observed in activated endothelial cells and neutrophil-like cells; in activated endothelial cells, liposome-associated fluorescence increased from 7.42% for Thd-Lip to 40.55% for Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip and decreased to 1.10% following free PSN competition. Additional validation supported PSN-dependent association with activated platelets and greater inflamed-tissue association of the dual-ligand formulation than with either single-ligand formulation. In vivo, Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip showed preferential and prolonged retention within inflamed intestinal tissues, with intestinal fluorescence remaining approximately 2.6-fold higher than that of Thd-Lip at 24 h. LC–MS/MS quantification further showed increased total intestinal thalidomide exposure and a higher intestine/plasma concentration ratio after Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip administration. In a murine intestinal BD-like model, Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip alleviated intestinal injury, restored colon length toward the healthy level, reduced neutrophil infiltration and local inflammatory cytokine expression, attenuated responses involving IL-17A+CD4+ and IFN-γ+CD4+ T cells, and partially restored the Foxp3+ regulatory T cell compartment. Microbiome, metabolomic, and transcriptomic analyses further indicated broader treatment-associated changes in the intestinal inflammatory microenvironment. Collectively, these findings suggest that dual-targeted nanoliposomes improve lesion-directed thalidomide delivery and suppress neutrophil-driven intestinal inflammation, supporting a pathology-guided nanotherapeutic strategy for intestinal BD.

title: Symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient CO2 electroreduction in strong acidic media
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in strong acidic media (pH ≤ 2) offers many unique advantages compared to alkaline electrolytes, but it still remains some significant challenges including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), low selectivity and poor stability. Herein, we report that symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites incorporated within ultrathin covalent organic polymer nanosheets (p-Ni1/2Pc), can simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient acidic CO2RR. Direct visualization via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the presence of Ni vacancies and uncoordinated pyrrolic N, which collectively break the local symmetry around Ni sites. This asymmetry not only optimizes the electronic structure of Ni sites to kinetically favor CO2RR over HER, but more importantly, it reconfigures the interfacial hydrogen-bond network via uncoordinated pyrrolic N. The reconstructed hydrogen-bond network effectively restricts proton transfer, while symmetry breaking creates a CO2-enriched local microenvironment. Consequently, p-Ni1/2Pc catalyst exhibits a remarkable 97.5% CO Faraday efficiency (FE) and a maximum 402.9 mA cm−2 partial current density (j

title: Ripple-induced fast-ion losses modeling in the WEST tokamak
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: The confinement of fast ions is of crucial importance in present and future tokamaks. In typical ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH)-heated scenarios in WEST, fast-ion losses can represent more than 20% of the total injected power. To investigate the origin and underlying mechanisms of these losses, we perform simulations of fast hydrogen ion trajectories in a realistic three-dimensional magnetic field. A weighting method is proposed as a post-process to study a particle distribution function with anisotropic temperatures, while preserving uniform statistics in terms of energy. The influence of the initial and final particle position in phase space is studied in details. The simulation results show that ripple losses fall into two categories: deeply trapped particles moving vertically towards the baffle, and drifting bananas striking the antenna along the direction of the magnetic field. If fast particle losses to the baffle can be directly compared with infrared (IR) measurements, diagnosing particles striking the antennas is more challenging, as IR cameras detect a combination of fast-ion losses, plasma heat convection, and radiation. A net reduction of baffle strikes is observed for particles accelerated on the high field side, whereas antenna strikes, in contrast, may be enhanced. Hence, this study suggests that optimizing the ICRH absorption layer position involves a trade-off: reducing deeply trapped losses at the cost of increasing drifting banana losses.

title: Topology-Dependent and Size-Controlled Singlet Oxygen Generation in Porphyrinic Coordination Frameworks for Antifungal Photodynamic Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two different coordination materials built with the same starting reagents, 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-pyridyl)porphyrin (H2TPyP) and Zn(NO3)2•6H2O, a nonporous 1D-porphyrin-based coordination polymer (CP) [Zn(TPyP)]n (UDS-4) exhibiting a zig-zag topology, and a porous 3D metal-organic framework (MOF) [Zn2(TPyP)(NO2)2]n (UDS-2), have been prepared in various particle sizes. Both nanosized materials exhibited stronger detected singlet oxygen (1O2(1Δg)) near 1280 nm than their bulk counterparts under the measurement conditions, with nanoUDS-2 giving the strongest signal. We then evaluated whether the enhanced 1O2 generation leads to improved antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) efficacy. In vitro assays using Botrytis cinerea revealed growth inhibition thresholds of ∼25 ppm for nanoUDS-2, compared to ∼50 ppm for bulk UDS-2, while UDS-4 and the free base ligand exhibited negligible activity. In contrast, nanoUDS-4 required substantially higher concentrations, with a growth inhibition threshold of 200 ppm. Concurrently, using nanoUDS-2 as the most effective photosensitizer (PS), visible-light treatment of tomatoes and apples markedly suppressed grey mold lesions without detectable damage to the fruit.

title: Photobiocatalysis at the interface of biocatalysis and biomimetic chemocatalysis
source: Nature Catalysis
abstract: This Perspective analyses representative photobiocatalytic systems to uncover the synergies between biomimetic and chemomimetic strategies and provides a framework for future developments in the field.

title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). Here we present high-resolution neodymium isotope (εNd) records from a depth transect in the equatorial Atlantic over the iNHG. We find a persistent latitudinal and depth gradient in neodymium isotope values in the deep Atlantic during the Late Pliocene, absent in the Early Pleistocene, indicating an expansion of NADW extent over the iNHG. In contrast, our reconstruction suggests very little glacial-interglacial variability in NADW extent during both the Late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene. These results suggest deep-water circulation was substantially different during a warm climate state, with implications for the role of NADW formation during major climate transitions and its future stability.

title: Ligand-Mediated Long-Range Interactions Enable Selective Activation of H2O2 for Efficient Water Decontamination
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Steering hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) activation to selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2•−) offers a potent solution for water decontamination, especially under neutral or even alkaline conditions. However, the practical potential of this approach has long been constrained by inefficient O2•− generation due to non-selective O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation. Here, we develop a biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) strategy to synthesize a meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin iron (TCPP-Fe) catalyst that directs heterolytic O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation, leading to predominant O2•− generation with an apparent O2•− generative selectivity of 90.3% among the quantified reactive oxygen species. The TCPP-Fe catalyst exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a normalized apparent rate constant of 40.6L2min−1gH2O2−1gcat.−1" role="presentation">40.6L2min−1gH2O2−1gcat.−140.6\,{{{{\rm{L}}}}}^{2}\,{\min }^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{{\rm{H}}}}}_{2}{{{{\rm{O}}}}}_{2}}}^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{\rm{cat}}}}.}}^{-1}, which is approximately 2.1-fold higher than the next-highest value in the compiled dataset of representative Fe-based, Fe-alloy, and related catalysts. This remarkable reactivity and selectivity arise from BSCSE-induced modulation of the electronic structure of Fe sites, which facilitates efficient electron transfer between H2O2 and Fe centers while electrostatically stabilizing the Fe–*OOH intermediate to steer O2•− generation. Integrated into a continuous-flow catalytic membrane filtration system treating real secondary effluent, TCPP-Fe enables >96% bisphenol A removal with negligible Fe leaching and sustained removal performance during 120 h of operation. This work bridges biomimetic principles with heterogeneous catalysis, providing a generalizable design strategy for next-generation catalysts toward sustainable water decontamination.

title: Sinking land is the fingerprint of global water bankruptcy
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Land subsidence is the physical fingerprint of irreversible groundwater loss, yet remains absent from water governance. Embedding it as an early warning metric could help societies act before depletion becomes water bankruptcy.

title: Educational bankruptcy in a water-insecure world
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Engineers can enter the water sector through undergraduate engineering programmes that give limited attention to systems thinking, governance literacy and agency. Where these capabilities remain underdeveloped, the resulting mismatch constitutes an educational bankruptcy that can threaten water security.

title: Global partnerships for saltwater intrusion
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Saltwater intrusion is a global issue with local societal and environmental impacts. Global funding mechanisms will be key in finding place-based solutions.

title: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation of mediodorsal thalamus disrupts decision flexibility during reward learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: When learning to find the most beneficial course of action, the prefrontal cortex guides decisions by comparing estimates of the relative value of the options available. Basic neuroscience studies in animals support the view that the thalamus can regulate this activity within and across the prefrontal cortex. We studied a group of patients (n = 37) undergoing unilateral MR-guided focused ultrasound for essential tremor, performing the restless bandit, a reward reinforcement learning task, immediately before and after thalamotomy. Thalamotomy significantly impaired the proportion of switch choices during the task without affecting overall performance. This effect was observed when the task was delivered to co-incide with maximal vasogenic thalamic oedema but not in a control group tested on the same day of their treatment. A reinforcement learning model fitted to the patients’ choices replicated the effect of thalamotomy when the model increased exploitation of the bandits’ learnt value estimate. This shift in the explore-exploit trade-off, manifesting as reduced choice flexibility, co-varied with the pattern of post-operative oedema extension into the mediodorsal nucleus. These findings confirm a causal role of the thalamus and specifically the mediodorsal nucleus in regulating the extent to which value estimates are used to guide decisions and learning from reward.

title: Identification of translation events that drive nonsense-mediated mRNA decay reveals functional roles for alternative RNA isoforms
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway targets mRNAs undergoing premature translation termination for degradation. Previously, RNA-seq of yeast lacking NMD revealed that most genes targeted by NMD lack obvious premature termination codons (PTCs). We develop a combined approach using RNA-seq and 40S ribosome profiling to identify cryptic premature termination events that could account for NMD on nearly all these transcripts, including many alternative RNA transcript isoforms associated with annotated genes. Many NMD-targeted transcripts appear to be involved in two-promoter gene regulatory systems and share properties with long un-decoded transcript isoforms (LUTIs). In particular, we show that the DAL5 LUTI regulates expression of the DAL5 protein-coding mRNA in response to changes to environmental nitrogen. Our work expands the functional roles for LUTIs and establishes the importance of NMD in their regulation.

title: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). RSM01 is a long-acting RSV monoclonal antibody (mAb) in development for LMICs. In vitro generation of RSM01 resistant mutants has previously been unsuccessful. We systematically assessed the in vitro resistance barrier of RSM01 and the susceptibility of a panel of global contemporary strains to RSM01. Monoclonal antibody resistant mutants (MARMs) were generated by serially passaging triple plaque-purified RSV-A2 and RSV-B1 using HEp-2 cells under pressure from RSM01, nirsevimab, or palivizumab, followed by phenotypic and genotypic characterisation. Moderate resistance was defined as > 3-fold and high resistance as > 30-fold increase in IC50 compared with parental virus.
