The susceptibility of contemporary global clinical strains to RSM01 was tested in a neutralisation assay. RSV-A and B strains developed high resistance to palivizumab and nirsevimab, while RSM01 pressure induced moderate resistance. No MARMs demonstrated a fitness advantage. RSM01 neutralised global contemporary strains. In conclusion, in vitro RSM01 resistance was infrequent and moderate and RSM01 had broad activity against circulating strains. The confirmation of the high barrier to resistance of RSM01 is encouraging and provides an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

title: Dynamic staged solid electrolyte interphase via sequential chemical and electrochemical reactions for highly reversible zinc battery
source: Chem
abstract: Fluorinated cations and anions are incorporated to synergistically restructure the EDL architecture, thereby enabling the formation of a dynamic staged SEI with an organic upper and an inorganic-rich inner via chemical and electrochemical reactions. The preferential adsorption of FPy+ cations promotes adsorption of the OTF− anion at the EDL, thereby engineering an EDL architecture with low active water. This not only facilitates the formation of a dynamic staged SEI film but also effectively mitigates interfacial side reactions.

title: Contemporary synthetic tools for the total synthesis of natural products
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract: This Tutorial Review discusses uses of modern synthetic tools in the total synthesis of natural products over the last five years, including photocatalysis, electrochemistry, biocatalysis, skeletal editing, flow chemistry and mechanochemistry.

title: Radical addition approaches for 2m/2π-intermolecular reactions of alkenes and alkynes
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract: This review organizes radical intermolecular reactions of two π-components through the 2m/2π-synthon framework, highlighting the main strategies used to sort alkene and alkyne partners.

title: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb caused an outbreak of >100,000 cases globally, with highest disease burden in people living with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), those with CD4 count 3. We performed an extensive autopsy on a fatal case of mpox in a man living with advanced HIV-1, who achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution despite > 6 months antiretroviral therapy and had progressive necrotizing mucocutaneous mpox disease despite multiple prolonged mpox-targeted therapies. We quantified MPXV DNA across 76 autopsy samples from different anatomical sites and observed a high burden in skin and mucosal tissue and a lower burden in all central nervous system (CNS) tissues tested. However, we detected replication-competent MPXV in multiple CNS tissues and confirmed neuronal and glial cell infection using RNA-scope in situ hybridization. MPXV sequencing from body and brain tissues revealed widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated variants. This case proves that replication-competent MPXV and tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates can infect and persist in the CNS of people with advanced HIV thus informing future therapeutic design.

title: Whole-brain modeling of dynamic causal circuits in human cognition using amortized variational inference
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding dynamic mechanisms underlying cognition remains a major challenge in human neuroscience. Here, we develop, validate, and apply Multivariate Dynamical Systems Identification with Amortized Variational Inference (MDSI-AVI), a computational framework designed to address critical challenges in capturing asymmetric, context-dependent, whole-brain directed interactions while accounting for regional hemodynamic response variability in fMRI data. MDSI-AVI leverages simulation-based inference through forward and reverse variational inference to address the limitations of conventional variational methods in high-dimensional settings. By averaging over uncertainty in hemodynamic response parameters using forward simulation, MDSI-AVI provides well-calibrated posteriors of directed connectivity that scale efficiently to networks with hundreds of nodes. Applied to Human Connectome Project data (N = 728), MDSI-AVI provides insights into working memory mechanisms, identifying the dorsal anterior insula as a critical hub influencing activity at the whole-brain level. We demonstrate task-dependent modulation of causal influences, where the salience network drives frontoparietal network activity, which differentially influences the default mode and sensorimotor networks depending on working memory load. These whole-brain causal interactions distinguish task conditions with high accuracy and predict working memory performance. Our framework demonstrates reproducible results across whole-brain parcellations, establishing MDSI-AVI as a robust tool for advancing our understanding of circuit dynamics in cognition and disease.

title: Energy poverty in an era of geopolitical instability: The role of Chinese FDI and south–south cooperation in Africa
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: The rising geopolitical fragmentation, driven by geopolitical tensions, conflicts and wars, has reshaped the global energy landscape, increasing uncertainty and vulnerability in energy markets. These disruptions present serious challenges for different economies in the Global South, where countries already face significant difficulties in facilitating energy transition and mitigating energy poverty. In this context, South-South cooperation may represent an important tool to address energy challenges, particularly through foreign investment. This study investigates the contribution of Chinese FDI to reducing energy poverty in Africa through different channels and whether conflict conditions influence the extent to which Chinese FDI contributes to improving energy outcomes. Our study contributes to the literature on the role of Chinese foreign capital in reducing energy poverty in Africa by examining both the underlying mechanisms and the potential role of conflict conditions in shaping these effects. To empirically explore this complex nexus, we rely on Structural Equation Modelling using a set of energy and socioeconomic variables from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal a significant positive association between Chinese FDI and energy performance, with the prosperity channel representing the main mechanism. This association appears weaker in conflict-affected contexts, suggesting that geopolitical stability conditions the extent to which foreign investment is associated with improved energy outcomes. Policymakers in the region should consider creating a more attractive and stable investment environment to promote trade ties with Chinese companies, as these ties could be used as a tool to alleviate energy poverty.

title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Humanitarian emergencies test the resilience of global health systems, yet policy is constrained by limited empirical evidence on the magnitude and timing of service delivery disruptions. Here, we assess the association between measured childhood vaccination—as a proxy for health service delivery—and forced displacement, armed conflict, and natural disasters. Across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023, sudden increases in displaced populations were associated with declines in vaccination coverage of approximately 3 to 6 percentage points, persisting for 2 to 3 years before recovery. Dose-response analyses revealed a nonlinear relationship: coverage fell steeply at low displacement levels and plateaued at extreme exposure. Conflict intensity followed a similar nonlinear pattern that plateaued near 3000 annual battle-related deaths while mortality from natural disasters showed no detectable association with coverage. Displacement’s association was largely independent of armed conflict, indicating that displacement may act as a distinct, additive shock rather than a proxy for violence.

title: Jumping from scaling to scale-up
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Jonathan Boreyko discusses how to utilize scaling analysis to progress from fundamental discovery toward practical applications with a close look at capillary-inertial jumping droplets.

title: Morphogenesis of the muscular ventricular septum is driven by retinoic acid signalling to myocardium
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mammalian heart is divided into four chambers by septa that isolate systemic and pulmonary circulation and are hotspots of congenital heart defects (CHD). The muscular ventricular septum develops between left and right ventricular cardiomyocytes derived from the first and second heart fields. Despite its clinical importance, mechanisms underlying development of the ventricular septum are poorly understood. Here we show that myocardial reception of retinoic acid (RA) signalling regulates formation of the compact septal core. Activation of a dominant negative RA receptor in second heart field-derived myocardium during septal morphogenesis results in a deep interventricular cleft and bifid cardiac apex. This phenotype is preceded by ectopic trabecular contributions to a RA-independent septal primordium. Molecular analysis identifies defective cardiomyocyte maturation and impaired RAC1 activation in mutant hearts. These results support an infolding and RA-dependent fusion model of septal morphogenesis, providing new insights into ventricular development and the origins of CHD.

title: Gut microbiota GABA regulation by intestinal pH osmolality and microbial consumption
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) by the gut microbiota has garnered attention due to its potential role as a driver of gut-brain axis signaling. However, mechanisms regulating microbiota-derived GABA under physiological conditions remain unclear. Here, we identified low pH and high osmolality as promoters of GABA production in the gut microbe Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron by driving changes in the expression of the glutamate decarboxylase system. pH also emerged as a critical factor for enhancing GABA production in a broader set of gut microbes. However, in the cecal microbiota of specific pathogen-free mice and in an ex vivo model of the human colon microbiota, GABA levels did not increase under physiologically relevant acidic conditions. This can partly be explained by microbial GABA consumption. Consistently, reducing cecal pH increased GABA levels in Oligo-MM12 mice, a gnotobiotic model lacking GABA-consuming gut microbes. Our findings highlight the intricate balance between gut microbial GABA production, consumption, and environmental factors such as pH and osmolality.

title: In vivo dynamics of ovulation and oocyte entrance into the oviduct in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ovulation is a dynamic multistep process essential for female fertility. Although central to reproductive success, the real-time behaviors of oocytes, ovarian tissues, and oviducts during the ovulatory process in vivo remain unknown. Here, we use intravital microscale volumetric imaging to reveal the in vivo spatiotemporal dynamics of key stages of ovulation associated with follicle opening, oocyte release, and the subsequent transport of the ovulated oocyte into the oviduct in mice. Unexpectedly, we find a time lag between follicle opening and subsequent abrupt changes in follicular volume and oocyte position, followed by the release of the cumulus-oocyte complex (COC). Remarkably, oocytes deform into an elliptical shape as they squeeze through a relatively small opening of the follicle but regain a spherical shape shortly after being released. We also discover repetitive pulses of fluid emitted from the oviduct that inflate the periovarian space, increasing fluid flow required for COC movement into the oviduct. These findings uncover previously unrecognized cellular, tissue, and organ-level mechanisms that coordinate ovulation and oocyte transport, offering potential insights into the etiology of ovulatory disorders and female infertility.

title: Confronting water bankruptcy
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: With 2030 and the conclusion of the current round of Sustainable Development Goals on the horizon, the world has entered a state of water bankruptcy. A collection of opinion and research explores how this bankruptcy affects environmental and social systems and asks how we return to sustainable and resilient water futures.

title: Transforming spinel LiMn2O4 into a Na-layered cathode
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The positive electrode structures of practical sodium-ion batteries are generally confined to polyanionic or layered transition metal oxide frameworks, where the trade-off between specific energy and structural stability limits their application. As a well-established positive electrode structure in lithium-ion batteries, the spinel framework has abundant storage sites for alkali metal ions, but it has received less attention for sodium-ion batteries. Here we show that spinel LiMn2O4 can be transformed into a sodium-ion positive electrode. Electrochemical sodiation drives Mn-ion migration along an octahedral–tetrahedral–octahedral pathway, creating a layered/spinel heterostructure for further sodium storage. Moreover, residual spinel domains inhibit the strain and structural degradation within the layered structure. Consequently, a 26650 cylindrical cell using a LiMn2O4-derived sodium-ion positive electrode achieves a capacity of 3.85 Ah and retains 95.7% capacity after 900 cycles (1.925 A). This work demonstrates that spinel LiMn2O4 can serve as a viable positive electrode for sodium-ion batteries, and that electrochemical transformation is a feasible approach for creating positive electrode frameworks.

title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures (Tc), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO2 plane – as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) – and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record Tc of Bi2223.

title: Upcycling of polyolefin and polyester mixtures via a single-atom alloy
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Upcycling of mixed plastic waste is challenging due to the complex compositions and high sorting costs, lacking robust catalysts for simultaneous conversion of polyolefins and polyesters. Herein, guided by machine learning, we design a Ru1Cu/CeO2-GR single-atom alloy catalyst that enables one-pot hydrogenolysis of mixed plastics into fuel-range hydrocarbons. Ru single atoms anchored on Cu nanoparticles lower C–C bond cleavage barriers, while Cu suppresses benzene ring overhydrogenation. Under mild conditions (280 °C, 30 bar H2), the catalyst delivers ~75% liquid yield (C5–C22) with 59.5%–62.7% C8–C16 fraction and ~15% aromatic products yield from five-component mixed plastics. Life cycle and techno-economic analyses confirm that this direct upcycling route outperforms traditional sorted recycling with lower environmental impacts and higher economic benefits. This work provides a sustainable and economically viable strategy for mixed plastic waste valorization.

title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacteriophages, viruses infecting bacteria, are abundant in the human gut, but their population-level structure and metabolic associations remain unclear Here we present a foundational characterisation of the gut phageome using deep shotgun metagenomic data in a large population-based cohort (n = 1,069: TwinsUK). We assembled 116,740 non-redundant vOTUs of which 52.9% were predicted to be temperate and 47.0% virulent. Individuals harboured an average of 3,370 vOTUs, mostly at low abundances, exhibiting structured population-level co-abundance patterns with bacterial species including Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Blautia wexlerae. Phageome diversity was mostly driven by environmental factors, with modest heritable components. We detected 4 significant vOTU diet associations. Additionally, 6,572 phages were associated with short-chain fatty acids and secondary bile acids, identifying extensive population-level associations between phage-associated genomic variation and microbial metabolites. Over 100 vOTUs encoded auxiliary metabolic genes, while a distinct subset of phages encoded virulence-associated genes, including vacuolating autotransporter toxin (vat) and LPS glucosyltransferases (gtrA, gtrB, gtr) implicated in O-antigen modification and immune invasion, and showed consistent co-abundance patterns with bacterial species previously associated with opportunistic or pathobiont features. These results identify structured population-level associations between phage-associated genomic elements, bacterial communities, and microbial metabolites, motivating future experimental and mechanistic studies.

title: Vinylcyclopropanes in Rearrangement Reactions
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more than six decades of development, vinylcyclopropane chemistry has undergone remarkable evolution, particularly in recent years. Accordingly, these transformations have emerged as powerful tools for the generation of molecular complexity through strain-release-driven reaction manifolds involving both homolytic and heterolytic bond-cleavage mechanistic pathways. This Review provides a comprehensive account of the current state of the art in vinylcyclopropane rearrangement chemistry, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic principles governing these transformations and on their synthetic applications in modern organic synthesis. The different rearrangement modes accessible to vinylcyclopropane derivatives are discussed, including stereomutation processes, vinylcyclopropane-cyclopentene rearrangements, divinylcyclopropane-cycloheptadiene rearrangements, vinylcyclopropane-to-skipped-1,4-diene rearrangements, and cycloisomerization reactions involving specifically functionalized vinylcyclopropane substrates. Particular attention is devoted to the influence of substrate structure, stereochemical features, catalyst design, and thermodynamic and kinetic factors on reaction outcome, in terms of efficiency and selectivity. The broad applicability of these transformations in the synthesis of structurally sophisticated carbo- and heterocyclic architectures, including natural-product-related targets, is highlighted together with current limitations and future opportunities for the continued development of vinylcyclopropane chemistry.

title: STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis links innate immune activation to tau pathology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Genetic risk for Alzheimer’s disease and related tauopathies is strongly enriched in pathways governing microglial activation and cholesterol metabolism, yet how these processes converge to drive neurodegeneration remains unclear. Here, we identify the oxysterol 25-hydroxycholesterol (25-HC) as a pathogenic lipid downstream of the cGAS-STING–Interferon (IFN) pathway. In models of tau pathology, interferon signaling induces microglial expression of Cholesterol 25-hydroxylase (CH25H), the enzyme responsible for 25-HC production. Ch25h deletion in female P301S mice suppressed tau aggregation, preserved synapses, prevented brain atrophy, and rescued memory. Mechanistically, loss of CH25H disrupted STING trafficking, attenuated IFN activation, and dampened self-perpetuating microglial inflammation. Strikingly, 25-HC directly accelerated tau propagation in human iPSC-derived neurons. It also disrupted lysosomal and mitochondrial lipid composition, driving cholesteryl ester accumulation and promoting neuronal death under tau-induced stress. These findings define a STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis that bridges innate immune activation to tau pathology and toxicity, offering a tractable therapeutic pathway for inflammation-driven neurodegenerative conditions.

title: Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off between achieving spatial charge separation, which is necessary for dipole formation, and maintaining sufficient wavefunction overlap to ensure efficient radiative recombination. Here, we overcome this trade-off in the two-dimensional perovskite (AE3T)PbI4 by leveraging organic-inorganic band-edge engineering to induce frontier-state hybridization, thereby forming bright hybridized dipolar excitons with spatially indirect character and appreciable optical transition strength. These excitons combine an out-of-plane permanent electric-dipole component, room-temperature nonlinear transport consistent with long-range dipole–dipole repulsion, and finite optical transition dipole moments. Beyond addressing a key constraint in dipolar-exciton design, this work establishes frontier-state hybridization as a molecular design principle for constructing optically active, electrically polarized excitons in low-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Lipid droplets amplify inflammasome-driven cytokine secretion in infection and inflammation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) accumulating in infected cells are traditionally viewed as passive nutrient stores exploited by invading pathogens. Here, we show that during infection with virulent Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), but not BCG, host LDs orchestrate protective immune responses by bridging the ISGylation and inflammasome pathways. Proteomic and imaging analyses reveal the selective recruitment of ISGylated proteins together with caspase-1 and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) precursors to the LD surface. Comparative LD proteomics in wild-type and ISG15-deficient macrophages, combined with ISGylome profiling, identify ISGylated proteins as mediators of pro-IL-1β binding to LDs. Functionally, disruption of LD biogenesis in primary human macrophages impairs mature IL-1β secretion and compromises Mtb control. Notably, this LD-dependent amplification of IL-1β release is not restricted to microbial stimuli but also occurs in response to sterile inflammasome activation. Collectively, these findings redefine LDs as immunoactive organelles integrating microbial and danger signals to potentiate inflammasome-dependent IL-1β responses during infection and inflammation.

title: Mapping redox networks in cardiomyocytes reveals non-overlapping response pathways for cytosolic versus mitochondrial H₂O₂ signaling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are essential redox messengers, yet their effects depend on concentration, localization, and duration. Here, we investigate how compartment-specific hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) production influences cardiomyocyte redox signaling and function. Using human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CM) expressing the H₂O₂ biosensor HyPer fused to D-amino acid oxidase (DAO), we achieve chemogenetic control of H₂O₂ generation in the cytosol, mitochondria, or nucleus. Cytosolic H₂O₂ propagates throughout the cell, whereas mitochondrially generated H₂O₂ remains spatially restricted, reflecting compartmentalized antioxidant buffering. Cytosolic H₂O₂ impairs contractility and relaxation in both 2D and 3D engineered heart tissue models, accompanied by preferential oxidation of Z-disc–associated and actin-binding proteins and by altered sarcomere organization. Antioxidant treatment attenuates these effects. In contrast, mitochondrially produced H₂O₂ is better tolerated and associated with adaptive redox remodeling, with preserved contractile performance that is antagonized by conoidin A-induced inhibition of cytosolic peroxiredoxin activity. These findings demonstrate that the subcellular source of H₂O₂ shapes redox propagation, oxidation patterns, and functional responses, highlighting redox compartmentalization as a determinant of cardiomyocyte performance and stress resilience.

title: Partially functional hypomorphic missense variants in BRCA2 are reduced penetrance pathogenic variants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Identification of partial loss-of-function (hypomorphic), reduced penetrance pathogenic missense variants (RPPVs) and assessment of the clinical relevance of these variants is needed for improved hereditary cancer risk estimation. Here we show that 70 candidate hypomorphic missense variants in the DNA-binding domain of BRCA2 reduce homologous recombination DNA repair activity and endogenous cell survival, decrease RAD51 foci formation, and increase sensitivity to Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. The 34 “strong” hypomorphs with greatest effects on function are associated with moderate risks of female breast cancer and later ages of diagnosis than pathogenic variants (PVs), and 14 of these variants can be classified as “likely pathogenic” by integration of functional data into a ClinGen BRCA1/2 variant curation model. In addition, 32% of tumors with hypomorphic variants and corresponding loss of heterozygosity for BRCA2 display homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) compared to 83% of tumors with PVs and 7% with benign variants. These RPPVs represent a class of BRCA2 variants that have implications for the clinical management of carriers.

title: Atomic-level coordination-engineered quantum dots orchestrate mitochondrial energy rescue for diabetic bone regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Diabetic bone regeneration is critically impaired by a cellular energy crisis that disrupts osteoimmunological processes. While mitochondrial transfer represents a potential metabolic rescue mechanism, this process can be hijacked in diabetes mellitus to propagate inflammation. Current mitochondria-protecting strategies fail to address the spatiotemporal dynamics of intercellular mitochondrial transfer in regenerative tissues. Here, we identify key mitochondrial donor cells, a therapeutically targetable cell population functionally coupled to osteoimmunological outcomes via mitochondrial transfer. We design a nanotherapeutic based on atomic-level coordination-engineered quantum dots to restore functional mitochondrial transfer for energy homeostasis. These quantum dots markedly reduce the ROS catalytic reaction energy barrier and protect mitochondria. Furthermore, their Mn-coordinated degradation fragments activate the CaMKKβ-AMPK signaling axis in diabetes mellitus. This enhanced mitochondrial quality control and transfer efficiency render macrophages competent mitochondria donors. Consequently, our work provides a transformative approach to correct pathological mitochondrial transfer and rescue diabetic bone repair.

title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack.

title: Single-cell mass accumulation reveals copiotrophic bacterial growth rates in native seawater
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The growth of marine microbial communities drives ocean biogeochemical cycles, yet the growth rates of individual species remain poorly understood. Copiotrophic bacteria, such as Vibrio species, are thought to live a feast-and-famine existence, as their capacity for rapid growth contrasts with their typically low abundance. Here we use a microfluidic mass sensor adapted to directly measure subtle and otherwise undetectable mass accumulation of individual marine bacteria in native seawater. We observe growth of several copiotrophic bacteria and find that Vibrio species consistently grew across diverse temporal conditions and had higher buoyant mass than co-occurring species. Remarkably, their growth rates were similar across samples collected over days to months and followed a well-known nutrient growth law previously established in laboratory cultures. Overall, our findings suggest that low-abundance species may play a disproportionately large role in the marine carbon cycle, with rapid biomass turnover driven by high growth rates balanced by intense predation.

title: Resilience as a governing principle in water governance
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Water governance often treats resilience as an end state, achieved mainly through technocratic decision-making and standard engineering tools. Drawing on five international cases, we argue that resilience should instead guide governance design and operation through adaptability, coordination, learning and accountability.

title: Monitoring water attacks
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Attacks on critical water infrastructure have become normalized in modern military conflict. To counter this, argues Hussam Hussein, water scientists must build and maintain real-time monitoring and documentation infrastructure in active conflict zones.

title: Water as our common denominator in the fragmented world
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: In the era of growing political polarization, water can be a force for cooperation towards a global agenda of unity, security, prosperity and sustainability, argues Kaveh Madani.

title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

title: Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mechanochemistry is an expanding and generally green synthetic route, which is attracting more and more chemists in academia and industry. Yet, its applicability is often still limited by the lack of information on the mechanochemical processes. Therefore, to help elucidating reaction pathways in the solid state, we need to develop new real time monitoring techniques. Here we present an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando (i.e., real-time in situ) mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this original technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in ball-milling (BM). Lastly, we show that our NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution, during a reaction, directly inside the milling jar. This method, BM-NQR, represents a promising functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling syntheses.

title: Dearomatization and cycloaddition of furans and indoles enable divergent syntheses of spirooxindole alkaloids
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dearomatization has revived recently as a key tactic in organic synthesis due to major methodological developments that allow mild chemoselective dearomatization. A major challenge of this dearomatization tactic to strategically couple different dearomatization products and the cycloaddition of two different dearomatization products remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report the development of green oxidative dearomatization of indoles and furans and their formal cycloaddition reaction, leading to efficient construction of versatile biologically active tetracyclic spirooxindoles. Oxidation of furan derivatives (furfuryl amides) induces concomitant rearrangement (aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement) to provide 3-piperidones, which for the first time are elaborated with 3-4 steps to functionalized 1-piperideines and react with 3-(2-bromoethyl)−2-oxindoles derived from green oxidative dearomatization of indoles. This synthetic strategy enables rapid collective synthesis of >30 spirooxindoles within 7 steps and 10 spirooxindole natural products within 10-14 steps with satisfactory overall yields. This work establishes a blueprint for coupling distinct dearomatization manifolds in complex molecule synthesis, with immediate implications for medicinal chemistry and natural product-inspired drug discovery.

title: Hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring steers CO electroreduction toward ethanol
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of carbon monoxide (CO) to ethanol is challenged by competing pathways that remove oxygen from reaction intermediates and form ethylene. Here we show that strontium (Sr)-modified copper (Cu) promotes ethanol formation and propose hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring as a mechanism for oxygen-retention. Sr-derived sites are proposed to host hydroxyl adjacent to Cu reaction sites, creating a site-differentiated interface that shift hydroxyl from site-competing spectators to selectivity-directing components. In situ spectroscopy reveals Sr-dependent changes in signals associated with adsorbed CO and oxygen-containing intermediates. Calculations suggest that nearby Sr–OH groups can stabilize the oxygen-ends of selected intermediates through non-covalent interactions, mitigating C–O bond weakening. The resulting Sr(1.0%)-Cu catalyst achieves an ethanol Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65.4% at 1.0 A cm−2, with an ethanol-to-ethylene FE ratio of ~18.7, compared with a maximum of ~2.0 for pristine Cu. It also operates for over 200 hours in a membrane-electrode assembly and retains ethanol selectivity under syngas feeds. These findings highlight the spatial organization of interfacial hydroxyl species as a strategy for oxygen-retaining electrosynthesis.

title: Full-circle polychromatic photoluminescence in Mn-doped zero-dimensional metal halide under high-pressure
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polychromatic luminescent materials have attracted sustained interest owing to the potential applications in high-sensitivity visual optical sensing. Nevertheless, developing a rational design strategy that can simultaneously achieve a broad color gamut and tunable multicolor emission remains a highly challenging task. Here we show that a Mn2+-doped zero-dimensional metal halide, Mn2+:(TPA)2PbBr4 (TPA+ = tetrapropylammonium cation), demonstrates these desirable characteristics. By application of high pressure, the initial blue emission of Mn2+:(TPA)2PbBr4 undergoes a sequential transition from cyan to yellow, then to pink-purple, and ultimately returns to blue. This polychromatic color modulation originates from the interplay between the intrinsic blue emission of the [PbBr4]2- tetrahedra and the pressure-induced green-to-red shift of the [MnBr4]2- tetrahedra, accompanied by energy transfer processes between the two luminescent centers. Concurrently, enhanced hydrogen-bonding interactions between the inorganic and organic components suppress nonradiative recombination, increasing the polychromatic emission intensity, which is further amplified at low temperatures. These findings offer new insights into the mechanisms governing polychromatic emission and provide promising strategies for developing advanced optoelectronic materials.

title: Exciton binding regulation in oxygen-independent tumor photooxidation enables synchronous photoluminescence for cancer theranostics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Overcoming the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in light-driven cancer therapy remains a significant challenge for theranostics. Herein, we report a fullerene-loaded heptazine‒perylene (HP/C60) nanopolymer that enables the oxygen-independent oxidation of intracellular biomolecules via photogenerated hole transfer (+1.53 V vs. NHE). Concurrently, HP/C60 facilitates cancer theranostics through spatiotemporal fluorescence imaging with resistance to photobleaching. By precisely tuning the exciton binding energy through controlled interface-induced charge delocalization, we optimize the ratio of exciton recombination and dissociation pathways, enabling the rational allocation of photoluminescence for high-contrast bioimaging and photooxidation for efficient tumor elimination. A 20-minute red light irradiation of HP/C60 is sufficient to initiate the complete ablation of solid tumors of female mice, with the entire therapeutic process monitored via real-time fluorescence imaging. This work establishes exciton management as a universal design principle to synchronize photooxidation and photoluminescence and supports the development of organic semiconductors for cancer theranostics.

title: Stepwise transitions unlock three spin states and diverse SHG in a polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multifunctional spin-crossover materials are promising for information storage and nonlinear optics, yet stepwise spin-crossover coupled with controllable second harmonic generation switching is hindered by poor thermal stability of non-centrosymmetric lattices. Herein, we report an air-stable polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex displaying cooling-induced two-step spin-crossover but one-step transition during heating, delivering a wide thermal hysteresis of 75 K (199 K cooling / 274 K heating) via intense intermolecular cooperativity. Sequential phase evolution (P1 → P1 → Pn) creates three discrete spin configurations with c-axis cell duplication followed by a symmetry-increasing transition to full low-spin phase upon cooling. Second harmonic generation tests verify three separable nonlinear optical states consistent with magnetic responses. Crystal stacking analysis and density functional theory calculations validate that spin ordering-phase transition synergy rearranges molecular dipoles to realize stepwise second harmonic generation modulation. This study offers an original route toward dual spin-optic functional materials for optical storage applications.

title: Accounting for the mining industry’s global water footprint
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Millions of people share rivers, aquifers and coastlines with mining operations, but years of regulation and voluntary schemes have left these communities with limited knowledge of what water is withdrawn, discharged or contaminated. De-risking the sector requires mandatory transparency, which should be made a condition of the capital now flowing into critical mineral supply chains.

title: A map of multi-omics quantitative trait loci in a Chinese population reveals regulatory variations and disease links
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantitative trait loci (QTL) studies have been pivotal in mapping the genetic regulation of molecular traits but have been primarily conducted in European populations, limiting insights into diverse ethnic groups. To close this knowledge gap, we conduct a large-scale multi-omics QTL analysis using blood samples from 3,102 Chinese individuals, systematically characterizing the regulatory effects of genetic variants on DNA methylation, plasma levels of 365 inflammation-related proteins, and metabolites. Our study identifies 209 protein QTLs (pQTLs) for 155 proteins and 587 metabolite QTLs (metabQTLs) for 369 metabolites. By integrating these findings with cis-methylation QTL (meQTL) from our previous work, we define the shared genetic architecture across molecular layers. Colocalization analyses reveal 3,665 pairs of shared causal variants across traits, including loci such as LHPP, with mediation evidence supporting regulatory cascades linking DNA methylation, proteins, and metabolites. To link these molecular findings to health outcomes, we perform Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, identifying 497 potential causal relationships between molecular traits and diseases, including FCRL3 for Graves’ disease and deoxycholic acid 3-glucuronide for colorectal cancer. Collectively, we present a systematic genomic atlas of meQTLs, pQTLs, and metabQTLs specific to East Asian populations, providing critical insight into shared regulatory networks and candidate causal variants across molecular and disease phenotypes.

title: Pronounced Visible‐Light Cryptochirality Detection of Various Terpenoids via Helical Polyaromatic Capsules
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Cryptochirality refers to molecular chirality with undetectable/absent circular dichroism (CD) bands. Whereas there have been several host compounds capable of binding cryptochiral biosubstrates for their analysis, those with guest‐induced CD activity in the visible region remain quite rare so far. We herein report the host‐guest interaction‐based CD analysis of various terpenoids using two different, helical polyaromatic capsules under ambient aqueous conditions. When one molecule of CD‐inactive monoterpenoid, (–)‐carvone, is quantitatively encapsulated within a CD‐inactive capsule bearing a spheroidal cavity, the resultant host‐guest complex displays pronounced CD bands in the range of 350–430 nm with a relatively high absolute molar circular dichroism value (i.e., |Δ ε | >80 M −1 cm −1 at ∼390 nm), derived from the guest‐induced host helicity. The chirality of other cryptochiral mono/sesquiterpenoids is also detected with similar efficiency (∼30–90 M −1 cm −1 ). The enantiomeric excess (%ee) of d/l ‐mixtures of monoterpenoids can be determined with the helical cavity via comparative CD analysis. By the use of another larger capsule, di‐ and triterpenoids also induce its intense CD bands (up to ∼130 M −1 cm −1 ) in the visible region upon encapsulation. The present study highlights the potential application of helical polyaromatic hosts to the facile cryptochiral analysis of a broad range of biosubstrates with intense CD output.

title: Rationale‐Guided and Iterative Learning for Redesigning a Highly Enantio‐ and Chemoselective Flavin‐Dependent Phenolic Hydroxylase
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Flavin‐dependent monooxygenases (FDMOs) can catalyze C─H hydroxylation of phenolic compounds, yet the scope of their application has never been challenged beyond the hydroxylation of simple substrates nor explored for the ability to achieve selective hydroxylation. FDMO hydroxylation is often poorly controlled, yielding unstable, multiply hydroxylated products. Here, we used a mechanistic insight‐guided iterative learning workflow to redesign the active site of p ‐hydroxyphenylacetate hydroxylase to expand its capability for chemo‐ and enantioselective control in the synthesis of ( R )‐norepinephrine. Within only three rounds of an engineering campaign, a DISD_LG variant that switched from ( S )‐ to ( R )‐selective hydroxylation was obtained with excellent enantioselectivity (97.6%ee ( R )). This variant also produced markedly fewer multiply hydroxylated products (R )‐norepinephrine was obtained with 48.8% isolated yield and 96.2%ee ( R ). The molecular mechanisms underlying the enantio‐ and chemoselective control achieved by the DISD_LG variant were elucidated using molecular dynamics simulations. This work presents an enzyme engineering workflow to achieve kinetic resolution in combination with a controllable degree of hydroxylation, the aspects previously overlooked or underemphasized in FDMOs.

title: Promoting CO 2 Electromethanation via Reverse H‐Spillover on Zeolite Y‐Confined CuO Nanoclusters
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (eCO 2 RR) presents a promising route for converting CO 2 emissions into valuable products, with methane (CH 4 ) being particularly attractive owing to its high energy density and infrastructure compatibility. However, selective CH 4 formation via sequential *CO hydrogenation remains kinetically challenged by competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we encapsulate CuO nanoclusters within zeolite Y, where spatial confinement enables the uniform dispersion of CuO and enhances the reverse H‐spillover (RHS)‐mediated utilization of *H species generated on the zeolite support for sequential *CO hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH 4 Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% ± 1.3% at 600 mA cm −2 and 65.6% ± 1.0% at 1000 mA cm −2 . Experimental and theoretical studies show that H 2 O is preferentially activated on the zeolite support, generating *H species that are rapidly transferred to adjacent CuO via RHS for CO 2 hydrogenation. Operando spectroscopic detection of CH 4 ‐related *OCH 3 /*CH x intermediates, together with DFT calculations, indicates that zeolite–CuO interactions favor *CO hydrogenation to *CHO over *CO dimerization, thereby promoting CH 4 formation. This work establishes spatial confinement‐coupled RHS as an effective strategy for regulating interfacial *H transfer and sequential hydrogenation in the eCO 2 RR process.

title: Precise Control of Spin–Orbit Coupling for High‐Efficiency Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence: Toward Photo‐Responsive Patterning and Visual Oxygen Sensing
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Photo‐responsive pure organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials rely on the compatible synergy between high phosphorescence quantum yield ( Φ P ) and high oxygen sensitivity. However, a fundamental dilemma exists: high Φ P typically requires a shorter triplet exciton lifetime to suppress non‐radiative deactivation, whereas high oxygen sensitivity demands a longer triplet lifetime for efficient energy transfer. To resolve this contradiction, a series of pure organic RTP molecules are designed via the functional unit combination strategy. In these molecules, the flexible (4‐(tert‐butyl)phenyl)thio unit undergoes excited‐state geometric torsion, and the nonbonding n‐orbital of the sulfur atom is decoupled to varying degrees from the π‐orbital of the RTP core, enabling precise control of the spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) strength. Among them, the optimal molecule 56M2T achieves both a high oxygen sensitivity and a high Φ P of 87.6%, exhibiting excellent photo‐responsive RTP enhancement. Based on this photo‐responsive dynamic RTP, we have further developed a high‐contrast, cyclically‐stable “optical writing & humidity erasing” photo‐responsive patterning system and a low‐cost time‐dependent method for visual oxygen sensing. This work not only provides novel insights into the molecular design of highly efficient and oxygen‐sensitive RTP materials, but also sheds light on their application in the field of intelligent responses.

title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOFs) incorporate various metals and/or linkers within a periodic backbone, offering structural diversity and emergent functionalities. Typically, conventional one‐pot synthesis does not allow for any control over the spatial arrangement or sequencing of metals within the framework. Here, we present a synthetic strategy to alter metal arrangement in multimetallic MTV MOFs, yielding materials with nearly identical composition yet distinct properties. Using isostructural m CB‐Co and m CB‐Ni MOFs, we generate two MTV MOFs with different one‐dimensional Ni/Co arrangements, resulting in distinct semiconducting and magnetic properties. High‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI‐HRMS) reveals the formation of distinct precursor species in solution, suggesting that prenucleation chemistry influences the final metal arrangement. This work establishes a new approach for modulating metal arrangement in MTV MOFs, enabling tunable functional properties in multimetallic frameworks for applications in catalysis, electronics, and quantum materials.

title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m − 2 . Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

title: One Acceptor Core, Two Bright Pathways: CF 3 ‐Substituted Triazines Achieve Highly Efficient Intermolecular Exciplexes and Intramolecular TADF
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT)‐based exciplexes provide broad design flexibility through independent donor and acceptor selection, but often suffer from low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) due to limited orbital overlap. In contrast, intramolecular CT‐based thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) systems can achieve high PLQYs through controlled donor‐acceptor interactions, but generally require precise molecular design and substituent tuning. Here, we show that a CF 3 ‐substituted triazine scaffold ( T4 ) serves as a unified molecular platform for achieving highly efficient emission through both intermolecular and intramolecular CT pathways. The CzCF 3 ‐substituted derivatives T4‐2CzCF 3 and T4‐3CzCF 3 formed highly emissive intermolecular exciplexes with mCBP, achieving PLQYs of 100%. Incorporation of stronger carbazole donors afforded T4‐3Cz , which exhibited intramolecular CT‐based TADF with PLQYs reaching 100% in solution and 100% in an mCBP‐doped film. T4‐3Cz also displayed near‐infrared multiphoton absorption, with a two‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ 2 ) of 80 GM at 780 nm and a three‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ 3 ) of 2.94 × 10 −80 cm 6 s 2 at 1210 nm. Furthermore, OLEDs based on the T4‐3CzCF 3 intermolecular exciplex and the intramolecular CT‐based TADF emitter T4‐3Cz exhibited efficient electroluminescent performance. These findings establish the T4 scaffold as a versatile molecular framework that integrates highly efficient intermolecular exciplex TADF, intramolecular CT‐based TADF, multiphoton absorption, and OLED functionality.

title: Domain-encoded DNA barcodes for combinatorial multiplexed protein imaging via stepwise displacement
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Multiplexed protein imaging via DNA barcoding faces a fundamental scaling constraint: Each target requires a distinct DNA identity, making barcode capacity grow only linearly with the number of validated sequences. Combinatorial encoding in RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization achieves exponential scaling by distributing shared readout sequences across dozens of probes per transcript, but antibody-based protein labeling lacks this multiprobe architecture. Here, we report domain-encoded DNA barcodes (DEDBs), which embed combinatorial identity within the internal domain organization of a single-stranded DNA scaffold. Three orthogonal encoding units arranged across three encoding domains define a theoretical design space of 27 barcodes. Sequence reuse does not compromise readout specificity: Each read strand spans two adjacent domains, so a mismatched read strand inevitably contains a continuous stretch of noncomplementary bases and forms a thermodynamically disfavored intermediate that is subsequently displaced by the perfectly matched strand. We term this self-correcting behavior thermodynamic proofreading, and a three-process kinetic model shows that specificity arises not from initial binding discrimination but from cognate-driven correction at the product level. Coupled with signal-amplified antibody labeling, DEDBs enable quantitatively decoded nine-target intracellular protein imaging in fixed cells. The same barcode library supports Polychrome trajectory decoding for combinatorial identification and Monochrome cycle-resolved visualization for direct single-target inspection through reconfiguration of read-strand labeling. By generating combinatorial identities through the positional arrangement of reusable sequences within a single DNA strand, DEDBs reframe DNA barcode design from sequence enumeration to positional encoding.

title: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Despite highly efficacious antiretroviral therapy (ART), durable ART-free remission remains a central objective of HIV-1 cure strategies. The randomized, placebo-controlled RIO trial recently demonstrated that long-acting broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies (bNAbs) can sustain prolonged virologic control after ART interruption, including control that persisted beyond the period of therapeutically relevant antibody concentrations, providing clinical evidence consistent with host-mediated suppression. However, the mechanisms underlying these “vaccinal” effects remain unresolved. Here, we establish Fcγ receptor (FcγR) engagement as an essential driver of multiyear remission after bNAb therapy in simian-human immunodeficiency virus (SHIV)-infected macaques. Brief therapy during acute infection with Fc domain variants of the bNAb 3BNC117, matched for antigen binding, neutralizing activity, and pharmacokinetics but differing in FcγR engagement, produced comparable early virologic control yet profoundly divergent long-term outcomes. Sustained CD8 T cell–dependent suppression lasting nearly 300 wk developed in every evaluable animal receiving the FcγR-engaging variant but arose in only one of eight recipients of the FcγR-null variant. FcγR-driven immunomodulation imprinted a CD8 T cell response characterized by enhanced antigen-specific effector function, early clonal focusing with sustained clonotype persistence, and distinct cellular-state transcriptional signatures. Our findings identify the Fc–FcγR axis as a critical determinant of the reliable induction of durable remission and provide a mechanistic framework for developing Fc-engineered bNAbs designed to enhance vaccinal immunity and advance antibody-based strategies with the potential to achieve functional cure.

title: Neurovascular protein half-lives in health and aging
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Specializations of blood vasculature in the central nervous system (CNS), including the blood–brain barrier (BBB), neurovascular coupling, and perivascular spaces, maintain CNS homeostasis and become dysfunctional in disease and aging. Protein turnover, the process by which proteins are continually degraded and replaced, profoundly influences cell and tissue function and is dysregulated in aging and disease. Understanding the turnover of neurovascular proteins could provide insight into how the vasculature achieves both long-term structural stability and dynamic regulation. Vascular proteins, however, are underrepresented in previous studies of in vivo brain protein turnover. In this work, we used stable isotope labeling, nonenzymatic blood vessel enrichment, and high-resolution mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify the half-lives of brain vascular proteins in young adult and aged mice. We report half-life estimates for 1,358 proteins, including components of endothelial junctions, BBB transporters, astrocyte endfoot proteins, and vascular basement membrane proteins. We found that certain classes of proteins with related functions had similar half-lives, including BBB junctional proteins (~3 d), BBB transporters (~2 to 6 d), and most basement membrane components (>30 d). We also identified peptide motifs enriched in proteins with short and long half-lives and found differences in half-life distributions for cell type–specific proteomes. Finally, although we did not observe a global age-related shift in vascular protein turnover, we did identify specific proteins with increased or decreased half-lives in aging. This work establishes a high-quality database of neurovascular protein half-lives and provides a foundation for understanding how protein turnover contributes to neurovascular function and age-associated dysfunction.

title: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Maintaining optimized nutrient exchange between partnered species across changing environments presents a fundamental challenge for nutritional mutualisms. Yet quantitative approaches linking nutrient acquisition by one partner with the nutritional requirements of the other have been lacking. Here we extend the Nutritional Geometry Framework from organisms and colonies to interspecific mutualisms by linking realized nutritional niches (RNNs) with nutritional performance landscapes to quantify nutritional homeostasis between interacting species. Nutritional analyses of thousands of DNA-barcoded plant fragments collected by free-ranging Panamanian leafcutter ants revealed that RNNs for fungal cultivar provisioning diverged between degraded urban and intact rainforest habitats. Despite this, colonies converged on similar nutritional intake targets that were similarly positioned relative to regions of high fungal performance, while fungal nutritional yield remained stable across habitats. These findings demonstrate that correspondence between colony nutritional intake and fungal nutritional performance provides a quantitative means of assessing nutritional homeostasis across interacting species and establishes a foundation for comparative analyses of nutrient exchange across mutualisms experiencing environmental change.

title: SCN1B intron 3 retention results in a nonsense-mediated decay–sensitive mRNA linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Biallelic variants in the voltage-gated sodium channel (VGSC) gene
                    SCN1B
                    are linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy type 52 (DEE52).
                    SCN1B
                    encodes two isoforms: transmembrane β1, generated by all 6 coding exons, and β1B, generated by exons 1 to 3 followed by retention of intron 3 (
                    SCN1B
                    -IR). Transmembrane β1 subunits are multifunctional proteins that regulate sodium current and channel cell-surface expression, participate in cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion, and modulate transcription. Several DEE52 variants in the transmembrane β1 coding region have been shown to result in mixed loss-of-function. DEE52 variants are also identified in
                    SCN1B
                    -IR, yet their functional impacts remain unknown. Here, we provide evidence that
                    SCN1B
                    -IR is a cell type–specific, nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)–sensitive transcript. We investigate a severe biallelic DEE52 patient variant in intron 3,
                    SCN1B
                    c.449-2A>G, which results in expression of
                    SCN1B
                    -IR, but not transmembrane β1 transcripts. A transgenic mouse model that expresses
                    SCN1B
                    -IR, but not transmembrane β1, transcript phenocopies
                    Scn1b
                    null mice with seizures and early death. Thus,
                    SCN1B
                    -IR functions as an NMD-sensitive transcript that cannot compensate for the loss of transmembrane β1. We propose that future work may reveal
                    SCN1B
                    -IR to be a therapeutic target similar to other NMD-targeted transcripts.

title: Intrinsically disordered ligands for the control of receptor uptake by endocytosis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Endocytosis plays a crucial role in signaling, recycling, and degradation of receptors. Controlling endocytosis of specific receptors is therefore a major goal for both basic science and medicine. While antibody-induced dimerization can drive signaling-induced uptake of some receptors, the steric bulk of antibodies generally inhibits endocytosis, such that control over receptor uptake remains an unmet need. Recent work has demonstrated that attractive interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins drive inward membrane curvature, a key step in endocytosis. To harness this phenomenon for the control of receptor uptake, we designed chimeras that consisted of disordered domains fused to ligands for specific receptors. These chimeras condensed on membrane surfaces, in agreement with computational modeling, driving receptor clustering and uptake via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. In contrast, chimeras that repelled one another resisted condensation, helping receptors escape endocytosis and remain on the cell surface. Taken together, these results suggest that by modulating the amino acid sequence of intrinsically disordered ligands, we can promote or hinder the internalization of specific receptors by endocytic pathways. More broadly, these findings suggest a generalizable strategy for controlling the plasma membrane lifetime of diverse receptors, opening up new pathways for modulating cellular behavior and delivering therapeutics.

title: Intranasal delivery of a ROS-activatable myeloperoxidase inhibitor alleviates Alzheimer’s-like symptoms and pathology
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are important contributors to Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Myeloperoxidase (MPO), a key driver of oxidative inflammation released mainly by activated microglia in the neurodegenerative brain, is a potential therapeutic target to inhibit the neuroinflammatory cascade and oxidative damage in AD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unexplored, and achieving targeted brain delivery of an MPO inhibitor and minimizing systemic effects remain significant challenges. We addressed these limitations by first establishing that genetic deletion of MPO in the 5XFAD mouse model improved memory performance and reduced amyloid deposition, validating MPO as a therapeutic target. We then developed a liposome-encapsulated reactive oxygen species (ROS)-activatable MPO inhibitor (LERAMI). LERAMI uniquely combines targeted delivery with on-demand drug release, utilizing a ROS-sensitive linker to selectively release MPO inhibitors in ROS-rich regions within the AD microenvironment, minimizing off-target effects and systemic toxicity. In the 5XFAD mouse model. By reducing MPO expression and activity, LERAMI significantly improved cognitive performance, accompanied by decreased microglial activation, attenuated oxidative DNA damage, improved synaptic and neuronal density, and reduced amyloid burden. RNA sequencing revealed a robust hippocampal transcriptomic reprogramming, with upregulation of pathways critical for synaptic plasticity, calcium signaling, axon guidance, and neuroprotection, along with downregulation of inflammatory and immune response pathways. These findings demonstrate that targeted ROS-activatable MPO inhibition with LERAMI represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD and potentially other neuroinflammatory diseases, offering a unique approach to mitigate neuroinflammation, preserve synaptic integrity, and restore cognitive function.

title: Visualization of actin filaments in Plasmodium falciparum blood cell stages
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The actin cytoskeleton is crucial to regulate cellular processes and morphology in eukaryotes, yet the tools to visualize it are not compatible with all organisms. In the apicomplexan
                    Plasmodium falciparum
                    , actin filaments are thought to be short and unstable, complicating their visualization. Here, we show that a tandem fusion of the actin-chromobody can label filaments in all
                    P. falciparum
                    red blood cell stages and observe actin structures in live cells with high spatiotemporal resolution. This work suggests that previous lack of labeling was due to suboptimal probes and that malaria blood stages have a filamentous and highly dynamic actin network.

title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client–scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client–scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client–scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue–resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.
