title: Structural insights into inhibition and activation mechanisms of plant calcium-dependent protein kinases
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) comprise the major group of Ca
                    2+
                    -regulated kinases in plants and protists. These enzymes comprise an N-terminal kinase domain and a C-terminal Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent activation domain (CAD). We solved the crystal structures of autoinhibited and activated forms of a plant CDPK,
                    Arabidopsis
                    CPK3. In the autoinhibited form, the CAD resembles a “dumbbell-like” calmodulin protein with a long helix in the N terminus that inhibits the kinase domain in a pseudo-substrate manner. Upon Ca
                    2+
                    binding to the four EF-hands, CAD undergoes a dramatic conformational change with a rotation around the kinase domain, thus exposing its active site for substrate recognition. Our structural and biochemical studies reveal that most plant CDPKs may involve distinct mechanisms of activation compared with CDPKs from the apicomplexan parasites.

title: Multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived biomimetic vesicles for cancer multimodal targeting and immune reprogramming
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Despite advances of biomimetic vesicles in cancer therapy, clinical challenges such as biosafety, scalability, and therapeutic efficacy remain significant hurdles. To address these limitations, we reveal the critical tumor-homing motifs of cancer cell membrane vesicles: a synergistic “chemotactic recruitment-adhesion anchoring” cascade effect, especially chemokine axes (e.g., CXCL12/CXCR4) and integrins (e.g., αVβ3). In this study, we identify autologous fibroblasts as an ideal “chassis” cell for engineering biomimetic carriers. Using this platform, we construct multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived nanovesicles (X-Fb-MNVs) coexpressing critical chemokine receptor CXCR4 and adhesion ligand iRGD, as well as PD-1 and CD47 protein, which achieved robust and broad-spectrum tumor targeting across breast, liver, pancreatic, and colon cancer PDX models. Significantly, CD47-modified X-Fb-MNVs reduced hepatic accumulation and phagocytic clearance, thereby minimizing off-target effects in vivo and improving tumor targeting efficiency. By loading diABZI STING agonist into X-Fb-MNVs with overexpressed PD-1, our system activates both T cell and innate immunity, reversing ICB resistance and achieving 83.3% survival with no tumor recurrence and long-term immune surveillance over 90 d, whereas no mice survived with free diABZI treatment. By merging multimodal targeting, immune reprogramming, and scalable production into a single platform, X-Fb-MNVs represent a remarkable biomimetic system with transformative potential for a wide-spectrum cancer immunotherapy.

title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman’s lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing “estrogen protection hypothesis,” which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield inconsistent results. Our results establish that perimenopause is a mechanistically distinct neurobiological window characterized by a unique failure of hippocampal-dopamine circuit regulation. By identifying this specific period of circuit instability, this work provides a framework for stage-specific psychiatric interventions and reframes reproductive aging as a series of distinct transitions in brain function.

title: Competitive disruption of COI1 receptor assembly by a hemibiotrophic bacterial effector suppresses jasmonate-mediated immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Hormone pathways are central hubs in plant immunity, and their receptors, the critical initiators of signaling cascades, are logical targets of pathogen effectors. The jasmonic acid (JA) pathway is a cornerstone of defense against phytopathogens, especially necrotrophs. However, whether pathogens can directly target its receptor COI1 to subvert this defense layer has remained unclear. Here, we show that JA signaling positively regulates resistance to the devastating hemibiotrophic pathogen
                    Ralstonia solanacearum
                    and identified a bacterial effector, RipBO, that directly targets COI1 to counteract this defense. RipBO binds with high affinity to the F-box domain of COI1, competitively disrupts the COI1-ASK interaction, and thereby blocks SCF
                    COI1
                    complex assembly. This disruption effectively stabilizes JAZ repressors and paralyzes JA-mediated immunity. Our findings clarify the contribution of JA signaling to bacterial wilt resistance and identify direct targeting of the hormone receptor as a pathogen virulence strategy, pointing to a potential vulnerability for crop protection.

title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype–phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype–phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar “frequency matching” results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the “replicated genotype–phenotype map” for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for mutational robustness. Last, our theory suggests a possible mathematical definition for evolvability with predictive power that can be tested in evolutionary simulations and, ultimately, in comparative genetics studies.

title: Endosomal mRNA transport coordinates local mitochondrial bioenergetics during polar fungal growth
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Mitochondrial function relies on the precise spatial coordination of protein synthesis and import. Most mitochondrial proteins are nuclear-encoded and must be supplied across varying intracellular distances. In highly polarized cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, active long-distance mRNA transport is thought to sustain distal mitochondrial function, but its mechanistic coupling to protein import and organelle physiology is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that endosomal transport of mRNAs encoding mitochondrial proteins orchestrates local bioenergetics in infectious hyphae of
                    Ustilago maydis
                    . Using the subunit Atp3 of electron transport chain Complex V as a model, we uncover that the endosomal mRNA transporter Rrm4 is required for efficient mitochondrial protein import, particularly at growth poles. Loss of Rrm4 leads to defects in mitochondrial import, resulting in altered physiology. We propose that endosome-coupled mRNA transport constitutes a fundamental layer of subcellular mitochondrial homeostasis, with implications extending from fungal pathogenicity to neuronal disease.

title: The sound of persuasion: Using generative AI to identify gender gaps in political influence
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women’s behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread pattern, the mechanisms behind the gender gap in persuasion are difficult to isolate and test in dynamic political conversations. Women may be less persuasive simply because role-based expectations prompt others to afford women less authority when speaking about politics generally or about some political topics. Alternatively, women may be less persuasive because they tend to use linguistic patterns or rhetorical strategies that are less effective. Using an original AI-based approach, we put 4,300 human subjects into realistic, real-time phone conversations with an AI agent. These agents were randomly assigned either a masculine or feminine gendered conversation topic and a male- or female-sounding voice, allowing us to manipulate topic and perceptions of speakers’ gender while holding constant other elements of rhetorical content and strategy. After validating the experimental treatments, we find no direct effects of perceived gender of the AI agent, as cued by voice. However, gender affects other important aspects of the persuasive interaction. Research subjects were more likely to be persuaded about the masculine topic (defense spending) than the feminine topic (aid to the poor). Additionally, women research subjects were, on average, more persuaded than men. To the extent that men and women emphasize different topics in political conversations and have different discussion partners, these dynamics are likely to shape women’s political persuasive influence.

title: Activation of ROPGEFs by a malectin-like receptor kinase is involved in tip growth regulation in Physcomitrium patens
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Rho-type GTPases of plants (ROPs) play essential roles in polarized cell growth, cell division, and organogenesis. Their activation depends on two types of guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs): the plant-specific PRONE-domain-containing ROPGEFs and DOCK-type SPKGEFs. While ROPGEFs have been proposed to be autoinhibited in pollen and activated by receptor-like kinases (RLKs), the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using the moss
                    Physcomitrium patens
                    , we show that moss ROPGEF4 and ROPGEF6 exhibit low intrinsic GEF activity and are not autoinhibited by non-PRONE regions, whereas the catalytic domain of SPK1 and SPK6 is highly active. Through a candidate screen, we identified MLRK1, a malectin-like receptor kinase, as a ROPGEF-interacting protein. MLRK1 directly phosphorylates ROPGEF4 and ROPGEF6 and stimulates their GEF activities in vitro. These effects are attenuated by substituting key phosphosites (Ser231 in ROPGEF4 and Ser524/Thr526 in ROPGEF6) with nonphosphorylatable residues. Structural modeling, pull-down assays, and functional analyses indicate that phosphorylation enhances ROPGEF-ROP interactions and promotes the membrane localization of ROPGEF4/6. Furthermore, ROPGEFs are not essential for polarized cell growth on their own but act redundantly with SPK2. At the apical membrane, ROPGEFs appear to activate ROPs, reduce their diffusion, promote actin filament assembly and vesicle secretion, and ultimately facilitate cell expansion and growth. Collectively, our findings provide functional evidence that RLK-ROPGEF-ROP signaling module has emerged in early land plants and is involved in cell growth regulation.

title: Single-molecule FRET at 30: Toward conformational sequencing
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Single-molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer (smFRET) turned 30 this year. We argue that three advances usually treated as separate endeavors, i.e., high-information-content per-molecule readout, sequence-linked massive parallelism, and automated trajectory decoding, are in fact one convergence that is turning smFRET from a one-molecule-at-a-time measurement into a high-throughput conformational sequencer, a platform that measures dynamic conformational phenotypes across sequence space at scale. This perspective traces the 30-y arc, forecasts which advances will prove most transformative over the next decade, states the conditions on which that forecast depends, and identifies the bottlenecks that still remain.

title: Acetate–FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are required for the protective effects of acetate, which are also dependent on FFAR2 signaling and IL-22. Neutrophil-specific deletion of FFAR2 impairs IL-22 responses, increases epithelial damage, and exacerbates colitis, while administration of recombinant IL-22 is sufficient to restore acetate protection in this context. Analysis of human ulcerative colitis biopsies reveals increased FFAR2
                    +
                    neutrophils correlating with IL-22-related gene signatures. These findings indicate that acetate–FFAR2–neutrophil–IL-22 axis modulates intestinal inflammation, revealing a metabolic mechanism that links microbiota-derived signals to mucosal protection and highlighting potential therapeutic targets for inflammatory bowel diseases.

title: Anomeric configuration encodes mesophase preference of glucosylceramides in phospholipid membranes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Glycosphingolipids are key components of the cell glycocalyx, yet the extent to which their anomeric configuration affects their membrane organization remains unclear. Glucosylceramide (GlcCer) exists as α- and β-anomers with distinct biological activities, while the biophysical basis for these differences is unknown. Here, using nitroxide spin-labeled analogs of α- and β-GlcCer, we examined how the glycosidic stereochemistry affects their partitioning in phospholipid bilayers. In 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine, dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine, and distearoylphosphatidylcholine liposomes, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra of both probes contained two components: a broad, motion-restricted component consistent with GlcCer incorporated into the lamellar lipid bilayer and a sharp, highly mobile component attributed to some segregated, bilayer-associated GlcCer-rich nano-assemblies. EPR spectral simulations and complementary analyses showed that α-GlcCer predominantly partitioned into the lamellar phospholipid phase, whereas β-GlcCer was strongly enriched in the segregated GlcCer-rich phase. Importantly, analogous anomer-dependent EPR behavior was also observed for aqueous GlcCer dispersions in the absence of phospholipids, indicating that the distinct assembly propensities are intrinsic to the glycolipids and are modulated, rather than created, by the phospholipids. These findings support a two-mesophase model in which anomeric configuration acts as a stereochemical switch that biases GlcCer between phospholipid lamellae and segregated glycolipid nano-assemblies. Notably, such anomer-dependent behaviors were observed at a probe loading of only 0.5 mol%. Thus, even at rather low abundance, a subtle stereochemical difference in GlcCer can substantially alter its compatibility with a phospholipid membrane matrix, providing a plausible physical basis for anomer-dependent glycolipid sorting, signaling, and disease-associated membrane organization.

title: Unconventional modulation of Nav1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Voltage-gated sodium (Na
                    v
                    ) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Na
                    v
                    channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from
                    Lychas mucronatus
                    . LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Na
                    v
                    1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNa
                    v
                    1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSD
                    II
                    ) and the extracellular loop III (ECL
                    III
                    ) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3–S4
                    II
                    loop and displaces S0/S3
                    II
                    helices to trap VSD
                    II
                    within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSD
                    II
                    conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSD
                    II
                    trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECL
                    III
                    engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECL
                    III
                    region underlie the prominent species- and isoform-dependent activities of the toxin toward insect and mammalian Na
                    v
                    channels. Our study provides a structural basis for the dual-action mechanisms of β-scorpion toxins on Na
                    v
                    channels and presents a structural framework for understanding toxin binding, channel gating modulation, ecological adaptation, and rational drug design.

title: Diffusive and advective transport in structurally anisotropic fibrous hydrogels
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Changes in fiber orientation in structurally anisotropic fibrous extracellular matrices govern transport, distribution, and accumulation of biologically active molecules and therapeutic nanoparticles in tissues. Fundamental studies of advection-driven transport in such matrices are challenging because changes in network anisotropy are generally coupled with variation in fiber dimensions, density, and surface chemistry. Here, a fibrous hydrogel was engineered in which the type and degree of fiber orientation were decoupled from these structural characteristics. Advection of charge-neutral nanoparticle probes under physiologically relevant pressure gradients was studied in a channel geometry that imposed spatially nonuniform flow across the fibrous network. The probe advection was quantified by the time of probe permeation through the gel along the fastest flow path and the time of probe distribution within the gel. We show that the permeation timescale was governed by advection along the pressure gradient, whereas the distribution timescale transitioned between advection- and diffusion-limited behavior depending on fiber orientation and probe dimension. The decoupling between these timescales became more pronounced with stronger alignment along the pressure gradient and with increasing probe dimension. Scaling analysis and a fluid dynamics simulation model further provided mechanistic insight into these experimental findings. Together, these results identify the key structural factors governing advection in anisotropic fibrous networks and provide a platform for future studies of the role of fiber orientation in tissues in regulating the transport, distribution, and dissemination of biologically active molecules, exosomes, and nanoparticle therapeutics under interstitial fluid flow.

title: Resilient j = 3/2 superconductivity in topological semimetal YPtBi
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cooper pairing in most of the known fermionic superfluids occurs via spin-1/2 quasiparticle interactions that lead to spin-singlet or spin-triplet pairing. In the topological semimetal YPtBi, strong spin–orbit coupling results in a band inversion between highly symmetric
                    s
                    - and
                    p
                    -like electronic bands and a degeneracy at the Γ point that ensures the manifold of
                    j
                    = 3/2 quasiparticle states thrive near the Fermi level, where superconducting pairing occurs. Here we study the effects of magnetic and nonmagnetic disorder and carrier density on this exotic superconducting pairing state. By varying levels of disorder and carrier densities by nearly two and three orders of magnitude, respectively, we show that the superconducting critical temperature of YPtBi has a remarkable robustness, with little variation across this span. Our results suggest that superconductivity in YPtBi may reside in a regime where phase stiffness, rather than pair formation, governs the transition temperature. The insensitivity of Cooper pairing to dramatic changes in quasiparticle environment in a
                    j
                    = 3/2 superconductor highlights a form of protection realized in topological high-spin superconductors.

title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mass cytometry (MC) enables highly multiplexed single‐cell protein analysis, but its full analytical potential remains constrained by the limited range of available mass tags. Here, we report deferoxamine‐engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DFO‐MSNs) for high‐capacity loading of multiple underutilized high‐valent metal ions within a common nanoparticle scaffold. DFO‐MSNs accommodated Zr 4+ , Hf 4+ , Nb 5+ , and Ta 5+ at approximately 10 4 metal atoms per nanoparticle, with high metal retention in physiological buffers. Following PEGylation and antibody (Ab) conjugation, the resulting Zr‐, Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐based probes enabled antigen‐specific detection of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by co‐staining with commercial Maxpar reagents. Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐loaded MSN_CD8a probes resolved CD8a+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes at titers as low as 30 NPs/cell. In a 30‐plex staining panel, Ta@MSN_CD25 resolved low‐abundance CD25 hi CD127 lo T reg ‐like cells with apparent population recovery comparable to the corresponding Maxpar reagent, while consuming ca. 35‐fold less Ab. Together, these results establish a modular strategy for incorporating underutilized high‐valent metals into functional mass tags and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating MSN‐based probes into multiplexed MC immunophenotyping workflows.

title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C19, C24, and C29 Terpenoids
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The terpenoid substrate analog 14‐ nor ‐farnesyl pyrophosphate (14‐ nor ‐FPP), lacking the methyl group Me14, was synthesized and enzymatically elongated to 18‐ nor ‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (18‐ nor ‐GGPP) and 22‐ nor ‐geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (22‐ nor ‐GFPP) by GGPP synthase (GGPPS) and GFPP synthase (GFPPS), respectively. Downstream conversion with 20 diterpene synthases (DTSs) and 10 sesterterpene synthases (StTSs) yielded in total 24 new compounds. Surprisingly, in two cases the substrate analogs were converted by GGPPS and a DTS into nor ‐sesterterpenes (C 24 ), while one combination of GFPPS and a StTS yielded a nor ‐triterpene (C 29 ), demonstrating that the lack of just one carbon allows for extension with one more terpene unit than expected, in contrast to the strict product selectivity observed for GGPPS and GFPPS with normal FPP. For certain enzyme‐substrate pairings, the altered reactivity caused by the absence of Me14 unveiled reaction pathways toward di‐ and sesterterpenes with unique frameworks, for which the mechanisms were investigated through DFT calculations. Absolute configurations of the obtained compounds were determined through chemical correlation with stereoselectively deuterated precursors or through a comparison of optical rotations to those of structurally related natural products containing Me18/Me22.

title: Photocatalytic Biomass Valorization: Electronic Polarization Enables Oxygen Activation and Selective C─C Bond Cleavage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic valorization of biomass into value‐added chemicals requires catalysts capable of simultaneously activating molecular oxygen and controlling C─C bond cleavage. In this work, we introduce an electronic polarization engineering strategy by integrating CF 3 ‐induced charge redistribution on Co active‐site regulation in polymeric carbon nitride. It demonstrates that the as‐prepared Co/g‐C 3 N 4 ‐CF 3 photocatalyst enables selective conversion of biomass‐derived carbohydrates into formic acid under visible‐light irradiation and mild aqueous conditions. Mechanistic investigations reveal that ─CF 3 functionalization creates localized electronic polarization, while Co sites promote oxygen activation and facilitate the formation of superoxide radicals (•O 2 − ). Density functional theory calculations reveals that this electronic modulation lowers the energetic barrier for the key C─C bond cleavage step. Therefore, this work establishes a general framework for coupling electronic polarization with active‐site engineering to help perform selective oxidation chemistry in solar‐driven catalysis.

title: Synergistic Bimolecular Reconstruction of the Perovskite‐Carbon Interface Enables 23.6%‐Efficiency Fully Printable Mesoscopic Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole‐conductor‐free, fully printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (p‐MPSCs) hold compelling promise for photovoltaic industrialization. However, their power conversion efficiency (PCE) remains constrained by limited hole collection at the perovskite‐carbon interface. Here, we introduce a synergistic bimolecular post‐treatment using toluene diisocyanate (TDI) and 4‐methyl sulfonyl phenyl methylammonium chloride (MSBH) to reconstruct this critical interface. We demonstrate that TDI reacts with surface formamidinium to polish and activate the perovskite terminations, while MSBH subsequently grafts onto this activated surface. This combined action simultaneously reconstructs the interface with optimized surface energy band bending and minimized interfacial defects, thereby facilitating hole extraction and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, this strategy elevates the PCE of small‐area p‐MPSCs (0.1 cm 2 ) to 23.6%. Furthermore, it enables the fabrication of a p‐MPSC minimodule with an active area of 52.7 cm 2 , achieving a PCE of 22.1%, among the highest values ever reported for carbon‐based, fully printable architectures. Devices retained 98% of their initial PCE after 750 h of operational stability testing at 55°C ± 5°C. This work provides an effective interface reconstruction strategy that concurrently addresses defect passivation and energy alignment, paving the way for high‐performance, stable, and scalable cost‐effective perovskite photovoltaics.

title: High‐Density Colossal Barocaloric Effect in Quasi‐Spherical Ionic Plastic Crystal (Et4N)(CrO3Cl)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The barocaloric effect driven by hydrostatic pressure of solid‐state phase transition materials is regarded as one of the means to replace traditional vapor compression refrigeration technology due to its environmental friendliness and high efficiency. However, the refrigeration density of the currently reported solid‐state barocaloric refrigerants is generally low, which is not conducive to the low cost and miniaturization of refrigeration equipment. In order to solve this problem, we explore the barocaloric effect of ionic plastic crystal (Et 4 N)(CrO 3 Cl), which shows a high refrigeration density due to weak hydrogen bond interaction, quasi‐spherical structure, and large volume change during the first‐order phase transition. Under a driving pressure of 100 MPa, the reversible isothermal entropy changes (Δ S it, rev ) per unit mass and per unit volume are 284.1 J kg −1 K −1 and 0.397 J cm −3 K −1 , respectively. Regardless of the evaluation from any perspective, this refrigerant shows a high refrigeration density. In addition, (Et 4 N)(CrO 3 Cl) shows relatively high‐pressure sensitivity (). This also enables it to exhibit excellent refrigeration capacity (RC = 3636 J kg −1 = 5.08 J cm −3 ) at a relatively low pressure (100 MPa). The discovery of this high‐density barocaloric refrigerant will help to promote the research on the miniaturization of refrigeration equipment.

title: Sequential Regulation of Dendrite Initiation and Propagation for High‐Current Hydroborate‐Based Solid‐State Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydroborate solid electrolytes (SEs) offer fast Na + transport, low density, and compatibility with Na metal, yet their current tolerance is restricted by dendrite‐induced short circuits in all‐solid‐state Na metal batteries (ASSNBs). Here, a spatially coordinated dual‐interlayer architecture is developed to regulate dendrite initiation and propagation in Na 4 B 10 H 10 B 12 H 12 (NBH)‐based ASSNBs. At the Na|NBH interface, a three‐dimensional Sn/C framework enables Na infiltration into the porous scaffold and homogenizes current distribution, while dynamically formed Na–Sn sites facilitate Na + transport and redistribution, thereby maintaining intimate interfacial contact and suppressing dendrite initiation. Within the NBH SE, a Na 2.9375 PS 3.9375 Cl 0.0625 (NPSC) sulfide interlayer reacts with penetrating Na to suppress dendrite propagation, with crack‐like pathways terminating near the NBH|NPSC interface. This sequential regulation increases the critical current density from 0.5 to 3.3 mA cm −2 . Symmetric cells operate stably for 7000 and 1000 h at 0.5 and 3.0 mA cm −2 , respectively. Full cells with an O3‐type NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 cathode retain 75% capacity after 800 cycles at 2 C, while supporting cathode loadings up to 15 mg cm −2 . This work establishes sequential control of dendrite initiation and propagation as a design principle for high‐current hydroborate‐based ASSNBs.

title: Flexible 2D Donor‐Acceptor MOFs Enable Tunable and Pressure‐Responsive TSCT–TADF for Heterocrystal Photonic Logic
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials that combine high efficiency, color tunability, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness are highly desirable for adaptive photonic technologies, yet remain difficult to realize within a single crystalline platform. Here, flexible two‐dimensional (2D) donor‐acceptor (D–A) metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are developed through integrating an aggregation‐induced‐emission‐active triphenylamine donor with size‐matched electron‐deficient acceptors. Solvent‐directed assembly, donor conformational flexibility, and acceptor electronic modulation cooperatively regulate the D–A packing and through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) effect. The resulting MOFs exhibit broadly tunable TADF emission (474–635 nm), delayed lifetimes (0.11–7.65 µs), and photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY, 0.52%–74.24%). Relative to the DMF‐derived structures, the DMA‐derived MOFs display increases of up to 51‐fold in delayed lifetime and 6‐fold in PLQY, while calculations support an unconventional high‐lying reverse intersystem crossing (hRISC) pathway. More importantly, the structural adaptability of the layered frameworks enables pressure‐induced reconfiguration of D–A interactions, giving rise to reversible piezochromic TSCT–TADF with emission shifts of up to 113 nm. A multicomponent heterocrystal is further constructed to translate pressure‐dependent emission changes into optical logic operations. These results establish flexible 2D D–A MOFs as a dynamic platform for integrating efficient TADF, mechanical responsiveness, and heterocrystal photonic functionality.

title: Reconceptualizing Thermal Runaway Mechanisms in Sulfide Solid‐State Batteries via Dynamic Interfacial Reconstruction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The commercialization of sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) is often predicated on their perceived “intrinsic safety”. However, recent evidence of violent thermal runaway under abuse conditions has shattered this consensus, revealing a sobering gap in our mechanistic understanding of solid‐state failure. In this Perspective, we argue that the current stagnation in safety research stems from a “liquid‐legacy” mindset that fails to account for the unique solid–solid reactive landscape. We propose that the thermal failure of sulfide ASSBs is fundamentally governed by a dynamic interfacial reconstruction involving the continuous electrochemical and chemo‐mechanical evolution of the interphase during cycling. By deconstructing the staged thermochemical cascade, we demonstrate how cycling‐induced metastable species, such as polysulfides and mixed‐conducting interphases, act as reactive “pre‐conditioners” that dictate failure pathways. This framework explains long‐standing experimental inconsistencies, including divergent SO 2 evolution profiles and fluctuating trigger temperatures across identical material couples. This shift from a static material‐centric view to a dynamic interface‐centric framework reframes the rational design of truly robust, next‐generation energy storage systems.

title: Interfacial Electronic Reconstruction Activates TiO2 in MnO2/TiO2 Heterostructures for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Chemistry
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics originating from insufficient regulation of interfacial electronic structures. Here, we report a MnO 2 /TiO 2 heterostructure with integrated interfacial bonding, in which residual carbon is inherently incorporated into the interfacial region. The characterizations reveal pronounced reconstruction of the local coordination and electronic environment upon heterostructure formation, including Ti─O─Mn bonding, reduced Ti states, and substantial changes in the surface potential and valence‐band structure. DFT calculations suggest that the reconstructed interface involves the coexistence of net intercomponent charge redistribution and localized bond polarization, with residual carbon contributing to interfacial electronic coupling. Consistent with this reconstructed electronic environment, Ti‐derived sites exhibit enhanced electronic response toward polysulfides, while MnO 2 and residual carbon contribute to the coupled interfacial structure. Consequently, MnO 2 /TiO 2 catalyst enables stable cycling under a high sulfur loading of 9.2 mg cm −2 and, when integrated as a functional interlayer, allows the sulfur cathode to deliver a high specific capacity of 1569 mAh g −1 together with durability over 1000 cycles, with a capacity decay rate of 0.054% per cycle. This work highlights chemically integrated oxide heterointerfaces as an effective platform for regulating local electronic structures and accelerating sulfur redox chemistry.

title: Spatiotemporally Controlled Lithium Delivery via a Graphene‐Hydrogel System for Wnt Activation and Spinal Cord Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Wnt signaling plays essential roles in neural development and has significant potential to promote regeneration after central nervous system (CNS) injury. However, therapeutic strategies that locally modulate Wnt signaling in vivo remain limited. Herein, we develop a battery‐inspired graphene‐lithium hydrogel (GLH) that enables sustained, controllable delivery of lithium ions (Li + ) to injury sites. Li + inhibits glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK3β), activating pro‐regenerative Wnt/β‐catenin signaling. Beyond Wnt activation, GLH provides complementary therapeutic functions: oxidation of lithium (0) attenuates reactive oxygen species‐associated stress, while the gelatin‐based hydrogel matrix supplies a permissive extracellular matrix (ECM)‐like niche. In co‐cultures of human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived neural progenitor cells and macrophages, GLH suppresses pro‐inflammatory signaling and enhances neurogenesis. In a murine spinal cord injury complete transection model, a single GLH injection sustains Wnt activation for over one week, reduces acute neuroinflammation and astroglial/fibrotic scarring, and promotes long‐term tissue preservation and functional recovery. Transcriptomic and protein analyses further support coordinated modulation of Wnt‐related, redox, inflammatory, and ECM‐remodeling pathways, accompanying improved locomotor and bladder function and reduced neuropathic pain. Given the conserved role of Wnt signaling in regeneration, the GLH offers a multifunctional materials platform with potential applicability beyond the CNS.

title: Topological‐Insulator‐Based Ion‐Electron‐Coupled Nanochannels With a Photothermally Induced Thermoelectric Field for Enhanced Ionic Transport
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient ion transport is essential for high‐performance energy storage and conversion, yet strong ion–channel interactions in conventional highly polar nanochannels can increase migration barriers and impede rapid ion motion. Here, we report layered ion‐electron‐coupled Bi 2 Te 3 /Ti 3 C 2 T x nanochannels, in which ion transport is synergistically regulated by highly polar interfaces, highly conductive surface states, and a photothermally induced thermoelectric field. The polar MXene interfaces support selective ion transport, whereas the highly conductive surface states of Bi 2 Te 3 enhance interfacial electronic responsiveness, facilitating charge equilibration and mitigating local charge accumulation during ion migration. This interfacial coupling reduces the ion‐transport activation energy to 8.02 kJ mol −1 , 34.6% lower than that of pristine MXene nanochannels. As a functional demonstration of enhanced ion transport, the nanochannels deliver a 5.56‐fold increase in osmotic power density (18.9 W m −2 ) under a 50‐fold NaCl concentration gradient. Upon illumination, the photothermally induced temperature gradient activates the Seebeck response of Bi 2 Te 3 , providing an additional thermoelectric driving force for directional ion migration, as reflected by a further increase in power density to 25.5 W m −2 . This work provides a strategy for enhancing ion transport under nanoconfinement through interfacial‐electronic‐coupling‐mediated regulation and thermoelectric‐field‐assisted driving.

title: Halide Perovskite Heterojunction Crossbar Arrays for Selector‐Free Analog In‐Memory Computing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Passive memristor crossbars require each cell to suppress sneak‐path currents while retaining gradual, reproducible conductance programmability. In halide perovskites, however, sneak‐current suppression and analog programmability have rarely been integrated and validated across passive arrays. Fabricated arrays have typically relied on peripheral circuitry to mitigate parasitic currents, whereas self‐rectifying analog memristors have largely remained at the single‐device level. Here, a discrete three‐dimensional/two‐dimensional (3D/2D) FAPbI 3 /BDAPbI 4 heterojunction, formed through controlled in situ conversion, is shown to integrate diode‐like rectification and analog resistive switching within a single, nominally symmetric Au/perovskite/Au cell. The 3D perovskite enables field‐assisted ion migration, while the 2D perovskite introduces an interfacial barrier that induces asymmetric transport, resulting in intrinsic rectification and stable analog switching. A 32 × 32 passive crossbar array comprising 1024 cells, fabricated on silicon below 150°C, exhibits a 99.4% functional‐device yield, a synaptic nonlinearity of 0.007, and stable operation over 640 000 programming pulses. Cell‐resolved measurements demonstrate analog image programming and erasing, and a tiled‐array inference model incorporating the measured cell characteristics and electrical nonidealities connects the experimentally realized array to in‐memory‐computing performance. These results establish chemically defined perovskite heterojunctions as a low‐temperature, silicon‐compatible materials strategy for selector‐free analog in‐memory computing.

title: Ultrarobust and Thermo‐Mechano‐Photo‐Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust elastomers are being widely used in multi‐stimuli‐responsive systems including closed‐loop recycling, information encryption, and advanced photolithography. However, their advancement is hindered by an inherent trade‐off: structural integrity for mechanical robustness versus molecular‐level reversibility for stimuli responsiveness. In this study, we constructed ultrarobust recyclable and photo‐responsive supramolecular‐dynamic covalent networks (SDCN) based on molecular engineering of anthracene‐functionalized poly(urethane‐urea‐amide) (PUUA) networks with hindered urea motifs. Well‐designed SDCN achieves multiscale assembly through coordinated π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and dynamic covalent interactions, creating dynamic coupling between soft‐chain crosslinks and self‐assembly hard domains, and driving microphase separation. Under stretching, strain‐activated disassembly of dynamically assembled nanostructures synergizes with stress‐induced crystallization, in situ evolving three‐dimensional topological architectures and promoting strength‐toughness enhancement. Consequently, PUUA elastomers exhibit remarkable mechanical performance (100.17 MPa tensile strength, 1286.79% elongation and 498.15 MJ m −3 toughness at room temperature; 113.67 MPa strength and 667.8% elongation at −40°C) and recycling performance (92.4% recyclability via solvent reprocessing). Significantly, UV‐responsive anthracene photonic moieties combined with temperature‐mediated interfacial SDCN transition enable fluorescent encryption and sub‐micron photolithographic patterning. Therefore, this work coordinates dynamic thermal‐mechanical‐optical responses and multi‐scale molecular transition mechanisms, which can be expected to boost high‐precision photolithographic patterning and flexible microcircuit printing fields.

title: 3D‐Printable Bioinspired Heterostructured Polymer With Exceptional Toughness and Fatigue Resistance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric materials are widely used in load‐bearing biomedical applications, yet achieving concurrent high fracture toughness and fatigue resistance remains a longstanding challenge due to their intrinsic trade‐off. Here, we propose a bioinspired heterostructure (BIHS) fatigue‐resistant strategy inspired by the material‐structure synergy of natural intervertebral discs (IVDs). The optimized BIHS composite achieves a fracture toughness of 1252 ± 70.13 kJ/m 2 and a fatigue threshold of 8010 J/m 2 , outperforming conventional polymer materials. The BIHS enables stress redistribution at crack tips and activates multiple energy‐dissipation pathways, including crack bridging and deflection, fiber pull‐out and rupture, and interfacial interactions, thereby suppressing crack initiation and propagation under cyclic loading. Leveraging this design, we further develop a BIHS‐IVD that withstands 1.5 × 10 7 cycles without failure under physiological loading in saline conditions, corresponding to an estimated 45‐year cycle‐equivalent fatigue life. These results establish a generalizable bioinspired design framework for durable polymeric materials and provide a promising pathway toward long‐lasting biomedical implants.

title: Orthogonal Self‐Assembled Two‐Dimensional Charge‐Transfer Cocrystals With Superior Photothermal Stability for Low‐Loss NIR‐II Waveguiding and Epitaxial Heterostructure Fabrication
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐dimensional organic near‐infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two‐dimensional (2D) structural growth and low‐loss waveguiding within the NIR‐II region remains a formidable challenge due to one‐dimensional (1D) packing tendencies imposed by strong charge transfer (CT) interactions. In this study, we strategically choose the extended π‐conjugated structure donor dithieno[2,3‐d:2',3'‐d']benzo[1,2‐b:4,5‐b']dithiophene and the strong electron‐withdrawing acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, and report the first large‐scale preparation of 2D organic CT cocrystal microsheets with NIR‐II emission at 1050 nm via a gas‐phase self‐assembly. The strategically expanded conjugation framework not only further promotes the luminescence red‐shift but also introduces an interaction network with orthogonal directions, counterbalancing the intrinsic 1D stacking constraints brought by the strong CT interactions and guiding the crystals into a thermodynamically stable 2D morphology. The compact network plays a crucial role in endowing the material with exceptional structural and photothermal stability, as well as low‐loss optical waveguiding. Furthermore, attributed to the extremely low lattice‐mismatch rate, 1D‐2D branched heterostructures were constructed, which demonstrated efficient energy transfer (ET) and cross‐band optical signal conversion over 600 nm. This work breaks new ground in extending 2D organic cocrystals into the NIR‐II region and provides a promising material platform for low‐loss, and integrated NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: π‑Conjugated Helical Polymer for Circularly Polarized Photodetection and Secure Optoelectronic Encoding
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical polymers are promising materials for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection and hardware‐level information security owing to their tunable chiroptical properties, efficient charge transport, and intrinsic conformational randomness. However, designing helical polymers with high chiroptical activity, which can be effectively translated intohigh‐performance CPL detection remains challenging. Herein, we reported the helical polymer, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T, in which point chirality was effectively transferred to π‐extended diperylene diimide (diPDI) backbone. Compared with non‐helical polymer ( SS )‐PDI‐C8‐T‐T, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T exhibited chiroptical activity (the absorption dissymmetry factors, g abs = −1.4 × 10 −3 at 460 nm) in chloroform (10 −5 M), owing to the optimized electric–magnetic ( µ ‐ m ) transition dipole alignment. CPL detectors based on ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films exhibited higher average photocurrent dissymmetry factors ( g ph ) of 0.52 at 535 nm and −1.03 at 405 nm, the latter of which is the highest g ph reported for single‐component chiral polymer‐based CPL detection. The enhanced chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect increased the spin polarization to 89.03%, contributing to the higher g ph for ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films. Leveraging the dual‐wavelength CPL response of ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films and spatial randomness, 5 × 8 CPL‐PUF array enabled optoelectronic fingerprinting, with inter‐ and intra‐Hamming distances of 49.278% and 1.655%, respectively. This work highlights helical polymers for CPL detection and chiral optoelectronic fingerprinting.

title: An Implantable In‐Tube System for Quantitative Precision Vagus Neuromodulation and Feedback of Intestinal Motility
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrical vagus neuromodulation of intestinal motility has demonstrated significant clinical utility in the field, where targeting the brain–gut axis can serve as an adjunct in treating intestinal diseases. However, quantitatively understanding vagus‐intestine interoceptive information about real‐time and in situ feedback on intestinal motility under the influence of electrical stimulation parameters is one of the most urgent challenges. Here we propose an implantable closed‐loop system that combines a scalable catheter‐type ionic piezoelectric (in‐tube) sensor as diverse as the gut, a microelectronic chip, an electrical vagus stimulation electrode, and a display interface to realize point‐of‐care precision vagus neuromodulation and feedback of intestinal motility. Owing to the radial gradient hydrogel structure design and stress concentration effect, the in‐tube sensor can simultaneously quantitatively detect and display four key parameters of intestinal motility, including intensity, frequency, duration, and local compression rate, with a high sensitivity of 7.0 mV mmHg −1 and unique pressure–time integral behavior with a time sensitivity of 24.1 mV s −1 , making up for the deficiency of traditional sensors that cannot obtain pressure duration. After implanting the in‐tube sensor in the anatomically challenging intestinal lumen of rabbits, we intuitively show how electrical vagus stimulation affects intestinal motility, which guides the optimal frequency window of 5 ∼ 10 Hz.

title: Ultra‐Strong, Leak‐Proof Bio‐Based Polyurethane Ionic Fibers for Sustainable Smart Wearables
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI)‐integrated digital flexible devices have been widely used in motion detection. However, the emphasis on sensitivity and response speed often overlooks environmental sustainability. Based on a green‐mechanical‐electrical synergistic design, a polar coordination and chemical confinement strategy is proposed to fabricate an ion‐conductive polyurethane fiber. Specifically, chemical confinement refers to the covalent incorporation of the polymerizable ionic‐liquid component into the polyurethane backbone through its hydroxyl‐functionalized imidazolium moiety. Polar coordination involves reversible Mg 2+ –carbonyl interactions that contribute to mechanical reinforcement and Mg 2+ retention. The resulting fiber exhibits a tensile strength of 52.75 MPa and an elongation at break of 1414%. Meanwhile, the in situ grafted ionic liquid provides an ionic conductivity of 0.209 mS cm −1 . After 120 h of vigorous stirring in water, the Mg concentration in the test medium reached 1.9 ppm, showing limited Mg release under the tested condition. Integrating this fiber into smart fabrics enables full‐body motion monitoring and accurate recognition of complex movements with 100% accuracy. This study establishes a closed‐loop paradigm from sustainable molecular design to AI‐driven decision‐making, offering new material design insights for next‐generation green, safe, and high‐performance smart wearable devices.

title: Luminescent and Stable Eu(III) Complex Nanocrystals: A Class of Eu(III) Emitters Toward Amine/Ammonia
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Eu(III) complexes exhibit highly efficient luminescence, while their emissions are significantly sensitive to amine/ammonia‐induced quenching. Herein, we report a class of Eu(III) complex nanocrystals in which aliphatic amines serve as structural regulators to construct highly luminescent and stable ultrasmall Eu(III) emitters. The addition of aliphatic amines enables the originally insoluble complexes to be dissolved in n ‐hexane, producing Eu(III) complex nanocrystal solutions. The primary‐ and secondary‐amine based Eu(btfa) 3 PBI nanocrystal solutions showed photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) reaching 24%–36% and 30%–37%, respectively. In a sharp contrast, the complex's luminescence was completely or substantially quenched when dissolved directly in primary or secondary amine liquids, with PLQYs decreasing to 0 or 0.0%–1.2%. The significantly suppressed quenching upon nanocrystal formation originated from the substantial reduction of vibrationally induced nonradiative decays, which was further supported by the low quenching constants toward amines. The nanocrystal's emission was further enhanced upon using the tertiary amines. A remarkable PLQY of 64% was obtained for tri‐ n ‐decylamine based Eu(dbm) 3 dmbipy nanocrystals. The nanocrystal solutions exhibited excellent stability, with their PLQYs well retained after 10 h of ambient storage or continuous irradiation with 365 nm UV light. Furthermore, proof‐of‐concept experiments demonstrated the potential application of nanocrystal solids as amine/ammonia‐resistant warning labels.

title: Advancements in Multi‐Dimensional Hexagonal Boron Nitride‐Based Thermal Management Materials: A Review
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hexagonal boron nitride (BN), due to its high thermal conductivity (TC), excellent electrical insulation, and low dielectric constant, has become an ideal filler for designing advanced thermal management materials (TMMs), effectively addressing thermal failure and electromagnetic leakage issues in advanced chips. BN structures in different dimensions (0D, 1D, and 2D) each have their own advantages, their interface morphology directly affects the TC of composite systems. However, there is still a lack of systematic understanding of phonon transport behavior at different interfaces in composite systems and their impact on thermal conduction network construction. This review focuses on dimensional classification and compares the intrinsic TC, phonon transport mechanisms, and network formation behavior of 0D, 1D, and 2D BN fillers. In addition to the traditional filler/polymer interfaces, this analysis also focused on the phonon transport properties at the homogeneous and heterogeneous nanoadditives interfaces of BN. At the same time, the TC of mono‐, di‐, and multi‐component nanoadditives systems were systematically evaluated, revealing the synergistic effects among BN of different dimensions. This review aims to provide a reference for reducing the thermal resistance of complex interfaces and promoting the practical application of micro–nano materials in the field of thermal management.

title: Engineering Tunable Helper Lipid Architecture to Improve Messenger RNA Lipid Nanoparticle Performance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper lipid architecture as a major, largely unexplored design lever for optimizing LNP performance. Using a modular library of more than 80 rationally designed helper lipids, we show that systematic variation in headgroup chemistry, linker topology, and tail cardinality reshapes both LNP biophysical behavior and biological performance. Martini molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with multimodal structural analyses reveal that high‐performing scaffolds undergo a pH‐dependent transition into fusogenic inverse hexagonal‐like ordering, substantially lowering the energetic barrier for endosomal escape. These performance gains persist across the clinically relevant ALC‐0315 and DLin‐MC3‐DMA platforms, establishing helper lipid architecture as a transferable design parameter across distinct ionizable lipid chemistries. Translating these design principles into function, optimized helper lipid formulations restore hepatic protein expression in a mouse model of ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency and increase antigen expression and immunogenicity in both preclinical models and in the in vitro human MIMIC platform. Together, these findings establish helper lipids as tunable molecular actuators of potency, tolerability, and stability, offering an engineering framework for next‐generation mRNA vaccines and therapeutics.

title: Water-energy-carbon nexus footprint of seawater desalination and transfer for industrial development: a hybrid life cycle -node-flow framework
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Seawater desalination is becoming increasingly important in arid, industrializing regions, but planning assessments often consider the embodied energy of supply chains and the operational energy of water transfer separately. This study presents a hybrid life cycle and node-flow framework that combines embodied energy and carbon emissions with a spatially explicit model of pumping energy based on elevation gain and hydraulic head losses. The framework is applied to Iran's Persian Gulf Seawater Desalination and Transfer (SDT) project, which supplies 138.76 million m 3 of water annually. Two strategies are compared: Water Transfer (WT), which pumps water inland while transporting products to the coast, and Industrial Transfer (IT), which relocates industries to the coast and transports raw materials from inland areas. Rail and truck freight represent the best- and worst-case transport scenarios, respectively. Pumping-energy intensity ranges from 333.2 to 21,462.4 MWh per million m 3 , depending mainly on transfer distance and elevation. Although industrial relocation reduces long-distance pumping-energy by 99.4%, transporting raw materials offsets much of this saving. Under the grid-average electricity scenario, rail transport results in nearly unchanged total energy use (+0.9%) but reduces carbon emissions by 22.7%. With truck transport, energy use and carbon emissions increase by 121.9% and 53.8%, respectively. Under low-carbon electricity, relocation increases carbon emissions with both transport modes. Benefits also vary by industry: relocation reduces energy use at the steel site under both modes and at the pelletizing site by rail, but not at the copper sites, where raw-material requirements are substantially greater than product output. The water footprint changes only slightly (−4.4%). This framework supports integrated assessments of energy and carbon trade-offs in desalination-dependent industrial systems.

title: Spatial patterns of hybrid PV–CSP–TES configurations for green hydrogen production across Algeria
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Existing studies have optimized hybrid PV–CSP plants or mapped suitable locations for solar hydrogen production, but the spatial dependence of the optimal hybrid architecture remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops a national-scale framework that couples GIS–FAHP screening with hourly PV–CSP–TES–electrolyzer simulation and site-specific NSGA-II optimization to determine how the cost-optimal system design changes across Algeria. At each meteorological location, PV capacity, CSP power-block capacity, TES duration, and solar multiple are jointly optimized for a fixed 50 MW electrolyzer, with the final configuration selected as the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) solution satisfying annual demand satisfaction (ADS) ≥ 90%. The resulting architecture varies substantially across the country: optimal PV capacity ranges from 70.03 to 168.86 MW, CSP power-block capacity from 50.00 to 92.98 MW, and solar multiple from 2.35 to 3.40, while annual hydrogen production remains comparatively stable at 7.58–7.65 kt H₂ yr −1 . Unconstrained LCOH ranges from 6.00 to 10.78 € kg −1 H₂ and narrows considerably after GIS-based deployment constraints are imposed. At Hassi R'Mel, the selected architecture combines approximately 100 MW PV, 50 MW CSP, SM = 2.80, and 16 h TES, achieving an LCOH of 6.53 € kg −1 H₂, 90.3% ADS and approximately 7.6 kt H₂ yr −1 . Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate and CSP capital cost as the strongest economic influences within the examined parameter ranges. A matched-output comparison shows that PV-only production can achieve lower LCOH when intermittency is acceptable, whereas PV–CSP–TES substantially increases electrolyzer utilization and production continuity. The results demonstrate that site-specific optimization is necessary to capture how economically preferred generation capacities and solar-field sizing adapt to local solar-resource conditions.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.
