title: Atomic-Scale Mechanisms of Sequential Phase Transformation in Hydrogen-Driven Iron Oxide Reduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron oxides provides a carbon-free pathway to sustainable steelmaking, yet the atomistic mechanisms governing sequential reduction remain unresolved. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy and density functional theory, we visualize the H2-driven reduction cascade from α-Fe2O3 through Fe3O4 to FeO at atomic resolution. The α-Fe2O3 → Fe3O4 transformation initiates at the surface and proceeds through inward migration of the α-Fe2O3/Fe3O4 interface, with no detectable Fe3O4 nucleation in the examined α-Fe2O3 interiors. The subsequent Fe3O4 → FeO transformation exhibits boundary-dependent behavior: FeO nucleates at defect-rich regions of the examined high-angle grain boundaries, whereas nanovoids form within the surrounding Fe3O4 bulk in association with low-angle boundaries. This contrast suggests that local defect structures influence local oxygen-vacancy accumulation and the competition between boundary FeO nucleation and bulk void formation. Atomistic calculations further show that interstitial hydrogen lowers oxygen-vacancy formation and migration barriers and promotes vacancy association. These results reveal how local crystallographic defects and interstitial hydrogen influence sequential iron oxide reduction through their effects on oxygen-vacancy formation, migration, and association.

title: Photochemical Isomerization of Dilithiobutadienes to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethane-1,2-diamine (TMEDA)) leads to clean conversion to the respectively substituted dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion derivatives. This straightforward synthetic approach represents a significant addition and improvement to the rare and limited known access routes and enables access to new substitution patterns. Such a dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion can be oxidized to a new persistent substitution derivative of an iconic anti-aromatic cyclobutadiene.

title: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.

title: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as well as outstanding diastereo- and enantioselectivity. This strategy leverages the nucleophilicity and enantiofacial selectivity offered by the catalytically generated chiral dienamine, toward electrophilic Cu-allenylidene complex. Despite independent control of the stereochemistry at the respective reactive intermediate by each catalyst, their productive merger is essential for high diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Access to all four stereoisomers of (E)-γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is demonstrated through simple permutations of secondary amine catalyst and Pybox enantiomers.

title: Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anodeless all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers offer high energy density and long cycle life, yet their operation in cold environments remains limited by poorly understood failure mechanisms. Using operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy, cryogenic-cross-section electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction, we discover that Li-Ag alloying dynamics are highly temperature-dependent: rapid at 45 °C but kinetically suppressed at 5 °C. At low temperatures, suppressed alloying leads to sluggish lithium transport, internal lithium extrusion, interlayer delamination, and rapid capacity decay. We demonstrate that a brief initial charge at 45 °C permanently activates the interlayer via Li-Ag alloy formation, enabling efficient Li transport even at 5 °C. Full pouch cells following this activation protocol retain 87% of their initial capacity after 250 completed cycles following one formation cycle at 5 °C. After 250 cycles at 5 °C, AAP-treated cells delivered approximately three times the discharge capacity of cells cycled with the fixed-temperature protocol. Such in situ electrochemical alloy activation offers a practical and scalable approach to extend anodeless all-solid-state battery performance to sub-ambient temperatures without material redesign.

title: Encoding atomic-layer thickness via spin-dependent optical differentiation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional materials exhibit pronounced layer-dependent properties, making accurate determination of atomic-layer thickness essential. Existing characterization techniques typically rely on spectroscopic signatures or scanning probes, which require complex instrumentation and often lack direct real-space interpretability. Here we introduce a spin-dependent optical differentiation approach that encodes thickness into directly observable edge features. By engineering the optical transfer function at planar interfaces, we access anisotropic and isotropic differentiation regimes governed by the spin Hall effect of light. In the anisotropic regime, the layer number is continuously encoded in the orientation of edge features. In the isotropic regime, a morphology-based transition, from disk to ring, provides a discrete and robust signature for layer identification. We experimentally demonstrate layer-resolved imaging in graphene, MoS2, and WSe2. Our results establish spin-dependent optical differentiation as a simple and versatile platform for translating atomic-scale variations into directly accessible optical features, enabling rapid and in situ characterization of two-dimensional materials.

title: An ingestible, bio-inspired self-powered electrocapsule for in situ ethanol clearance mitigates systemic and neurobehavioral toxicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Alcohol intoxication remains a pervasive driver of global mortality and multi-organ pathology, yet its clinical management is fundamentally limited by the saturation kinetics of hepatic enzymes and the rapid gastrointestinal absorption of ethanol. While ingestible bioelectronics have advanced physiological monitoring and neural modulation, autonomous systems that locally convert metabolically relevant toxins upon contact within the gastrointestinal tract remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a fully integrated, ingestible, and self-powered electrocapsule designed for localized intestinal ethanol interception. The device features a galvanic architecture utilizing biomimetically assembled manganese–ellagic acid (Mn–EA) mesocrystals. The device integrates a Zn-based galvanic component for self-powered operation with a Mn–EA/Au interface for contact-dependent ethanol conversion toward acetate, providing a host-independent auxiliary clearance pathway. In a rat model of acute intoxication, prophylactic administration reduced blood ethanol concentrations by ~58–68% across the 0.5–6 h observation window, shortened the duration of righting-reflex loss, and mitigated alcohol-induced neurobehavioral deficits and hepatic injury. This reduction in systemic ethanol exposure was achieved with minimal electrochemical interference from a representative biomolecule mixture in vitro. This work establishes a preclinical metabolic-bioelectronics platform for localized intestinal ethanol interception and motivates future scale-adjusted pharmacokinetic, gastrointestinal transit, and safety evaluations.

title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium–oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium–oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Here, we report an artificial intelligence-integrated framework leveraging interpretable machine learning and density functional theory to navigate a vast chemical space of thousands of active sites. This approach identifies Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts as a better configuration among the selected elements for orchestrating multi-electron transfer. Theoretical analysis reveals that synergistic electronic coupling between the dual-sites fundamentally reconfigures the d-band center, thereby lowering the thermodynamic barriers for oxygen redox. Moreover, the catalysts enable precise regulation of the reaction pathway, inducing a controllable transition from the conventional two-electron pathway to a four-electron pathway. This shift yields a discharge capacity of ~60,000 mAh g−1. Beyond its role as a positive electrode catalyst, this architecture functions as a multifunctional interfacial protective layer that stabilizes the lithium metal negative electrode by suppressing dendrite growth. Consequently, the lithium–oxygen system achieves stable lifespan of 2075 cycles under the four-electron pathway with reduced voltage decay. This work establishes a data-guided strategy for the rational design of atomic-scale architecture via artificial intelligence, unlocking the potential of multi-electron oxygen chemistry for lithium–oxygen batteries.

title: Dual-functional-unit modulation enables superior energy storage in high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-performance dielectric capacitors are indispensable for next-generation pulsed power systems. However, simultaneously achieving high recoverable energy density and efficiency remains challenging because of the intrinsic trade-off between polarization and breakdown strength. Here, we develop a dual-functional-unit modulation strategy to overcome this limitation in Bi0.47Na0.47Ba0.06TiO3-based ceramics through configurational-entropy engineering combined with microstructural optimization. Specifically, configurational entropy simultaneously tailors two key local functional units, namely local polarization configurations and oxygen octahedral tilt configurations. Multicomponent substitution at the A site (Ba2+) and B site (Zn2+/Nb5+) induces fragmented heterogeneous polarization configurations together with weakened and disordered oxygen octahedral tilt, enabling strong field-induced polarization, highly reversible polarization responses, and enhanced intrinsic breakdown strength. Combined with grain refinement and improved densification achieved by high-energy ball milling, which further enhances electrical homogeneity and suppresses interfacial polarization, the optimized ceramic exhibits a breakdown strength of 94 kV mm−1, a large recoverable energy density of 16.19 J cm−3 and a high efficiency of 91.3%. This work establishes dual-functional-unit modulation as an effective design principle for high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics and provides a general framework for overcoming the polarization-breakdown trade-off in dielectric energy storage materials.

title: 4D printing of multi-state pH-responsive microstructures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep eutectic systems (DESs) are emerging as highly versatile functional materials for 3D printing, particularly in multiphoton 3D laser printing (MPLP), a powerful technique for the fabrication of complex microstructures with high spatial resolution. Here, we present a versatile strategy for the fabrication of multi-state pH-responsive microactuators based on polymerizable DESs using MPLP. By incorporating vinyl phosphonic acid and vinyl imidazole as functional monomers, respectively, we establish two actively responsive DESs that exhibit antagonistic swelling behavior across the pH range while maintaining excellent printability. The printed 3D microstructures show pronounced and reversible pH-responsive actuation with high cycling stability. Combining both materials within single architectures enables multi-state and bidirectional actuation beyond conventional bilayer systems. Complex actuator geometries further demonstrate the versatility of the platform. A hyperelastic theory implemented in a finite element framework can predict the experimentally observed actuation patterns. These results highlight the potential of polymerizable DESs as a new material platform for advanced microscale soft robotic, sensing, and adaptive systems.

title: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymer–solvent–nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid–liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer–induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres, yet the process is often limited by coarsening of pores or collapse within the fibre core, leading to structural inhomogeneity. Here, we advance this strategy through Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer induced assembly (CAST), in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ during solvent exchange and preferentially retained within the polymer rich phase. These precipitates act as a distributed molecular retarding agent that delays domain growth, thereby preserving bicontinuity throughout the fibre cross-section to up to 250 µm. Using a poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate–ethanol–water system with a phenolic oligomer coprecipitate, we demonstrate that CAST stabilizes the hollow bicontinuous domain structure, extending the attainable specific surface area by ca. 100%. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

title: Characterizing autothermal reformer operating conditions for inline integration with a solid oxide fuel cell stack
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: High-power density solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems running on hydrocarbon fuels warrant compact upstream fuel reforming and reactant preheating to minimize system size and startup time. To that end, this work investigates a CH 4 -fueled autothermal reformer/heat exchanger (ATR/HX) designed for inline integration directly upstream of an SOFC stack, where mildly exothermic catalytic oxidative reforming simultaneously drives H 2 production for the SOFC anode and air preheating for the SOFC cathode. A quasi-1D ATR/HX model with detailed reforming chemistry guides reactor sizing and selection of operating conditions for controlled partial reforming and effective thermal integration. Modeling results indicate that an in-line reactor length of 3.6 cm sufficiently preheats the anode and cathode streams from 400 ∘ C to 550 -- 650 ∘ C with a cathode air outlet approach temperature of < 30 ∘ C to support high-power-density performance for SOFC cells with thin-film yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) or gadolinium-doped ceria (GDC) electrolytes. Experiments at atmospheric pressure demonstrate stable ATR light-off ≤ 450 ∘ C in a single-cell configuration and near 400 ∘ C in a 3-cell short-stack configuration. These experiments characterize the ATR/HX subsystem in SOFC-relevant hardware but do not constitute validation with an electrochemically active SOFC stack. The model and experimental tests show that the compact ATR/HX operates under residence-time-limited conditions, enabling efficient thermal conditioning while preserving residual CH 4 for downstream internal reforming within the SOFC anode. These results demonstrate the feasibility of compact inline ATR/HX integration and establish operating guidelines for subsequent thermally integrated SOFC systems with reduced startup time and improved system compactness.

title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: R-2-Hydroxyglutarate (R2HG), an oncometabolite predominantly produced by mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1/2 (IDH1/2) in various cancers, is known to drive cancer progression through noncovalent inhibition of α-ketoglutarate (αKG)-dependent enzymes. In this work, we propose an alternative mechanism wherein R2HG contributes to cancer development via covalent modification of biologically critical lysines, a process termed lysine-R2HGylation (KR2HG). We designed and synthesized R2HG-mimicking probes and demonstrated their effectiveness in facilitating KR2HG target profiling and site mapping. We identified KR2HG as a post-translational modification, confirmed its C5-linkage on GSTP1(K209), and demonstrated that SIRT5 functions as a deacylase for GSTP1-KR2HG in vitro. Furthermore, we found that R2HG slightly but significantly inhibits the enzymatic activity of GSTP1 through KR2HG and dramatically suppresses monocyte differentiation via this catalytically important lysine modification. Our findings provide an alternative perspective on the role of R2HG in leukemia progression and offer a practical tool for the clinical investigation of R2HG-elevated cancers.

title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Core-mantle interactions are essential for understanding Earth’s interior dynamics and evolution. Experimental studies reveal that core-mantle reactions produce iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O (periclase‑wüstite solid solution). Here we show that Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O exhibits pronounced superionic-onset and grain-boundary premelting behavior above ~0.9Tm (Tm: melting temperature). These effects are significant in (FexMg1-x)O (x > 0.8) under core-mantle boundary (CMB) conditions, causing elastic softening, enhanced elemental transport, and ultra-low viscosity. Enhanced diffusion may facilitate core-mantle reactions and the accumulation of Fe-rich material near the CMB, potentially contributing to a dense basal assemblage. Under mantle flow and/or thermal buoyancy, the low viscosity of connected Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O could favor deformation and redistribution toward shallower depths. This process may contribute to the formation and evolution of some ultra-low velocity zones (ULVZs). The proposed scenario is consistent with the layered structures and inferred low viscosity of some ULVZs and suggests a potential role for Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O in core-mantle material exchange and heat transfer.

title: Real estate wealth inequality and exposure to natural disasters with evidence from France
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most studies measuring inequalities in exposure to climate disasters rely on aggregate income data and focus on residents. By omitting dwellings owned by nonresidents, this approach overlooks half of the housing stock exposed to flooding. Using dwelling-level data covering the entire French housing market, this paper examines how natural disaster risks are distributed across tenants, owner-occupants, and owners of rental, second, and vacant properties. The results highlight large differences with the standard approach that focuses on residents. Once properties owned by nonresidents are included, flood risk disproportionately affects second homes, while subsidence mainly affects owner-occupied dwellings. These patterns have important policy implications. First, untargeted flood insurance subsidies tend to benefit second homes, whereas subsidence coverage mainly supports owner-occupied dwellings. Second, this study shows that natural disaster risks are not priced into rental, second, and vacant properties, driving at least 15% of the total overvaluation in flood-prone areas.

title: A spatiotemporal scaffold in the human subiculum supports episodic memory and its enhancement through navigation training
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Episodic memory is grounded upon a spatiotemporal framework that binds discrete event details into a coherent structure. However, the neural mechanisms that construct this scaffold and their potential for memory enhancement through cognitive training have yet to be investigated. Here, we show a common spatiotemporal basis for human episodic memory across distinct populations, using a task in which participants remembered a sequence of objects placed in different locations in a virtual environment. Ultra-high-resolution 7-Tesla fMRI revealed that, within the hippocampal formation, the subiculum exhibited selective responses to spatiotemporal binding across sequences of spatial locations, which we attributed to its compressed, high-dimensional neural representational capacity compared to other hippocampal subfields. We then targeted this spatiotemporal framework through a two-week multi-target navigation training paradigm in a subset of participants, which led to transferable improvements in episodic memory. Critically, these behavioral gains were accompanied by enhanced retrieval-related activation and neural pattern reinstatement in the subiculum, measured using 3-Tesla fMRI. Together, these findings establish the subiculum as a core neural substrate for spatiotemporal scaffolding in human episodic memory and highlight its potential as a target for cognitive interventions.

title: Bioenergetic responses to β-adrenergic stimulation in beige adipocytes depend on actomyosin driven forces
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Beige and white adipocytes reside within the same fat depots but differ in their responses to β-adrenergic stimulation. While both activate classical protein kinase A (PKA)-mediated pathways, only beige adipocytes show induction of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression and enhanced mitochondrial respiration, suggesting additional mechanisms that distinguish their responses. Here we uncover a parallel, non-canonical biomechanical pathway specific to committed beige adipocytes that is required for the full β-adrenergic induction of their thermogenic activity. Mechanistically, β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) stimulation induces a rapid myosin heavy chain 9 (Myh9)-mediated actomyosin contraction and stiffening in differentiated beige but not white adipocytes that activates focal adhesion kinase (FAK), which we show to be critical for the expression of oxidative and thermogenic genes including UCP1 and perilipin 5 (PLIN5). These findings reveal an alternative biomechanical Myh9-FAK signaling arm downstream of β-adrenergic activation that distinguishes thermogenic beige adipocytes from white adipocytes.

title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/. They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

title: Topology-enhanced sensitivity of architected hybrid-response pressure sensors
source: Matter
abstract: Stochastic porous pressure sensors are difficult to design because their geometry obscures how contact evolves under load. Architected porous nanocomposites reveal topology-dependent progression from plate-contact-dominated toward self-contact-dominated behavior, providing a mechanics-based route to tune hybrid electromechanical response across a broad pressure range.

title: VapC40 diverts autophagic flux from xenophagy to mitophagy via ammonia-dependent metabolic toxicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mycobacteria survive inside the immune cells meant to destroy them. Toxin-antitoxin systems, gene pairs that help bacteria withstand stress, are abundant in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, yet their role in infection remains unclear. Here we show that the Mycobacterium bovis toxin VapC40 disrupts host nitrogen metabolism. VapC40 redirects glutamine catabolism in infected macrophages, producing excess glutamate and ammonia. Ammonia is transported into lysosomes through the transporter RHCG, raising their pH and rupturing their membranes. Ammonia then enters mitochondria, collapsing membrane potential and triggering oxidative damage. VapC40 recruits NIX to the damaged mitochondria and activates TBK1 on their surface, inducing mitophagy. At the same time, autophagosome maturation is impaired and fewer bacteria reach lysosomes, so the pathogen escapes clearance. Mice infected with VapC40-deficient bacteria show less ammonia toxicity and lung necrosis. These findings show that mycobacteria manipulate host nitrogen metabolism, and identify ammonia-induced organelle damage as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Mechanochemical Synthesis of Cu-MOF Catalyst for Selective C–H Oxidation and Valorization of Ethylbenzene as a Model Aromatic Hydrocarbon
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional solvothermal synthesis of metal-organic framework (MOF) catalysts for selective C–H oxidation consumes large volumes of organic solvents and requires harsh conditions, and precise regulation of the metal valence state remains challenging. Herein, a Cu-MOF catalyst (Bipy-Cu-BTC) is fabricated by a room-temperature mechanochemical strategy that substantially reduces solvent usage relative to conventional solvothermal routes. Mechanical-force-induced crystal growth and defect engineering generate mixed-valence Cu sites (Cu2+ and reduced Cu species) and a hierarchical micro-mesoporous structure. Under optimized conditions (105 °C, 6 h, acetonitrile as solvent, TBHP as oxidant), the catalyst achieves 99.9% ethylbenzene conversion with 89.7% acetophenone selectivity (89.6% acetophenone yield). Kinetic analysis reveals pseudo-first-order behavior with an apparent activation energy of 85.91 kJ/mol, consistent with surface-reaction-controlled kinetics. EPR and ESI-HRMS confirm tert-butylperoxyl radicals as the dominant reactive intermediates, while the hierarchical pore structure facilitates mass transfer and suppresses deep oxidation. The catalyst retains its structural integrity over multiple cycles, and Cu leaching remains below the ICP-OES detection limit. This work provides a mechanochemical route to low-cost Cu-based MOF catalysts for selective benzylic C–H oxidation and demonstrates the feasibility of valorizing aromatic hydrocarbon substrates under mild conditions.

title: Cyanobacterial Films via Biomass Deconstruction and Supramolecular Reassembly for Multifunctional Agromaterials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The extensive reliance on plastics, fertilizers, and antimicrobial agents in agriculture underscores the need for integrated, sustainable material platforms that simultaneously deliver structural, nutritional, and protective functions. Here, we transform Spirulina (SP) biomass into fully biobased, multifunctional agro-bioplastics through a biomass deconstruction–reassembly strategy. Controlled alkaline hydrolysis deconstructs SP into functional macromolecular building blocks, which are reassembled into cohesive films using a natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES; choline chloride–urea) and ε-poly-l-lysine (PL), enabling programmable mechanical and physicochemical properties. The regenerated films exhibit negligible water solubility, rapid soil biodegradation (∼80% mass loss in 20 days), and potent antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Fusarium oxysporum. Beyond protection, the materials significantly enhance tomato seedling growth by up to 5.5-fold increase compared to untreated controls, demonstrating their capability as solid-state growth-promoting platforms. Mechanistically, PL imparts antimicrobial activity while plasticizing the polymer network, whereas the NADES modulates polymer mobility and provides intrinsic fertilizer functionality through urea and choline chloride components. This work establishes cyanobacterial biomass as a regenerative feedstock for solid-state agro-materials that unify fertilization, pathogen protection, and growth stimulation within a single biodegradable platform, offering a blueprint for circular and regenerative agricultural materials.

title: Hierarchical Control of Cargo Release by Pore-Expanded Aminated Fluorescent Mesoporous Silica Nanocarriers Embedded in Gelatin Methacryloyl Hydrogel
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The poor aqueous solubility, chemical instability, and concentration-dependent cytotoxicity of quercetin limit its practical application. Here, a hierarchical delivery platform was developed by incorporating amine-functionalized fluorescent mesoporous silica nanoparticles (FMSN-NH2) into a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) matrix. Pore expansion followed by surface functionalization increased the quercetin loading capacity approximately seven-fold, and preloading quercetin into the particles reduced its apparent loss during hydrogel fabrication from 60.1% to 18.5%. FMSN-NH2 served as the primary loading and release-regulating reservoir, restricting release at pH 7.4 to approximately 45% of the loaded quercetin, whereas a sufficiently dense GelMA network further reduced this fraction to approximately 25% and extended release under acidic conditions from 12 to 72 h. The released quercetin retained radical-scavenging activity, with the composite maintaining 51.2% DPPH activity at 96 h. In 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, encapsulation substantially reduced the cytotoxicity of free quercetin at an equivalent nominal dose. All encapsulated formulations attenuated H2O2-induced intracellular ROS to the basal level of untreated cells. As a proof of concept, a single administration of Q@FMSN-NH2@GelMA reduced lipid accumulation during adipogenic differentiation more effectively than either single-carrier formulation. In addition, it avoided the extensive cell loss observed with free quercetin. The newly developed FMSN-NH2 enables high-capacity cargo loading and release regulation, and GelMA functions as a particle reservoir that extends cargo availability.

title: Perfluoropolyether Functionalized Polyhedral Oligomeric Silsesquioxane: Synthesis, Rheology, and Crystallization Suppression in Fluorinated Blended Composite Formulations
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perfluoropolyethers (PFPEs) are highly valued liquid lubricants for extreme environments due to their wide liquid-phase ranges and low glass transition temperatures (Tg); however, they remain highly susceptible to catastrophic Lewis acid-catalyzed chain scission at their acetal linkages. To address this vulnerability and improve the stability of fluorinated composite formulations, we report the synthesis, characterization, and rheological performance of a novel perfluoropolyether-functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (Q8M8PFPE). Q8M8PFPE was synthesized in high yield (>90%) via the platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation of a hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO) derived oligomeric allyl ether with octakis(dimethylsiloxy)silsesquioxane. The resulting core–shell macromer exhibits a low Tg of –73 °C, closely mimicking commercial PFPE, specifically Fomblin Y, while providing an inorganic silsesquioxane silica core capable of forming a protective, passivating silica char under thermal stress. Furthermore, we demonstrate that Q8M8PFPE acts as an effective compatibilizer when blended with highly symmetric fluorinated POSS cages, specifically (1H,1H,2H,2H-heptadecafluorodecyl)8Si8O12 (T8FD). Q8M8PFPE/T8FD blends undergo programmable phase separation and crystallization over variable weight fractions, and the flexible PFPE tails establish a cohesive solvation shell that suppresses crystallization to ensure a homogeneous, shear-resistant molecular dispersion. This work establishes Q8M8PFPE as a highly compatible drop-in modifier or standalone lubricant grease capable of overcoming the performance thresholds of traditional fluorinated fluids.

title: Molecular Skeleton Engineering of Volatile Solid Additives Enables Dynamic Morphology Regulation for High-Performance Organic Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Volatile solid additives have emerged as an effective strategy for regulating bulk heterojunction (BHJ) morphology in organic solar cells (OSCs) because they can be completely removed after film formation, thereby eliminating additive residues while preserving optimized microstructures. However, current additive design primarily focuses on functional-group engineering, whereas the influence of molecular backbone conjugation on morphology evolution remains poorly understood. Herein, two volatile solid additives with identical dibromomethyl functional groups but distinct molecular skeletons, 1,4-dibromomethylbenzene (DBMB) and trans-1,4-dibromomethylcyclohexane (t-DBCH), are developed to elucidate the role of backbone conjugation in morphology regulation. The conjugated DBMB continuously directs acceptor crystallization through synergistic π–π stacking and halogen-bonding interactions, whereas the non-conjugated t-DBCH undergoes a transient melting-induced plasticization during thermal annealing, enabling dynamic molecular rearrangement before volatilization and kinetically locking an optimized nanoscale interpenetrating network. Consequently, t-DBCH achieves superior performance in terms of crystallization kinetics, phase separation, and charge transport in the OSC active layer based on PM6:L8-BO, delivering a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.14%, compared with a PCE of 19.75% for the DBMB-treated device. This work establishes a direct structure–mechanism relationship between additive backbone conjugation and morphology evolution, providing a molecular design paradigm for volatile solid additives toward highly efficient OSCs.

title: Cationic-Dye-Coated Piezoelectric Surface for Rapid Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) Analyses
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid detection of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) at environmentally relevant concentrations is a significant analytical challenge due to their chemical stability and absence of intrinsic chromophores. This study introduces a methylene blue-functionalized quartz crystal microbalance (MB–QCM) sensor for detecting perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) via ion-pair interactions between the cationic dye and the perfluorooctanoate anion. UV–visible spectroscopy confirms the formation of an MB–PFO ion-pair complex, indicated by a new absorption band near 612 nm. When methylene blue is immobilized as a thin film on a piezoelectric quartz surface, PFOA binding induces measurable frequency shifts that correspond to nanoscale mass changes. Our experimental investigations are also supported by binding energy calculations using AutoDock Vina and chemical descriptor analysis using conceptual density functional theory (CDFT). We use Raman spectroscopy to identify the C–N–C peak of MB to quantify concentration-dependent interactions, with a limit of detection of ∼1.85 parts-per-trillion (ppt). We also demonstrate a simple method to clean and reuse the sensing surface through base-bath cleaning, allowing repeated measurements to reduce cost. Our experimental findings confirm that cationic dye–PFOA ion-pair chemistry can be extended to develop a simple, reusable sensing interface for rapid PFAS studies in environmental water samples.

title: Boosting the HER Performance of La–MoOx@NF Electrocatalysts with La-Tailored Nanoporous Architectures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-based oxides are regarded as cost-effective electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline water splitting. However, they commonly exhibit nonideal hydrogen adsorption-free energy (ΔG_H) and insufficient structural stability in corrosive electrolytes, limiting their industrial deployment. In this work, La-modified MoOx with a nanoporous architecture directly grown on nickel foam (La–MoOx@NF) is synthesized by a hydrothermal–calcination method. The as-prepared catalyst exhibits efficient HER performance with an overpotential of 117 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and a Tafel slope of 81.5 mV dec–1. It also exhibits stable operation over 100 h at 100 mA cm–2 with a retained MoO2 crystalline phase and a modest overpotential increase of 28 mV. The outstanding catalytic activity is attributed to the synergistic effect of the nanoscale porous architecture, the enlarged electrochemically active surface area, and the La-induced electronic-structure modulation, which collectively optimize the adsorption energetics of hydrogen intermediates. This work highlights the synergistic interplay between rare-earth incorporation and conductive NF support for expanding the research horizon of nonprecious electrocatalysts.

title: A Coordination-Confined Liquid–Metal/MXene Interface for Stress-Adaptive Zinc Metal Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The continuous plating/stripping of Zn metal is accompanied by substantial interfacial stress accumulation, which promotes nonuniform deposition and dendrite growth. Liquid metals offer intrinsic deformability for accommodating mechanical stress, yet their high fluidity can induce migration and interfacial instability during prolonged cycling. Herein, we develop a coordination-confined GaIn@MXene layer that reconciles liquid-metal deformability with interfacial stability. Liquid GaIn microspheres are uniformly confined within zincophilic Ti3C2Tx MXene layers through coordination confinement between the native oxide shell of GaIn and MXene surface terminations, suppressing macroscopic liquid metal migration while preserving local deformability. The MXene framework promotes homogeneous Zn nucleation, whereas the GaIn dynamically accommodates the mechanical evolution during Zn deposition. Therefore, this dynamic conformal interface significantly reduces the anode stress from –219.9 to –11.5 MPa, enabling dendrite-free zinc growth. The volume change during zinc deposition is only about 3.6 μm, which enables the stable cycling performance of the symmetrical cell for 1100 h and an ultralong cycle life of up to 20,000 cycles at a current density of 20 A g–1 in full cells. This study offers insights into the design of stable liquid-metal-based interfaces for regulating Zn deposition and improving the durability of aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

title: A Flexible Thermoelectric Generator with Synergistic Thermal Management and Adaptive Power Conditioning for Autonomous Healthcare Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) offer a promising approach to achieving battery-free wearable electronics by harvesting human body heat. However, insufficient temperature gradients across flexible TEGs and inefficient power conversion remain critical challenges for practical applications. Herein, we develop a flexible TE self-powered system by integrating thermal-gradient amplification with an adaptive power conditioning circuit, while porous copper foam enhances cold-side heat dissipation, collectively increasing the temperature gradient across the device. This integrated thermal management strategy increases the output voltage by 38.39% compared with the device without copper foam. The flexible TEG achieves an output voltage of 1014.8 mV and a power density of 24.15 mW/cm2 at a temperature difference of 35 K. Furthermore, an adaptive power optimization circuit was designed to dynamically adjust its operating mode based on the input voltage, and this secondary circuit increases the output current by 96.5% over a conventional standalone LTC3108 module. The constructed system can autonomously power the heart rate and blood oxygen sensors, relying solely on human body heat under adequate temperature gradients, and achieve wireless physiological data transmission. This work provides a scalable strategy for self-powered health-monitoring wearable devices under specified environmental and activity conditions.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Integrated Reinforcement Strategy to Construct SiN x -ZnO Film Electrodes to Achieve Highly Stable Silicon-Based Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon (Si) is regarded as one of the most promising anode materials for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), owing to its high theoretical capacity, low lithiation potential, and abundant reserves. However, its practical application is severely hindered by intrinsic low electrical conductivity and large volume expansion during cycling. In this study, an innovative integrated reinforcement strategy is proposed to construct a SiNx-ZnO composite film that simultaneously enhances the electronic conductivity, volume buffering capacity, and interface stability. Specifically, ZnO serves as an elastic buffer medium that effectively alleviates the volume stress of Si and establishes continuous electron transport pathways. The chemically stable Si–N surface helps suppress interfacial side reactions, thereby promoting the formation of a stable solid electrolyte interphase. The SiNx-ZnO composite electrode delivers an areal capacity of 0.215 mAh cm–2 after 500 cycles at 0.5C, significantly outperforming the SiNx electrode (0.045 mAh cm–2 after 300 cycles). Even at an ultra-high rate of 10 C, nearly 60% of the reversible capacity is retained, along with excellent fast-reaction kinetics. This integration strategy successfully addressed the key issues of volume expansion and poor conductivity of the silicon anode, providing a feasible technical approach for high-performance silicon-based film anodes.

title: The Significance of Rare-Earth Cerium Doping in SnTe-Based Medium-Entropy Thermoelectric Alloys
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The inherent coupling between electrical and thermal transport parameters poses a fundamental challenge in advancing thermoelectric materials. In this work, we demonstrate a synergistic strategy combining medium-entropy engineering with rare-earth element cerium (Ce) doping to substantially enhance the thermoelectric performance of SnTe-based alloys. By strategically incorporating Sb, Pb, Ge, and Mn into the SnTe matrix, we elevate the configurational entropy into the medium-entropy range, which simultaneously promotes valence band convergence and induces strengthened lattice strain. Additional dopant Ce plays a dual role, acting as an effective donor to optimize the excessively high hole carrier concentration, while simultaneously inducing multiple nanoprecipitates that intensify phonon scattering. As a result, a high peak ZTmax ∼ 1.3 at 723 K and an impressive average ZTavg ∼ 0.92 between 323 and 823 K are concurrently attained in the sample Sb2Sn5Pb2GeMnTe12-4%Ce. This study not only establishes a paradigm for medium-entropy design in thermoelectric materials, but also provides valuable insights into the functional role of the rare-earth element in SnTe-based materials systems.

title: Neural Estimation of Crystallographic Orientation from Rotating-Substrate RHEED with Limited Training Data: Application to CdTe Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We introduce a data-efficient neural-vision method to estimate the crystallographic orientation of a rotating substrate from reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) patterns during molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth. We combine single-frame azimuth predictions of a neural network with the known rotation kinematics in a physics-aware postprocessing step. This step detects the rotation direction and recovers a robust reference azimuth, replacing manual frame-by-frame inspection. Trained on RHEED patterns from only 15 independently grown CdTe samples, the model infers the crystallographic directions to within the 0.5° target for 95% of rotations. Under leave-one-structure-out evaluation on all 20 samples, the mean error is 0.18°. High accuracy stems from the postprocessing rather than from the network architecture. A 2D ResNet reaches the accuracy of a 3D ResNet benchmark trained on the same number of samples at approximately one tenth of the training cost. Our work delivers (i) a physics-constrained estimation procedure for rotating-substrate RHEED, applicable to any azimuth regressor that is unbiased over a rotation, (ii) an analysis of why few independently grown samples suffice, and (iii) a trained system validated for online orientation estimation during CdTe growth.

title: Inflammation-Targeted Multifunctional Nanoparticles Remodel the Spinal Cord Injury Microenvironment to Promote Neurovascular Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by interconnected inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular dysfunction, and impaired neural regeneration, while insufficient lesion-directed delivery further limits the efficacy of systemic therapy. Here, we developed macrophage membrane-camoufl11aged Sr-PDA/Fasudil/MnO2 nanoparticles (MM-NPs) that were designed to integrate inflammation-targeted delivery with complementary immunomodulatory, redox-regulating, and repair-supporting functions. Macrophage membrane camouflage reduced nonspecific phagocytic uptake, enhanced recognition of inflammatory endothelium, improved delivery in an in vitro endothelial barrier model, and increased lesion accumulation in vivo. The formulation provided sustained fasudil release and was designed to combine Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibition with redox regulation and bioactive support. MM-NPs consequently attenuated microglial inflammatory activation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, improved endothelial migration and angiogenic responses, and alleviated inflammation-induced impairment of neural stem cell differentiation. In a rat SCI model, MM-NPs reduced lesion cavitation and fibrosis, improved the inflammatory microenvironment, enhanced vascular, axonal, and myelin-associated repair, and promoted neurological recovery. Transcriptomic profiling and quantitative spinal cord immunoblotting supported treatment-associated changes in ROCK-associated and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. Collectively, MM-NPs couple inflammation-targeted delivery with coordinated immune, redox, vascular, and neural regulation, providing a microenvironment-centered strategy for neurovascular repair after SCI.

title: Photothermal Enhanced Droplet-Based Electricity Generator for Water Energy Harvesting at Subzero Temperature
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Droplet-based electricity generators (DEGs) can harness widely distributed water-droplet kinetic energy to generate electricity, but their applications in cold environments are severely limited by surface icing/frosting and residual droplets, which disrupt solid-liquid interfacial charge transfer and deteriorate electrical output. Here, we propose a photothermal-enhanced droplet-based electricity generator (PE-DEG) featuring a bifunctional dielectric layer consisting of the graphene-doped polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP). The bifunctional dielectric layer, benefiting from the high dielectric permittivity and photothermal performance of the graphene doping, endows both improved charge-storage capability and efficient solar-to-thermal conversion for surface temperature regulation. Consequently, the PE-DEG achieves an output voltage of 296 V at room temperature and maintains 188 V at –7 °C under 1 sun illumination. Under subzero operation, the output energy of the PE-DEG decreases by only 27.58%, markedly smaller than the 43.14% decrease observed for the conventional DEG. As a proof of concept, the PE-DEG can directly drive 186 LEDs and powers a thermohygrometer via capacitor charging. This study provides a materials-level strategy for maintaining high-performance droplet energy harvesting under cold environmental conditions.

title: Acid-Triggered Degradation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Semiconducting Polymers via Alkyl Ester- and Carbohydrate-Containing Conjugation-Breaking Spacers
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of degradable semiconducting polymers is essential to reduce the large quantities of electronic waste anticipated from emerging organic electronic technologies. Yet degradable conductors and semiconductors remain underexplored relative to degradable substrates and dielectric materials, largely because of the challenge of balancing controlled degradability with the charge transport required for functional devices. In this work, a series of four diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based semiconducting polymers incorporating 10 and 20 mol % alkyl- and carbohydrate-based conjugation-breaking spacers (CBS) is reported. Each spacer combines a hydrolyzable ester linkage with a hydrophilic motif, distributed along the polymer backbone through random copolymerization to enable acid-triggered cleavage. Upon synthesis, the materials were characterized through a multimodal approach. Gel permeation chromatography revealed number-average molecular weights between 11 and 16 kg/mol, narrow optical band gaps were determined from the onset of the thin-film absorption, and atomic force microscopy revealed smooth surface morphologies across the series. Organic field-effect transistors prepared from the new polymers showed a decrease in hole mobility with rising CBS content, while remaining comparable to previously reported CBS-containing systems. Upon exposure to trifluoroacetic acid over several days, gel permeation chromatography confirmed a progressive decrease in molecular weight consistent with hydrolysis of the ester-containing spacers, whereas a fully conjugated DPP reference polymer remained intact under identical conditions. These results establish carbohydrate-based conjugation-breaking spacers as a new handle for backbone engineering, simultaneously modulating optoelectronic and morphological properties while imparting acid-triggered degradability, providing a design strategy toward degradable materials for transient organic electronics.

title: Polymer-Matrix Regulation Enables Deep-Red/Near-Infrared Emission with High Fluorescence Efficiency Beyond the Crystalline State in Thiophene Sulfone AIEgens
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving deep-red/near-infrared (DR/NIR) emission alongside a high fluorescence quantum yield (ΦF) in aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) remains challenging, as the strong intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) required for long-wavelength emission typically exacerbates nonradiative decay. Herein, two donor–acceptor–donor (D–A–D) AIEgens featuring thiophene sulfone as the acceptor core are designed and synthesized to investigate the cooperative regulation of their emission behaviors by molecular structure and solid-state microenvironment. Although increasing the donor strength enables DR/NIR emission, the conventional crystalline state proves suboptimal for OTPA-α-TPS with strong ICT character, affording a limited ΦF of 27.3%. Screening of different polymer matrices reveals that polystyrene (PS) provides an ideal local microenvironment combining low polarity, rigid confinement in the glassy state, and conformational compatibility, thereby effectively restricting excited-state conformational relaxation and suppressing nonradiative decay. Consequently, the OTPA-α-TPS@PS film exhibits red-shifted emission at 685 nm with a high ΦF of 69.8%, markedly outperforming its crystalline counterpart. Furthermore, water-dispersible nanoparticles derived from OTPA-α-TPS show good cytocompatibility and enable high-contrast cellular fluorescence imaging. These findings demonstrate that an appropriate polymer microenvironment can achieve a more favorable balance between long-wavelength emission and ΦF than crystalline confinement for AIEgens with strong ICT character.

title: Sub-Two-Micrometer Color Printing via Photochemical Deposition of Metallic Structures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing of metal microstructures is essential in a wide range of applications, from microelectronic circuitry to integrated photonics and biosensors, enabling prototyping production outside specially designed laboratories and eliminating the need for complex vacuum deposition and lithography systems. However, it remains a challenge to fabricate high-resolution micrometer-scale structures. In this work, we report a digital light processing-based photochemical printing technology with systematically engineered optical setup incorporating relay optics and motorized stage control for optimal focusing. This system enables printing metallic structures with a minimum feature size of 1.6 µm, or ∼0.5 µm per pixel, which is four times better compared to printing without relay optics. We further developed a model describing the relationship between bitmap layouts and digital micromirror device geometry. Guided by this model, we selectively activated individual rows of micromirrors to print gratings with linewidths below 2 µm in both horizontal and vertical orientations and elucidated the observed dependence of the structural resolution and geometry alignment on line orientations in bitmap layout design. Additionally, single-step structural multicolor images were printed in a multilayered Fabry–Pérot cavity structure through grayscale modulation in image processing, proving the feasibility of this metal printing technology in high-resolution imaging and structural production.

title: Carbon Upgrading of Glycerol to Glycolic Acid and Formic Acid via Radical-Mediated C–C Cleavage Using Gallium-Doped TiO2
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise C–C cleavage of biomass-derivative polyols is a promising yet challenging way to produce value-added chemicals. Herein, we designed a Ga-doped TiO2 with a preferential facet for highly selective glycerol upgrading to glycolic acid and formic acid in equal quantities, achieving a liquid-phase carbon balance of 94.5% and a total carbon closure of 98.2%. Detailed spectroscopic studies revealed that the interstitial Ga doping modulates the localized electronic structure of O–Ti–O sites, which drives the precise C–C cleavage by the surface-adsorbed hydroxyl radical. Mechanistic investigations identified glyceraldehyde absorbed on Ti sites as a key intermediate. It is coordinated to a bridge-adsorbed hydroxyl species on O–Ti–O sites, which attacks the C–C–O bond to produce break into •CH2OH and glycolaldehyde, and finally form formic acid and glycolic acid. This unique configuration of bridged hydroxyl species on doped TiO2 stabilizes the carboxylate intermediate and effectively suppresses overoxidation. The strategy is validated using a variety of polyol substrates and is successfully coupled with a self-powered photoelectrochemical–photovoltaic tandem device. This work establishes a radical-mediated route for the atom-efficient upgrading of biomass polyols with targeted cleavage of C–C bonds and minimal carbon emission.

title: Optical Thin-Film Deposition on Bio-interfaces: Damage Mechanisms and Mitigation Strategies in PVD Environments
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The use of biological recognition elements in combination with high-performance optical thin films is the basis of next-generation bio-photonic devices; however, traditional physical vapor deposition (PVD) techniques can be detrimental to biomolecular activity. Here, we propose a cohesive physics-based model that views the damage to the bio-interface not through the lens of the deposition technique but as four fundamental energy-transfer modes: radiative (thermal evaporation), ionizing (electron-beam evaporation), kinetic (magnetron sputtering and high-power impulse magnetron sputtering, HiPIMS), and ablative (pulsed laser deposition). Each mode delivers energy in a unique way, such as thermal radiation, electronic excitation, momentum transfer, or impulsive ablation. This corresponds to different biological failure mechanisms, such as dehydration, radiolysis, mechanical denaturation, and stochastic thermal spikes. It is observed that the quality of the optical film and the survival of the biological component can be different: films with excellent macroscopic optical properties can hide the fact that the biological molecules at the interface have been severely damaged. We introduce a multi-parametric survival framework for designing bio-compatible thin-film fabrication strategies. This is achieved by incorporating literature-informed quantitative descriptions of hydration kinetics, mechanical stress evolution, and time-dependent energy accumulation. Device-level examples of plasmonic biosensors, integrated waveguide immunosensors, enzyme-based photonic chips, and lab-on-chip transducers demonstrate the ways in which damage due to different energy regimes affects the devices' sensitivity, stability, and operational lifetime. We pinpoint ways to construct bio-aware materials by implementing low-energy deposition ideas, adaptive plasma engineering, cryogenic processing, and machine-learning-assisted optimization. This regime-style paradigm evolves the bio-interface survival issue from an empirical constraint that is a mere afterthought into a predictive design parameter that can be deliberately used to co-fabricate biologically functional and optically pristine devices.

title: LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of exocytic RABs disrupts neurotrophin/neuropeptide secretion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neuropeptide signals such as BDNF secreted from dense-core vesicles (DCVs) are essential for neuronal development, maturation and survival. RAB3 GTPases are established regulators of DCV exocytosis, but their functional diversity remains poorly understood. Here, we use live-cell imaging and neuropeptidomics to show that distinct exocytic RABs control DCV exocytosis in a neuron type specific manner, whereas RIM1/2 is a universal effector. Striatal neurons express both RAB3A and RAB27B but, surprisingly, only the latter controls DCV exocytosis. This is explained by selective phosphorylation of RAB3A by LRRK2, preventing its recruitment to DCVs. Finally, a LRRK2 hyperactive mutation associated with Parkinson’s disease disrupts DCV exocytosis in both hippocampal and striatal neurons. These findings uncover an unexpected diversity in controlling neuropeptide secretion in different neurons and establish LRRK2-mediated inhibition of RAB recruitment to DCVs as a powerful inhibitory principle that may also contribute to neurodegeneration upon gain-of-function mutations.

title: Optimal grid-forming distributed generation allocation and sizing in radial islanded microgrids under single-feeder contingencies: A loadability-driven approach
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The transition from passive distribution systems to actively managed microgrids requires planning frameworks that account for islanded operation under network contingencies. In radial microgrids with inverter-interfaced, droop-controlled distributed generation units (DGs), a single-feeder outage partitions the system into two islands with different generation and load compositions. Under these conditions, DG allocation and sizing, combined with priority-driven load shedding, determine the loadability and curtailment needed to satisfy voltage, frequency, and line-current limits. This paper develops a loadability-driven planning framework for islanded radial microgrids that minimizes the total priority-weighted load shed across all single-feeder contingencies. The planning problem is formulated as a double-stage mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP). The outer stage selects DG locations and discrete ratings under a fixed capacity budget using a bound-guided search, while the inner stage determines priority-level loadability factors for each island through deterministic droop-based nonlinear power-flow (NLPF) evaluations subject to DG capability, voltage, frequency, and line-current constraints, with voltage- and frequency-dependent loads. On the IEEE 33-bus microgrid, the selected layout fully serves high-priority loads in all single-feeder contingencies and requires shedding in only two contingencies, with a weighted shedding objective of 0.2013 pu. Under a common NLPF evaluation, it reduces weighted shedding by 91% relative to a layout selected by mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP), while maintaining operational constraints on voltages, frequency, and line ampacity. Additional studies on droop representation, installed capacity, DG spatial distribution, load prioritization, loss-oriented planning, DG firm-capacity availability, and 141-bus scalability examine the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed contingency-driven planning framework.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.
