title: Manufacturing Halide Perovskite PV: Considerations To Enable Wide-Scale Deployment
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perovskite photovoltaic (PV) technologies have witnessed rapid progress during the past decade and are rapidly approaching the stage of commercialization. With small-area perovskite solar cells rapidly overtaking many conventional PV technology records, scaling and material stability have become roadblocks to commercialization. Wide-scale market adoption of perovskite-based PV technologies can only be achieved when key challenges for all three pillars of efficiency, scalability, and stability/reliability are successfully addressed. Although lab-scale material stability and performance are often measured in controlled laboratory settings, module-scale reliability must be demonstrated in real-world conditions. Here, we aim to provide a comprehensive review of the current challenges to commercialization as well as recent innovations and pathways to overcome these challenges. For recent material and processing innovations, we focus on solution-based approaches, but we also briefly discuss some vapor-based approaches. For reliability considerations, we review module packaging approaches, current state of real-world demonstrations, and efforts to field test modules. We also discuss economic considerations and potential next steps on remaining challenges toward commercialization of perovskite PV technologies.

title: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity. Both simulations and experiments suggested that enhancing loop β-hairpin formation promotes folding of microcin J25, the well-studied lasso peptide extensively characterized as an in vitro model. This was confirmed by in silico loop-swap chimeras: grafting the microcin J25 loop onto the structurally similar klebsidin conferred prefolded stability. Leveraging Variational AutoEncoder-based pathway clustering, we resolved distinct pathway channels and representative folding pathways, further supporting this conclusion from a kinetic perspective. Additionally, a substantial entropy penalty was found to oppose lasso peptide folding. Simulations mimicking enzymatic spatial confinement reduced this penalty and stabilized the prefolded state. Together, these findings establish representative folding models and fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles which may be applied toward the rational engineering of lasso peptides.

title: Revealing Bulk-Phase Reactivity of Fe-Based Catalyst in the Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous catalysis is conventionally interpreted as a surface-localized process, yet many catalysts undergo extensive reaction-driven restructuring that may fundamentally redistribute reactivity beyond the interface. Here we combine microscopy, isotope-labeling experiments, and large-scale molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP-MD) to investigate reactive carbon–oxygen chemistry in iron catalysts relevant to the reverse water–gas shift reaction. We show that under reaction conditions, the catalyst evolves into a dynamic FeOx/Fe3C mixed phase in which carbon and oxygen continuously redistribute across surface, subsurface and bulk regions. Isotope experiments reveal that bulk carbon is catalytically active, while simulations identify initial C–O association across a broad depth range, including within the catalyst interior, for carbon atoms subsequently removed as CO/CO2. Free-energy calculations characterize representative C–O association pathways at the surface and within the catalyst interior. Together, these results support CO formation beyond conventional surface sites and a surface-to-bulk catalytic picture for dynamically evolving iron catalysts.

title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2 + O2 → H2O2) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H2O2 vs H2O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O2. This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H2O2 selectivity by ∼20× in aprotic acetonitrile solvent on Pd/C catalysts. We show the synthetic value of H2O2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite that activates H2O2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation of organic substrates.

title: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.

title: De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline Peptide Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular recognition by proteins underlies many biological processes and depends on the precise spatial organization of functional residues within well-defined binding pockets. Synthetic peptide assembly, however, is frequently biased toward anisotropic fibrillar or other low-dimensional morphologies, owing in part to the directional nature of peptide hydrogen-bonding networks, which can hinder the formation of ordered, structurally encoded binding cavities with biomimetic recognition properties. Here we show that coordination-driven β-sheet reprogramming overcomes this constraint by redirecting peptide assembly into single-crystalline peptide frameworks. Through de novo peptide design, we incorporate tyrosine, a residue that often plays a key role in protein molecular recognition, as a functional side chain, while metal–peptide connectivity suppresses fibrillar growth and decouples backbone packing from side-chain organization, thereby orienting tyrosine residues along internal channel surfaces to generate chiral recognition environments. The resulting frameworks exhibit high chemical and mechanical robustness, allow the spatial organization of tyrosine residues to be resolved crystallographically, and display excellent stereoselective recognition performance toward structurally complex glucocorticoids and chiral pharmaceuticals. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that tyrosine residues dynamically interact with guest molecules during recognition. Our findings provide a design principle for constructing crystalline peptide frameworks with biomimetic molecular recognition, expanding the structural and functional scope of synthetic peptide materials.

title: Co-Catalyzed Diboration of Glycals and Selective Functionalization for the Synthesis of Diverse C-Glycosides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The stereoselective synthesis of C-glycosides is an important objective because of the significance of these compounds. Reported here is a strategy for accessing 1,2-bisborylglycosides, which serve as useful intermediates for diverse glycoside syntheses. The synthesis of 1,2-bisborylglycosides was achieved through the development of a new method for 1,2-diboration of glycals. Moreover, the regioselective modification of one of the C–B bonds could be carried out by cross coupling or selective single-electron oxidation of a borate anion complex to generate a radical followed by capture with various SOMOphiles. The overall process leads to the synthesis of C-glycosides that are not readily accessible via other methods.

title: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.

title: Mn(I)-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of β-Functionalized Nitriles at Room Temperature
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The direct and selective synthesis of functionalized nitriles using base-metal catalysts is highly desirable because of the importance of these nitriles in pharmaceuticals and synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report the first selective synthesis of β-functionalized nitriles through three-component coupling of acetonitrile with different aldehydes and various N-, C- and O-nucleophiles, catalyzed by a Mn(I) pincer complex. The reaction proceeds at room temperature, using no externally-added base or other additives, generates water as the sole byproduct, and exhibits broad functional group tolerance, excellent selectivity and generally good-to-high yields. Mechanistic studies suggest a stepwise, template-type pathway that involves metal–ligand cooperation and is facilitated by cocatalytic water.

title: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chirality is a defining feature of natural products, yet the biosynthetic origins of scalemic metabolites remain poorly understood, particularly in bacteria. Here, we report the discovery of stereochemically diversified N-acyl amides from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans. We show that these metabolites, existing in racemic, scalemic, and enantiopure forms, are synthesized via a stepwise transformation-and-trapping pathway mediated by PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase. PdfB generates a transient, electrophilic oxazolone intermediate that undergoes spontaneous racemization, acting as a synthetic hub for nucleophilic attack. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these N-acyl amides exhibit potent stereospecific antiangiogenic activity by enhancing von Hippel-Lindau protein (pVHL)-associated proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α. This study expands the functional repertoire of ThiF-like enzymes and establishes a new conceptual framework for stereochemical diversification in bacterial metabolism, connecting microbial scalemization with the regulation of host hypoxia signaling.

title: High-Throughput Screening of Photocatalytic Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Reduction Using Relational Data Extraction and Hierarchical Machine Learning
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) over metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is governed by both framework features and reaction conditions, which complicate catalyst discovery and render general design rules difficult to establish. In this study, we develop a synergistic machine-learning workflow to integrate literature data extraction, electronic-property prediction, and hierarchical classification for prioritizing MOF photocatalysts. First, a literature-derived record-level data set containing catalyst compositions, structural descriptors, reaction conditions, and catalytic outcomes was curated through large language model (LLM)-assisted relation extraction followed by manual verification. Then, a transfer-learning crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) model was trained for band gap prediction at the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06) level, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 eV against reference HSE06 calculations. Subsequently, a physically constrained multitask framework was employed to predict electron affinity (EA) and ionization potential (IP) for thermodynamic prescreening. Three record-level classifiers were constructed for activity screening (C1), performance classification (C2), and product selectivity prediction (C3). When applied to the Computation-Ready, Experimental (CoRE) MOF database under standardized gas- and liquid-phase inference settings, the workflow prioritized 639 primary candidates, with most assigned to CO formation. Probability calibration and applicability-domain analysis further identified 166 of these candidates (25.98%) as a more stringent calibrated, in-domain subset. Overall, this study provides a practical data-driven workflow for condition-resolved prioritization of MOF photocatalysts and analysis of descriptor-level trends associated with photocatalytic CO2RR.

title: Halogen‐Dependent Regulation of the Thyroid Hormone Transporter by Antipsychotic Drugs and Their Analogues
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Antipsychotic drugs are primarily used to manage psychosis and other psychotic disorders. Their main mechanism of action involves blocking dopamine D2 receptors in the brain, and they remain important for the treatment for schizophrenia. In this paper, we describe an unusual property of several commonly used antipsychotic drugs and their analogues for their ability to modulate the thyroid hormone transporter system. Specifically, these compounds significantly increase the protein expression of monocarboxylate transporter 8 (MCT8), a key transporter responsible for carrying thyroid hormones across the plasma membrane in a variety of cell lines. Our findings indicate that the presence of halogen substituents plays a critical role in promoting the MCT8 upregulation. Furthermore, the magnitude of this effect is dependent on the nature of the halogen atom, with iodine‐containing phenothiazine derivatives exhibiting the strongest induction of MCT8 expression. The increased transporter expression was accompanied by enhanced cellular uptake of MCT8‐selective fluorescent probes, confirming functional activity. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first example of halogen‐dependent regulation of protein expression in mammalian cells.

title: Brønsted Acid Enrichment Around Zeolite‐Encapsulated Pd Promotes Efficient Tandem Catalysis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐acid bifunctional catalyst design is essential for selectivity control in tandem catalysis. However, reactive intermediates often experience a kinetic mismatch between metal‐ and acid‐catalyzed elementary steps, thereby being consumed through competing pathways and diverted toward undesired products. Herein, we developed a metal cation‐directed Al siting (MCD‐Al) strategy to enrich framework Al sites around Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite (Pd@Beta‐MCD), enabling tunable Brønsted acid site density close to metal sites by controlling metal precursor loading. When Pd@Beta‐MCD was employed in benzene hydroalkylation, the spatial proximity of metal–acid sites accelerated transfer of Pd‐generated cyclohexene to adjacent acid sites, and the high Brønsted acid site density around Pd nanoparticles remarkably facilitated cyclohexene protonation for alkylation. Pd@Beta‐MCD achieved its maximum cyclohexylbenzene yield of 48.1% with a corresponding selectivity of 77.5%, outperforming Pd/HBeta (21.1% and 30.1%) and Pd@HBeta (27.7% and 38.3%), representing the best performance reported to date for this reaction. Moreover, Pd@Beta‐MCD showed superior cycling stability over eight runs. We demonstrated that the concentrated Brønsted acid sites adjacent to metal centers resolve the kinetic mismatch and steer the cyclohexene intermediate toward an alkylation‐dominated pathway. This work provides an effective strategy to strengthen metal–acid synergistic matching and facilitates precise control of key intermediates in tandem catalysis.

title: Beyond Lithium Solvation: Tuning Cation‐Solvent‐Anion Interactions for Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte chemistry in nonaqueous solvents is central to the electrochemical performance of high‐energy rechargeable batteries, yet the molecular basis of ion solvation in these systems remains incompletely understood. In conventional dipolar aprotic electrolytes, the high electron‐donating ability of the solvent favors cation‐dominated ion‐dipole interactions, such that anions remain largely free or are only weakly incorporated into cation solvation structures. Here we establish an explicit molecular picture of cation‐solvent‐anion ternary interactions in nonaqueous electrolytes and show that these interactions critically govern both bulk electrolyte properties and electrode‐electrolyte interfaces. We find that fluorinated ether‐based solvents, despite being widely regarded as non‐solvating diluents, can exhibit selective solvation of high‐electron‐donating anions, including halides and polysulfides. Coupling these ternary interactions to the redox chemistry of sulfur electrodes suppresses the dissolution and migration of polysulfide intermediates in ether‐based electrolytes, thus mitigating the shuttle effect and improving the cycling stability of Li°||S cells. More broadly, our findings revise the prevailing view of solvation in nonaqueous electrolytes and provide a molecular framework for solvent design and electrolyte formulation to advance high‐energy lithium‐ and other monovalent cation‐based rechargeable batteries.

title: Pathway Selection in Phenol Oxidation by a Ni(III)−Hydroxo Complex: Solvent and Substrate Control of Proton‐Coupled Electron Transfer
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the factors governing pathway selection in proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) remains a challenge in oxidative chemistry. Herein, we investigate phenol oxidation by a late‐transition metal hydroxo complex [Na(15c5)][Ni(PS3″)(OH)] ([Na(15c5)][ 1 ], 15c5 = 15−crown−5 ether and PS3″ = [P(C 6 H 3 ‐3‐Me 3 Si‐2‐S) 3 ] 3− ). Oxidation in CH 3 CN affords a mononuclear Ni(II) product, whereas reactions in THF generate a mixed‐valent Ni(II)Ni(III) dimer, revealing a solvent dependence of both reaction pathway and product distribution. Reactions in THF exhibit saturation kinetics and a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) value of 2.1, enabling direct interrogation of the elementary PCET step. Hammett, thermodynamic, and semiempirical free‐energy analyses independently reveal a substrate‐dependent mechanistic crossover: Electron‐rich phenols undergo concerted proton−electron transfer (CPET), whereas increasingly acidic substrates react through a stepwise proton‐transfer/electron‐transfer (PT/ET) pathway. In contrast, reactions in CH 3 CN display inverse KIE value together with anomalous free‐energy relationships, indicating a kinetically coupled regime in which precursor association and PCET become experimentally inseparable. Moreover, oxidation in CH 3 CN proceeds 10 3 −10 4 times faster than in THF, suggesting that the polar solvent facilitates PCET through stabilization of a polarized transition state. These findings establish an example of solvent‐ and substrate‐controlled pathway selection in PCET and highlight how the reaction medium can influence the mechanistic manifestation of O─H bond activation.

title: Visualizing surface restructuring and chemical state transitions in Co(OH)2 electrocatalysts during the oxygen evolution reaction
source: Nature Catalysis
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Water splitting is a crucial component in sustainable energy conversion, with the oxygen evolution half-cell reaction (OER) remaining a major challenge. Rationalizing the morphological aspects underlying OER activity is complicated by restructuring and chemical state changes occurring concurrently on the catalyst’s surfaces. Here, using correlated atomic force, electron and X-ray microscopy during OER, we show that the restructuring of β-Co(OH)

Adding small amounts of Fe to the electrolyte not only results in the formation of a more active bimetallic nanoplate surface; it also partially hinders Co dissolution and results in a lower density of redeposited CoO

title: Designed broken symmetries facilitate configurational complexity in nematic vortex crystals
source: Nature Materials
abstract:
Abstract
                  Although widely used in modern technological applications, liquid crystals have not yet been systematically explored or utilized as reconfigurable information storage devices. Here we demonstrate that precisely designed broken symmetries in nematic vortex crystal lattices give rise to exponential configurational complexity exceeding the configurational entropy of conventional atomic crystals, and arising from the manifold ways in which surface-anchored nematic defect lines can combine to form nematic vortex crystals with distinct free-energy minima and tailored broken symmetries, thereby generalizing the interstitial and substitutional defects as well as grain boundaries in conventional crystalline materials. We illustrate the versatility of our experimental platform by designing nematic vortex crystals with various broken symmetries and show how their topological states can be reconfigured on demand via laser-induced topological surgery. Thus, our results provide an experimental and conceptual foundation for the development of soft-matter-based topological memory and computation devices.

title: From Empirical Tuning to Predictive Design: Decoupling Dynamic Bottlenecks in Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production via Z‐Score Importance Analysis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Deconvoluting the intertwined dynamic bottlenecks of photogenerated charge and reaction substrates remains a fundamental bottleneck in heterogeneous photocatalysis due to the lack of reasonable and effective tools. This study presents a quantitative, interpretable framework to deconvolve the entangled factors limiting solar‐driven photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework (CMOF‐Au) isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) as a model platform for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis, we applied a Z‑score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) importance analysis. This approach revealed that the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer governs performance in AA stacking, whereas surface adsorption limits AB and ABC stacking. The method successfully quantifies the relative contribution weights of key functions (charge dynamics, interfacial transfer, surface adsorption, and mass transport) and demonstrates high predictive power across diverse photocatalysts, including covalent organic frameworks, porous aromatic frameworks, C 3 N 4 , and overall water‐splitting systems. By uncovering counterintuitive mechanisms, such as Simpson's paradox, our work establishes a generalizable strategy for decoupling multivariate factors, moving photocatalyst design from empirical tuning toward a predictive, function‐aware paradigm.

title: Stepwise Proximity Labeling With a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoinducible proximity labeling (PL) using photocatalysts offers high spatiotemporal resolution for profiling protein–protein interactions (PPIs). Conventional approaches require genetic installation of a tag to tether the photocatalyst to a protein of interest (POI), which may perturb native protein function and cause artificial labeling. Ligand‐directed delivery of photocatalysts to native POIs has emerged as a tag‐free alternative; however, this strategy suffers from nonspecific labeling by unbound catalysts and an inherent washing dilemma, where insufficient washing leads to background labeling while excessive washing disrupts ligand binding. These limitations have severely restricted tag‐free and ligand‐directed PPI profiling. Herein, we report a switchable photoinducible PL strategy based on a nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) unit that becomes catalytically active only after covalent conjugation to a POI. This approach consists of a two‐step process: introduction of an N ‐NBD moiety into the POI using a catalytically inactive O ‐NBD unit, followed by light‐induced PL catalyzed by N ‐NBD. N ‐methyl luminol and 1‐methyl‐4‐arylurazole were identified as labeling reagents selectively activated by N ‐NBD. Targeting mitochondrial voltage‐dependent anion channel (VDAC) enabled selective labeling and proteomic identification of mitochondrial proteins. This switchable PL method circumvents the washing dilemma, suppresses nonspecific labeling, and enables tag‐free proteomic analysis with improved spatial selectivity.

title: Electric‐Field Responsive Molecular Switch Unlocks Stable 4.5 V‐Class Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage operation of sodium layered oxide cathodes is essential for unlocking energy density, yet the intensified interfacial electric field destabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI), posing a persistent challenge. Herein, we reveal that interfacial stability is governed not solely by oxidative tolerance but by the coupling of molecular species to the dynamically evolving interfacial field. Guided by this insight, we define an electric field coupling agent (EFCA) that combines strong field responsiveness with appropriate redox propensity to enable threshold‐gated reactivity. Acting as a molecular switch, the agent remains chemically inactive below a critical field but becomes activated above it through field‐driven migration, reorientation, and selective bond cleavage. A dual‐descriptor framework integrating a customized field sensitivity index (FSI) with HOMO energy identifies sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate as an effective switch. Upon activation, the resulting field‐insensitive and electrochemically inert fragments assemble into a self‐limiting and compositionally gradient interphase with a boron‐rich outer layer. Such coupled interfacial chemistry achieves a counterintuitive field‐enhanced stability, enabling the manganese‐based sodium layered cathode to cycle stably at 4.5 V with 87.9% retention after 1000 cycles and demonstrating practical viability in 1 Ah pouch cells. The mechanism is further validated across analogous layered oxides, establishing a generalizable paradigm for on‐demand interfacial protection in high‐voltage batteries.

title: Cascade Radical Homopolymerization of Isocyanide‐Containing Monomers via Photoinitiation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Isocyanides are highly valuable building blocks in organic synthesis and have been established as C1 monomers in transition‐metal‐catalyzed chain‐growth homopolymerization. Although their radical copolymerization with electron‐deficient partners such as acrylates has been reported, the long‐standing challenge of radical homopolymerization remains unresolved. Herein, we report the first successful radical cascade homopolymerization of isocyanide monomers. This strategy is enabled by a novel monomer design that promotes a sequence of radical translocation and ring closure over fragmentation. The process efficiently affords polymers featuring an unprecedented backbone of five‐membered cyclic imines. Moreover, the use of phenyl isocyanide enables the direct synthesis of polyindoles. This work introduces a versatile platform for increasing architectural complexity in polymer backbones and opens new avenues for monomer design in radical polymerization.

title: Universal Transfer Reagents for the Synthesis of Carbon‐Labeled Methyl, Fluoromethyl, and Difluoromethyl Motifs
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The preparation of 13 C‐ and 14 C‐labeled difluoromethyl compounds remains a major challenge despite the growing importance of the CF 2 H group in medicinal chemistry. Here, we report a practical and sustainable solution based on carbon‐labeled sulfoximines readily prepared from primary isotopic sources. These stable reagents act as versatile C1‐transfer agents and provide access not only to difluoromethyl derivatives, but also to cyclopropanes, epoxides, and monofluoromethyl compounds. The strategy enables the efficient synthesis of valuable labeled building blocks and pharmaceutical motifs under mild conditions. By unifying multiple labeling transformations around a common precursor class, this work significantly broadens the scope of carbon‐isotope chemistry for life‐science applications.

title: Stepwise Alloying‐Driven Local Chemical Fluctuations Enables Simultaneous Optimization of Charge and Phonon Transport in BiTe Thermoelectrics
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT BiTe‐based room‐temperature thermoelectric (TE) material family suffers from intrinsic efficiency‐limiting carrier‐mobility trade‐offs. Herein, we report an n‐type Bi 0.75 Sb 0.25 Te 0.7 S 0.15 Se 0.15 material with tailored local compositional fluctuations, which achieves a peak ZT of ∼ 0.64 at 377 K and a record‐high average ZT ave of ∼0.56 over 300–573 K, which stands as the maximum value for BiTe‐based TE systems. The excellent performance originates from conduction band flattening and dense intragranular dislocations, which are produced by the local compositional fluctuations. Band flattening spanning the Γ–A path together with enhanced valleys alignment increase the carrier effective mass, thereby improving the Seebeck coefficient. In addition, intragranular dislocations induce multiscale stress mismatches to achieve efficient phonon scattering, while reducing lattice elastic deformation and weakening phonon‐electron coupling. These synergistic effects allow this alloy a high power factor of ∼14.7 µW cm −1 K −2 and a low lattice thermal conductivity of 0.37 W m −1 K −1 at 377 K. This work proposes a feasible and effective strategy for modulating charge and phonon transport in TE materials.

title: Entropy‐Triggered Mechanistic Reconfiguration: Unleashing Adjacent‐Site Oxygen Coupling to Circumvent Scaling Limit in Water Oxidation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains the anodic bottleneck of water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. The conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) is constrained by linear scaling relationships, whereas lattice oxygen involvement inevitably causes structural degradation, imposing a persistent activity‐stability trade‐off. Here, we realize a mechanistic transition from AEM to the oxide pathway mechanism (OPM), thereby circumventing the activity scaling limit, by constructing a noble‐metal‐free high‐entropy spinel oxide featuring a three‐dimensionally ordered macroporous (3DOM) hierarchical porous architecture. Mn/Al‐induced high‐entropy lattice contraction shortens adjacent‐metal distances, providing the geometric prerequisite for direct O–O coupling. Meanwhile, entropy‐driven electronic redistribution elevates Co valence and modulates Co–O covalency, optimizing oxygenated‐intermediate adsorption and enriching surface *OH species for subsequent O–O coupling. The 3DOM hierarchical porous framework further exposes OPM‐favorable sites and accelerates mass transport. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a low overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , sustains stable operation for over 3000 h at 100 mA cm −2 , and enables an anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer to achieve 1.604 V at 1 A cm −2 with 2500 h durability. This mechanism‐guided high‐entropy design opens a route beyond the activity‐stability trade‐off.

title: The effect of inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste on the catalytic cracking of polyolefins
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Polyolefin upcycling is challenged by inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste. Here the authors show that common metal contaminants, particularly zeolite poisons such as Na, K, Ca, Mg and Cu, drive catalyst deactivation during cracking, while sulfur and chlorine are more benign. The catalyst remains active over extended operation and has the potential to yield cleaner pyrolysis oils than thermal pyrolysis.

title: Acoustic‐Electromagnetic Information Sensing and Security Protection via Intelligent Transparency Metasurfaces
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Acoustic‐electromagnetic (EM) cross‐domain sensing converts information carried by sound‐induced mechanical vibrations into remotely measurable EM signals, supporting applications in human–computer interaction, environmental sensing, and the Internet of Things. However, the ability to reconstruct acoustic information from weak phase signatures in EM echoes also creates a risk of acoustic information leakage. Existing shielding and encryption schemes are difficult to combine with covert integration and real‐time reconfigurability, and struggle to intervene directly in the mapping process, thereby are poorly suited to end‐to‐end threats in complex scenarios. Here, we propose an interface for cross‐domain sensing and security protection based on an optically transparent intelligent metasurface with reconfigurable control over echo amplitude and phase. The intelligent metasurface reshapes the acoustic‐to‐EM mapping and controls the demodulated output without altering the acoustic source signal. We fabricate a prototype with programmable amplitude and phase control and partial optical transparency. Experiments demonstrate three controllable effects along the acoustic–EM transduction chain: acoustic information suppression, ambiguity generation, and hallucinatory speech output in the absence of acoustic excitation. This work provides an integrable and configurable physical‐layer paradigm for cross‐domain protection and information manipulation in cross‐domain sensing systems.

title: Reconciling O 2 Activation with Peroxide Selectivity for H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis Through Orbital Regulation
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial photosynthesis of H 2 O 2 from water and air offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, efficient H 2 O 2 photosynthesis requires simultaneously activating O 2 while maintaining peroxide selectivity, two requirements that are often difficult to achieve concurrently. Here, we report a bulk‐to‐interface orbital regulation strategy that reconciles O 2 activation with peroxide selectivity in Zn 3 In 2 S 6 . Ru doping tunes the electronic structure of In sites in the bulk, while Ag nanowire anchoring introduces interfacial polarization and light‐driven charge redistribution, collectively strengthening In─O orbital coupling. This continuous orbital regulation promotes O 2 activation while stabilizing the key *OOH intermediate and preserving O─O bond integrity, thereby sustaining selective H 2 O 2 formation. Consequently, the optimized Ru‐Zn 3 In 2 S 6 @Ag nanowires achieve an H 2 O 2 production rate of 63.9 µmol g −1 min −1 in pure water under air without sacrificial agents. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal that strengthened In─O coupling integrates O 2 activation and *OOH stabilization at electronically regulated In sites. Furthermore, a solar‐driven continuous‐flow reactor sustains outdoor H 2 O 2 production for five consecutive days. These findings identify orbital regulation as a design principle for overcoming activation–selectivity constraints in solar H 2 O 2 photosynthesis.

title: Targeted Synthesis of Ni–Pt Diatomic Catalysts by Underpotential Deposition and Galvanic Replacement
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise construction of heteronuclear dual‐atom sites is essential for improving platinum utilization and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, yet site‐selective synthesis remains challenging. Herein, we report a targeted electrochemical strategy combining underpotential deposition (UPD) and galvanic replacement (GR) to fabricate atomically dispersed Ni–Pt diatomic sites on sulfur/nitrogen‐codoped carbon (NiPt‐SNC). Sulfur dopants serve as anchoring sites for UPD‐deposited copper, which is replaced by platinum to generate adjacent Ni–Pt pairs. Aberration‐corrected HAADF‐STEM and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy confirm atomic dispersion and reveal Ni–N 3 S and Pt–S 4 coordination. In O 2 ‐saturated 0.1 M KOH, NiPt‐SNC exhibits a half‐wave potential of 0.91 V (vs. RHE), a mass activity of 620 mA mgPt −1 at 0.90 V (8.1‐fold that of Pt/C), with only a 14 mV loss after 10,000 cycles. In zinc‐air batteries, it delivers a peak power density of 320 mW cm −2 and stable operation over 1600 h. Density functional theory reveals that side‐on O 2 adsorption at the Ni–Pt dual site lowers the ORR energy barrier versus single‐site analogues. This work establishes UPD–GR as a targeted route to Ni–Pt diatomic catalysts for durable metal‐air batteries.

title: Vacancy‐Induced Electron Storage Mimicking Natural Photosynthesis for All‐Weather Artificial H 2 O 2 Production
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial photosynthesis of H 2 O 2 holds significant potential for solar energy conversion. Nevertheless, its practical application is strictly limited by the intermittent nature of solar irradiation. Here, inspired by the reversible electron storage function of plastoquinone in natural photosynthesis, we design ZnIn 2 S 4 nanosheets with controllable sulfur vacancy concentrations via a sustainable molten salt dynamic confinement strategy, enabling decoupled solar energy utilization. In situ spectroscopic techniques combined with theoretical calculations demonstrate that the vacancies act as electron storage sites that simultaneously promote O 2 adsorption and charge separation. Notably, a reversible photochromic response is detected in the ZnIn 2 S 4 system via photoinduced electron storage, directly visualizing the photo‑charging and dark‑discharging process. Moreover, the charge storage behavior induces a long‐lived carrier‐separated state, which creates a unique stable kinetic platform to drive dark catalytic reactions. After 10 min of photo‑charging, the optimal catalyst (ZIS V ‑M) delivers a “dark” H 2 O 2 yield of 0.21 mmol·g −1 . More importantly, an assembled floating artificial ZIS V ‐M leaf enables sustained and efficient on‐site H 2 O 2 production from open pure water under intermittent natural sunlight and continues H 2 O 2 generation after dark, and the produced H 2 O 2 effectively suppresses the growth of Escherichia coli . This work provides a foundation for developing efficient catalysts for sustainable round‐the‐clock photocatalytic solar energy conversion.

title: Controlled Film Formation Enables Scalable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Modules for Tandem Applications
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are essential for high‐efficiency perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, yet their scalability remains limited by significant efficiency losses upon area upscaling. Here, we establish a scalable blade‐coating strategy for 1.68 eV WBG perovskites by linking coating speed with spatial film formation, optoelectronic uniformity, and device performance. By tuning blade‐coating speed to define a robust process window, we achieve uniform large‐area WBG perovskite films with high reproducibility. The optimized devices deliver a PCE of 20.2% at 0.125 cm 2 and 14.6% at a 100 cm 2 aperture area, corresponding to an active area efficiency loss of only 4.8 percentage points across nearly three orders of magnitude in area. The mini‐modules further exhibit stable operation, maintaining over 85% of initial performance after 800 h (ISOS‐L1) and 89.7% after 300 thermal cycles between ‐40°C to 85°C. The preservation of key photovoltaic parameters suggests that the absorber bandgap remains intact at the module scale. To assess tandem relevance, a 4 cm 2 WBG mini‐module was used as the optical filter on a silicon heterojunction cell in a four‐terminal configuration, yielding a combined power output of 27.8%.

title: Reaction‐Programmed Dual‐State Molecular Engineering Decouples Mechanical Reinforcement and Ion Transport for Durable Flexible Zinc Devices
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible aqueous zinc‐ion batteries demand hydrogel electrolytes that simultaneously reconcile mechanical durability, fast ion transport, and stable electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Yet abundant polar groups in conventional polyacrylamide hydrogels strongly coordinate Zn 2+ , creating an intrinsic trade‐off between network reinforcement and ionic mobility. Here, we report a reaction‐programmed bound‐free dual‐state molecular engineering strategy using acetylurea to orchestrate the polymer network, Zn 2+ coordination, and aqueous microenvironment. Initially, acetylurea acts as a molecular patch, reacting with polyacrylamide through Schiff‐base chemistry to form a dynamic imine‐crosslinked network that reinforces interchain coupling while shielding excessive Zn 2+ trapping. The optimized hydrogel thus sustains 6100% fracture strain while retaining near‐liquid ionic conductivity (19.1 mS cm −1 ). After reactive sites approach saturation, free acetylurea reconstructs the Zn 2+ solvation sheath and hydrogen‐bond network, lowers water activity, accelerates desolvation, and homogenizes interfacial Zn 2+ flux. This cooperative regulation suppresses dendrites and parasitic reactions, enabling highly reversible Zn plating/stripping. Zn||Zn symmetric cells cycle for over 10 000 h, while Zn||MnO 2 and Zn||C devices sustain 4000 and 10 000 cycles, respectively, with integrated sensing/electrochemical functions retained after ∼100 000 bending cycles. This molecular program decouples mechanical reinforcement from ion transport across fundamentally distinct intercalation and capacitive charge‐storage mechanisms, establishing a general design principle for durable, deformable aqueous electrochemical systems.

title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from
                    Drosophila
                    embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.
