title: Biological stochasticity increases the evolutionary limit of lifespan
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The mutation accumulation theory attributes aging to the decline in selection strength with age. While classical models assume fixed ages of mutation expression, empirical evidence reveals significant interindividual variation in the timing of mutation expression. Here, we develop mathematical models incorporating this stochasticity. By tracking the fate of lethal mutations, we characterize the boundary of the “selection shadow” where genetic drift overcomes purging selection against such mutations—a fundamental evolutionary limit, termed the lifespan drift barrier, setting a theoretical benchmark for the pace of aging. Our results show that for both stochastic age- and state-dependent mutations, variation in the age of mutation expression generally pushes back this lifespan drift barrier. This outcome is a universal consequence of the inherent convexity of the selection gradient under extrinsic mortality: early expression in a subset of individuals intensifies purging selection, thereby raising the drift barrier. In addition, we demonstrate that while this variance shifts this evolutionary threshold (determining the pace of aging), it leaves the mortality trajectory at mutation–selection balance (the shape of aging) fundamentally unaltered. These findings thus help explain how the pace and shape of aging can become uncoupled.

title: CD49f identifies stem-like memory T cells with enhanced therapeutic potency
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The efficacy of adoptive cell therapies depends on the presence of T cells with durable self-renewal, proliferative capacity, and differentiation potential, yet heterogeneity within starting cell populations remains a major barrier to consistent clinical outcomes. Here, we identify CD49f as a marker of a unique subset of human memory T cells with stem-like characteristics. CD49f
                    Hi
                    memory CD8
                    +
                    and CD4
                    +
                    T cells exhibited transcriptional and phenotypic features associated with T cell stemness, including elevated LEF1, TCF1, CCR7, CD27, and CD28, while CD49f
                    Lo
                    cells exhibited effector-like transcriptional programs. Clinical evaluation of solid-organ transplant recipients treated with virus-specific T cells for cytomegalovirus complications demonstrated that autologous T cell therapies manufactured from CD49f
                    Hi
                    -enriched T cells were associated with superior immune reconstitution and greater in vivo expansion of CMV-specific T cells. Functional assays further revealed that CD49f
                    Hi
                    memory T cells possessed enhanced proliferative capacity and transcriptional plasticity following activation. Consistent with these findings, CD19 CAR T cells engineered from CD49f
                    Hi
                    memory T cells demonstrated improved persistence and conferred superior survival in a preclinical lymphoma model. Together, these findings establish CD49f as a marker of a stem-like memory T cell subset with enhanced therapeutic potential and identify CD49f
                    Hi
                    enrichment as a practical strategy to improve the consistency, durability, and clinical efficacy of both virus-specific and CAR T cell therapies.

title: Localized end-on heating for hot spot ignition in precompressed isochoric plasmas
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
In fast ignition inertial confinement fusion, a “heating cone” is employed to shorten the transport distance of the relativistic electron beam (REB) to the high-density plasma core, thereby mitigating energy losses at the plasma edge. However, its insertion depth and survival time are constrained by the sustained pressure from the large-scale plasma edge during the implosion process. Our whole-process simulations demonstrated that, in the double-cone ignition scheme, the head-on collision of two deuterium-tritium plasma jets not only forms a high-density plateau with a small-scale edge, but also substantially reduces the interaction time between the heating cone and the colliding plasma to approximately
                    
                      
                        
                          0.1
                          
                          ns
                        
                      
                    
                    . This shortened interaction time enables the heating cone to remain intact after the peak compression, even when placed directly at the small-scale edge of the colliding plasma. The small-scale edge is compatible with the range of the soft-spectrum REB generated by the heating lasers. Such a REB efficiently heats a localized end-on hot spot adjacent to the high-density plateau, guided by a kT-level magnetic field amplified from a seed field during the collision process. Ignited by the localized hot spot, the high-density plateau can undergo sufficient burning and achieve a fusion energy gain of 6.8 using
                    
                      
                        
                          60
                          
                          kJ
                        
                      
                    
                    heating lasers.

title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

title: Intracellular Bacterial Imprinting Enables Preservable Whole‐Cell Vaccination
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Whole‐tumor‐cell vaccines preserve broad tumor‐antigen repertoires, but converting living tumor cells into safe and intrinsically immunogenic vaccine substrates remains challenging. Here we generated bacteria‐imprinted tumor (BiT) cells through the controlled internalization of attenuated Salmonella and subsequently prepared them as nonproliferative cellular vaccines by freeze‐drying. Within a defined bacterial‐loading window, intracellular Salmonella induced endoplasmic reticulum stress‐associated immunogenic preprogramming while preserving tumor‐cell integrity, thereby enhancing danger‐signal exposure, antigen‐presentation capacity, and immune visibility. Freeze‐drying preserved the bacteria‐induced immunogenic imprint by retaining key molecular and functional attributes while maintaining overall cellular architecture and markedly reducing residual bacterial viability. Vaccination with freeze‐dried BiT (FD‐BiT) cells elicited coordinated innate and adaptive immune responses, including antigen‐presenting cell activation, T follicular helper‐B‐cell cooperation, and germinal‐center formation. This coordinated T–B cell response was accompanied by durable memory formation and enhanced intratumoral CD8 + T‐cell infiltration, proliferation, and functional maintenance. Accordingly, FD‐BiT reduced primary tumor establishment and pulmonary metastasis and restrained the growth of tumors that emerged despite prophylactic vaccination. These findings establish intracellular bacterial programming and freeze‐drying‐mediated imprint preservation as a cell‐engineering principle for whole‐tumor‐cell vaccination.

title: Manipulating Monomicelle Monolayer Assembly via Salt Effect Toward Tailorable Mesoporous Polydopamine Superstructures for Aqueous Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous superstructures poses a significant challenge. Here, we report a salt effect‐modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for the precise construction of monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures. The concerted salt effect arising from Debye screening and salting‐out stabilizes the composite monomicelles, reduces their hydrophilicity, and promotes their migration and lateral monolayer assembly at the emulsion interface. Increasing the salt content accelerates assembly kinetics, enhances interfacial affinity, and increases micellar rigidity, enabling tunable interfacial coverage and thereby producing a series of monolayer mesoporous superstructures, including monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous nanosheets, monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous vesicles, monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous vesicles, and monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous nanosheets. As a proof of concept, monolayer honeycomb‐like nanosheets with open mesochannels and abundant functional groups were demonstrated as a nano‐ion divider. By homogenizing the ion flux and enhancing ion affinity and transport, this architecture enables dendrite‐free Sn aqueous batteries with an exceptional lifespan of 2794 h. This work opens new avenues for constructing monolayer superstructures with unparalleled architectural modularization.

title: Modulating Compound Orientations by Modular Synthesis of Lyotropic Liquid Crystalline Alignment Media
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The unambiguous determination of relative configuration is an indispensable part of modern compound development in chemistry and medicine. Anisotropic NMR parameters, like residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), are of global nature providing angular structure information and thus complement established structure elucidation methods. RDCs become accessible if the compound in question is oriented with respect to the magnetic field, for example, by using a lyotropic liquid crystal. Modern approaches of RDC‐based structure elucidation do not rely on a priori models of structure and dynamics but require RDC sets of several linearly independent orientations. Herein, the modular synthesis of a series of substituted polyglutamates, all of which form lyotropic liquid crystals in organic solvents, is presented. The new alignment media become accessible from a time‐efficient and straightforward procedure, additionally giving access to functionalities inaccessible via conventional polypeptide synthesis. The orientation of a model compound is investigated as a function of the different side chain motifs. It is demonstrated that these different side chain motifs are clustered into different categories, with linearly independent orientations provided across these clusters. We demonstrate that data are highly complementary, allowing structure elucidation of a model compound using vector orientations from 1 D C‐H ( 1 D C‐C for methyl groups) RDCs as only restraints.

title: Precursor–Cavity Compatibility Directs C−N Bond Evolution Toward Edge Reconstruction for H2O2 Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT ZIF‐derived metal–nitrogen–carbon (M−N−C) catalysts provide a versatile platform for constructing atomically dispersed metal sites, yet their pyrolysis‐driven local coordination evolution remains largely governed by stochastic reconstruction processes. The lack of predictive structural descriptors linking molecular precursors with atomic‐scale active‐site evolution limits the rational design of high‐performance M−N−C catalysts. Here, we identify precursor–cavity compatibility as a key geometric descriptor that steers confined pyrolysis pathways and regulates C−N bond cleavage, leading to the formation of defect‐rich, edge‐reconstructed Co−N 4 environments. The optimized Co(bpy) 3 ‐NC achieves 95.9% H 2 O 2 selectivity at 0.60 V versus RHE and sustains nearly 90% Faradaic efficiency for 120 h at 200 mA cm −2 in an ambient‐air‐fed flow cell. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reconstructed Co−N 4 environments optimize Co−OOH interaction by balancing *OOH stabilization with O−O bond preservation, thereby favoring the selective 2e − ORR pathway. Furthermore, the electrogenerated dilute H 2 O 2 stream enables effective nitrite regulation in recirculating aquaculture systems, demonstrating the potential of integrating molecularly guided catalyst design with decentralized chemical production. This work establishes precursor–cavity compatibility as a rational design principle for steering atomic‐scale coordination evolution in confined pyrolysis.

title: Microstructure Engineering of Organic Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors, an Emerging Toolbox for Performance Enhancement and New Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) have attracted growing attention for biointegrated electronics and human‐robot interfaces because they can transduce ionic signals into electronic outputs, while offering mechanical compliance for seamless integration with soft biological systems. Achieving high‐performance in OMIEC‐based devices requires precise control over structural parameters across multiple length scales, from molecular‐level chemical structure to macroscopic device architecture. Particularly, because OMIECs operate through direct contact with electrolytes and rely on coupled ionic and electronic transport, microstructural engineering provides a powerful strategy to regulate the electrolyte‐OMIEC interface, ion‐transport pathways, and volumetric doping behavior, thereby bridging molecular design and device‐level architecture. In this review, we categorize microstructural engineering strategies for OMIECs across different length scales, ranging from nanoscale phase‐separated domains to microscale porous and three‐dimensional architectures, and discuss the underlying structure‐formation mechanisms and key processing parameters of each approach. Using organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) as a benchmark platform, we summarize how these strategies have been implemented to enhance device performance and enable new functionalities, while also highlighting their limitations and remaining challenges. Finally, we examine applications of microstructured OMIECs beyond OECTs, focusing on electrochromic devices, and discuss future directions for establishing a deeper understanding of microstructure‐property relationships in mixed ionic‐electronic conducting materials.

title: Stage‐Specific Pressure Programming Decouples Low‐Pressure Sulfur Reduction From High‐Pressure Interfacial Reconstruction in All‐Solid‐State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The commercialization of all‐solid‐state Li–S batteries (ASSLSBs) remains constrained by the “impossible trinity” between high energy density, long cycle life, and low stack pressure. Here we show that stack pressure is not merely a static mechanical boundary, but a stage‐specific regulator of sulfur conversion and interfacial reconstruction. Using a static pressure‐resistance‐overpotential (P‐R‐η) operational threshold algorithm, low‐stack‐pressure operation is predicted feasible for 50 wt% S cathodes. Further operando electrochemical measurements and multiscale chemical and structural characterizations reveal that 1 MPa discharge promotes Li 2 S 2 ‐rich interfacial intermediates. However, constant low‐pressure cycling induces progressive pore filling that prolongs charge transport pathways, leading to inactive Li X S accumulation and triphase interfacial contact losses. State‐resolved very‐small‐angle neutron scattering (VSANS) further uncovers a ∼5 nm structural feature that persists after low‐stack‐pressure discharge, which specifically diminishes upon high‐pressure charging. Guided by this mechanism, we implement a pressure‐programmed protocol combining 1 MPa discharge with 180 MPa charge. The resulting cell retains 98.8% of capacity after 100 cycles at 30 °C. This work establishes a dynamic pressure modulation strategy towards alleviating the “impossible trinity” by decoupling the asymmetric pressure‐electrochemical behaviors.

title: Oxygen Anchoring Enabled by Ce‐Based Pyrochlore Coating for Robust Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel‐rich layered oxides (≥ 80% Ni) are pivotal cathode materials for next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries. However, under high cutoff voltage, the over‐oxidation of active cations and oxygen anions triggers structural instability and the continuous migration of O n− (0 n 0.84 Co 0.08 Mn 0.08 O 2 (NCM) during cycling. Combining a Ce‐based pyrochlore coating that possesses a high oxygen storage capacity with bulk Ce doping that modulates the TM─O bonds, the modified NCM cathode exhibits exceptional cycling stability under harsh operating conditions. The assembled CR2032 cells achieved 72.2% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C under a high cutoff voltage of 4.50 V at 60°C. Moreover, pouch‐type full cells exhibit ultra‐stable cycling performance, retaining 91.0% capacity after 1000 cycles at 1 C within 2.75–4.20 V, and 80.2% after 1000 cycles when the upper cutoff voltage is raised to 4.40 V. This work not only provides a feasible two‐pronged modification strategy for layered oxide cathodes but also promotes the development of ultrahigh‐energy‐density rechargeable batteries.

title: Biomimetic Subcellular Chemomechanical Nano‐Regulator for Allergic Rhinitis Treatment
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a highly prevalent and debilitating chronic inflammatory disease; however, its complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely explored, resulting in a significant lack of effective therapeutic strategies in clinical practice. Here, we found that the submucosal extracellular matrix undergoes profound pathological stiffening during AR development and is associated with severe epithelial mechanometabolic dysfunction and physical barrier collapse. Based on this pathomechanical observation, we developed a spatiotemporally programmable subcellular chemomechanical regulator (SCM) to reconstruct the damaged mucosal barrier. Capitalizing on its precise targeting and cascade‐responsive capabilities, SCM provides immediate anti‐inflammatory activity to stabilize stressed epithelial cells. Beyond this acute intervention, the regulator scavenges intracellular free radicals, attenuates pathological mitochondria‐associated membrane (MAM) over‐coupling, and restores mitochondrial metabolic homeostasis. In parallel, the Mn‐containing nanocore and pirfenidone jointly attenuate fibroblast activation and abnormal extracellular‐matrix stiffening. Formulation‐resolved cellular and animal studies distinguished a predominant TA‐associated contribution to early inflammatory and epithelial‐barrier responses from a predominant PFD‐associated contribution to later matrix remodeling. Full SCM combined these stage‐associated response domains while rebuilding epithelial‐barrier integrity and shifting systemic immune readouts toward tolerance. These findings provide a preclinical mechanobiology‐guided framework for treating AR and other mechanically driven inflammatory diseases.

title: In Situ Programming of Armored CAR‐Macrophages by Microneedle‐Mediated Gene Delivery for Melanoma Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite clinical advances in CAR‐T therapy and immune checkpoint blockade, effective immunotherapy for solid tumors remains limited by restricted immune‐cell access and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR‐M) provide an alternative strategy by combining antigen‐directed myeloid programming with local immune remodeling. A self‐locking microneedle platform incorporating mannose‐modified nanoparticles (MNPs) enables localized in situ programming of CAR‐expressing macrophages at melanoma sites. The platform co‐delivers a tumor‐antigen‐directed CAR and a hypoxia‐responsive anti‐PD‐L1 single‐chain variable fragment (scPD‐L1). Initial studies in B16F10‐OVA tumors establish antigen‐dependent CAR activity and coordinated local immune remodeling. Therapeutic efficacy is subsequently evaluated in parental B16F10 tumors using an endogenous tyrosinase‐related protein 1 (TYRP1)‐directed CAR. MNP(TYRP1/scPD‐L1) microneedles delay tumor progression, prolong survival, and promote coordinated myeloid and CD8 + T‐cell responses, while providing lower terminal tumor burden, greater local surface CAR + tumor‐associated macrophage abundance, and reduced systemic exposure compared with dose‐matched intratumoral administration. Reciprocal depletion further shows that CAR‐programmed macrophages contribute to the antigen‐directed myeloid response, whereas CD8 + T cells are major downstream effectors required for maximal and sustained tumor control. These findings establish a localized transcutaneous strategy that coordinates antigen‐directed myeloid programming with adaptive antitumor immunity.

title: Probing Phonon Dynamics for Kinetic Stabilization of Single‐Crystal Nickel‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural degradation and lattice oxygen loss remain major obstacles to the long‐term stability of nickel‐rich layered cathodes, especially under high‐voltage and high‐rate operation. Conventional strategies primarily rely on thermodynamic stabilization via cation doping or surface protection, while the kinetic dimension of oxygen release has received less attention. Herein, we investigate Si─Ti co‐doped single‐crystal LiNi 0.83 Co 0.12 Mn 0.05 O 2 cathode materials, which exhibit reduced Li/Ni mixing, modified surface chemistry, and altered transition metal–oxygen (TM─O) lattice dynamics. Combined Raman spectroscopy and phonon dispersion calculations suggest that Si─Ti co‐doping enhances phonon scattering and modifies TM─O optical phonon modes. Operando and synchrotron‐based characterizations reveal substantially enhanced reversibility of lattice oxygen redox and transition‐metal local coordination. As a result, the optimized cathode exhibits suppressed oxygen release and mitigated irreversible phase transitions, retaining 83.17% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 C. These improvements are likely associated with the synergistic effects of thermodynamic and kinetic stabilization, with phonon dynamics proposed as one possible contributor among these coupled effects. This work highlights that the kinetic factors relevant to oxygen release warrant greater attention in the design of durable Ni‐rich cathodes.

title: Enhancing the Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction of Spinel Co Sites Under an Alternating Magnetic Field by Regulating Their Spin State
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of spin‐engineered catalysts with an external alternating magnetic field (AMF) in a collaborative manner has emerged as an appealing approach to enhancing photocatalytic performance. However, the intrinsic correlation between spin state of catalyst and the magnetic field‐assisted mechanism still needs to be explored. Here, we propose a spin‐state modulation strategy involving the selective substitution of the geometric configuration of Co sites in the NiCo 2 O 4 /C 3 N 4 heterojunction. Separately incorporating Zn and Cr atoms into tetrahedral and octahedral sites induces a charge redistribution that converts low‐spin Co 3+ sites into intermediate‐ and high‐spin states, respectively. Detailed characterizations and theoretical simulations reveal that an AMF can increase the concentration of CO 2 ‐derived intermediates on the surface of the spin‐engineered catalysts. This enhancement is strongly correlated with the spin configuration of Co sites. The modulated arrangement of electrons in cobalt alters the corresponding d‐band center under AMF, consequently optimizing the binding strength of crucial intermediates. Remarkably, the Zn‐doped sample with an intermediate‐spin state exhibits an impressive CO production rate of 318.3 µmol g – 1 h −1 under an AMF, which is 15 times higher than without AMF assistance. This work provides new insight into developing efficient spin‐related catalysts with the help of an external magnetic field.

title: Reactive Phase Conversion‐Enabled 1D/3D Heterostructure Engineering Toward High‐Performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a reactive phase conversion strategy for 1D/3D heterostructure engineering in perovskite photovoltaics. During crystallization, 1‐carboxymethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium chloride (CMMIMCl) reacts with PbI 2 , enabling the in situ formation of one‐dimensional (1D) CMMIMPbI 3 within the 3D perovskite matrix. This precursor‐level process simultaneously consumes residual PbI 2 and constructs an internally coupled 1D/3D heterostructure, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes oriented crystal growth, and redistributes residual stress. The resulting 1D framework further modulates defect energetics and interfacial charge transport, thereby suppressing non‐radiative recombination and ion migration. Notably, at an optimized low CMMIMCl concentration, the initially formed 1D‐related species potentially serve as crystallization templates, modifying the crystallization pathway and facilitating more complete conversion of PbI 2 into high‐quality 3D perovskite. Benefiting from these integrated structural and optoelectronic improvements, inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.09% (certified 26.98%), while scalable perovskite modules reach 22.01%. Furthermore, wide‐bandgap PSCs achieve a PCE of 23.66%, enabling perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact tandem devices with an efficiency of 33.03% (certified 32.98%). This work establishes a versatile route for simultaneous regulation of crystallization, defects, strain, and charge transport in high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: A Benchmark Library for Distributed Power System Analysis and Optimization
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
abstract: DPLib is an open-source benchmark library created to support research and development in distributed power system analysis and optimization. Unlike centralized tools such as MATPOWER and PGLib, no general purpose, reproducible data library package currently exists for distributed power system studies. DPLib, available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DPLib.git}{GitHub}, fills this gap by providing 40 multi-region benchmark test cases ranging from 5 buses to 20758 buses, along with a graph-based partitioning toolkit that converts MATPOWER-compatible systems into distributed regional datasets. The toolkit generates standardized \texttt{.mat}, \texttt{.csv}, and \texttt{.m} files, regional MATPOWER version 2 cases, local and global bus mappings, generator and cost assignments, explicit inter-regional tie-line records, and bus-to-region partition maps. It supports unweighted, electrically weighted, and user-defined partitions, and is compared with METIS, KaFFPa, and an IPA-inspired baseline. DPLib also provides ADMM-based distributed DC and AC OPF solvers for validation. Numerical studies report partitioning sensitivity, centralized run times, distributed OPF iterations, run times, and optimality gaps. These results establish DPLib as a reproducible data layer for distributed power system research.
